title: Outcomes of Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Endovascular Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Cardioembolism: A Secondary Analysis of the POST-UK Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis improves outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion. METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of the POST-UK (Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Near-Complete to Complete Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke) trial, which was conducted from November 15, 2022, to March 29, 2024. Patients were randomly assigned to the intra-arterial urokinase group or the control group. The primary outcome was disability-free survival at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included 90-day all-cause death, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours. RESULTS: P P Among 209 patients with cardioembolism (median age 73 [interquartile range, 63-81] years; 45.9% men), 106 were assigned to the control group and 103 to the intra-arterial urokinase group. Compared with the control group, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly increased the odds of disability-free survival at 90 days (adjusted risk ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.08-2.06];=0.01; inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted risk ratio, 1.47 [95% CI, 1.04-2.09];=0.03). No significant differences were found between groups in 90-day mortality rate, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly improved disability-free survival at 90 days without increasing the risk of death or intracranial hemorrhage. title: Gut microbiota as a potential mediator of the disease-ameliorating effects of molecular hydrogen: mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
abstract: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 Molecular hydrogen (H) has emerged as a promising bioactive gas with well-documented antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties, and its therapeutic potential for a range of human diseases has been increasingly recognized. Accumulating evidence suggests that the gut microbiota (GM) may contribute to some of the biological effects of H. The GM serves as both a key site for endogenous Hproduction and consumption, and a potential site of interaction with exogenous Hsupplementation, with possible implications for intestinal microecological homeostasis. This narrative review critically summarizes current evidence on the bidirectional relationship between Hand the GM, focusing on microbial Hproduction and consumption, the potential role of Hin maintaining gut microbial homeostasis, and the impact of exogenous Hsupplementation on intestinal microecology. The potential therapeutic relevance of H-associated GM modulation is further discussed in metabolic diseases, gastrointestinal disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases. Proposed mechanisms include regulation of microbial composition, reinforcement of intestinal barrier integrity, suppression of inflammation and oxidative stress, modulation of microbial metabolites, and gut-organ axis signaling. Collectively, current evidence supports that Hmay influence the GM ecosystem. However, most supporting data remains preclinical, and whether GM alterations causally mediate the biological or therapeutic effects of Hremains to be established. Elucidating the reciprocal interaction between Hand the GM may provide new mechanistic insight into H-based interventions and facilitate the development of microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategies for human diseases.

title: Puerarin preserves microglial homeostasis and protects against acute cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by regulating autophagy and oxidative stress through Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microglial oxidative stress and dysregulated autophagy contribute to secondary neuronal injury following ischemic stroke. Puerarin (PUE), a bioactive isoflavone with established antioxidative and neuroprotective properties, may protect against cerebral ischemia by modulating microglial dysfunction; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: The neuroprotective effects of PUE were investigated in a rat transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model and in BV2 microglia subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Microglial phenotypic alterations, oxidative stress, and autophagic activity were evaluated using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), ultrastructural, biochemical, and fluorescence-based analyzes. Data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics, pharmacological gain- and loss-of-function approaches, and adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) knockdown were employed to define the role of Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (JAK2/STAT3) signaling. Microglia-mediated neuroprotection was further assessed using an HT22 neuron-microglia co-culture system. RESULTS: PUE reshaped the microglial landscape by preserving the homeostatic microglial phenotype while suppressing ischemia-induced pathological activation. PUE reduced intracellular and mitochondrial ROS production, restored redox homeostasis, suppressed excessive autophagosome formation, and downregulated the autophagy-related proteins 3/5/12 (ATG3/5/12). Mechanistically, these protective effects were mediated through inhibition of JAK2/STAT3 signaling. Genetic silencing of JAK2 recapitulated the effects of PUE, whereas pharmacological activation of JAK2/STAT3 largely abolished its antioxidative, anti-autophagic, and neuroprotective activities. Furthermore, conditioned media from PUE-treated microglia significantly alleviated neuronal injury in HT22 cells, supporting a microglia-mediated paracrine mechanism of neuroprotection. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings identify JAK2/STAT3-dependent regulation of the oxidative stress-autophagy axis as a critical mechanism underlying microglial homeostasis after acute cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) and establish PUE as a promising therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.

METHODS: The neuroprotective effects of PUE were investigated in a rat transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model and in BV2 microglia subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R).

title: Central retinal artery occlusion preceding hemispheric ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy: A case report.
abstract: RATIONALE: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) is a form of ischemic stroke that may signal underlying cerebrovascular or cardiac disease. PATIENT CONCERNS: A 52-year-old man developed sudden, painless vision loss in the right eye. Nine days later, he presented with left-sided weakness and speech difficulty, with a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 8. His medical history included dilated cardiomyopathy, and electrocardiography revealed atrial fibrillation. DIAGNOSES: Ophthalmologic examination and fluorescein angiography supported right CRAO. Computed tomography (CT) angiography at neurological presentation showed right internal carotid artery occlusion from its origin. CT perfusion demonstrated estimated infarct core and penumbral volumes of 37 and 186 mL, respectively. INTERVENTIONS: Emergency mechanical thrombectomy with aspiration and adjunctive balloon angioplasty achieved expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade 2c reperfusion. OUTCOMES: The NIHSS score improved to 2 at discharge, 7 days after admission. At 3 months, the modified Rankin Scale score was 1, although right-eye visual loss persisted. LESSONS: CRAO warrants prompt cerebrovascular and cardiac evaluation, with reassessment when new neurological deficits develop. The nine-day interval between retinal symptoms and thrombectomy does not establish the duration of carotid occlusion or cerebral ischemia. The favorable individual outcome does not establish the efficacy of thrombectomy beyond 24 hours.

title: Zinc activates autophagy by regulating HDAC6 expression following cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury.
abstract: Intracellular zinc accumulation and excessive autophagy have been reported to contribute to neuronal death following cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R). Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6), which contains a zinc-dependent active site, is closely associated with autophagy. However, the relationship between zinc, HDAC6 and autophagy following cerebral I/R remains unclear. In this study, we aim to investigate whether ischemia-induced zinc accumulation activates autophagy through HDAC6. Rats were treated with zinc chelator, autophagy activator/inhibitor or HDAC6 inhibitor during a 90-minute middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume, neurological deficits, protein expression, and the colocalization of HDAC6, Beclin1, and zinc in neurons were evaluated. Our results demonstrate that beclin1 expression was significantly increased after cerebral I/R and this elevation was markedly attenuated by zinc chelation. Notably, reactivation of autophagy with rapamycin significantly, though not completely, diminished TPEN-mediated neuroprotection, suggesting that zinc-induced autophagy is an important contributor to neuronal injury following cerebral I/R. Moreover, immunofluorescence revealed that HDAC6 was colocalized with Beclin1 in the penumbra of ischemic rats, and inhibition of HDAC6 reduced Beclin1 expression and alleviated brain injury. Molecular docking analysis suggested a potential interaction between HDAC6 and α-tubulin, which may influence autophagy by regulating microtubule stability and autophagosome transport. Furthermore, chelating zinc decreased HDAC6 expression, while HDAC6 inhibition did not influence zinc levels, demonstrating that zinc acts upstream of HDAC6. In conclusion, our findings identify a novel zinc-HDAC6-autophagy signaling axis underlying neuronal injury following cerebral I/R, suggesting that targeting zinc homeostasis or HDAC6 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy.
englishSummary: Intracellular zinc accumulation and excessive autophagy have been reported to contribute to neuronal death following cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R). Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6), which contains a zinc-dependent active site, is closely associated with autophagy. However, the relationship between zinc, HDAC6 and autophagy following cerebral I/R remains unclear.

title: Essential oil from Angelica sinensis Radix attenuates ischemic stroke via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK pathway: insights from network pharmacology and molecular mechanism evaluation.
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: As a traditional herbal remedy, the root of Angelica sinensis has long been used to treat headaches, strokes, and dementia. As the primary active ingredient in A. sinensis, A. sinensis essential oil (ASEO) also plays a significant role in the therapy of stroke. Although ASEO has shown clear therapeutic effects, its specific mechanism of preventing ischemic stroke still needs to be further clarified. AIM OF THE STUDY: Through network pharmacological analysis combined with in vitro and in vivo experimental verification, this study investigated the protective effects of ASEO against stroke and elucidated the underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used to analyze the chemical composition of ASEO. Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats were administered different doses of ASEO to evaluate its therapeutic effects. The therapeutic effects were evaluated using behavioral, histopathological, and immunofluorescence assays. In addition, using network pharmacology techniques, the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the treatment of ischemic stroke with ASEO have been preliminarily elucidated. HT22 cells treated with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) were used as an in vitro model. Subsequently, the key signal transduction pathways involved in the therapeutic effects of ASEO against ischemic stroke were further validated using multiple experimental approaches, including enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), flow cytometry, Western blotting, pathway-specific pharmacological inhibition and PKG-specific siRNA knockdown. RESULTS: Twenty-seven compounds were identified from ASEO by GC-MS. In vivo experiments demonstrated that ASEO treatment exerted significant protective effects on MCAO/R rats by improving impaired neurological function, reducing cerebral infarct volume, alleviating neuronal apoptosis, and modulating the expression of apoptotic proteins. Mechanistically, network pharmacology studies suggested that the protective mechanism of ASEO may involve the cGMP/PKG and MAPK signaling pathways. Subsequent experiments confirmed that ASEO inhibited neuronal apoptosis via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK axis both in vivo and in vitro. Importantly, both pharmacological inhibition and siRNA-mediated genetic knockdown of PKG significantly attenuated the protective effects of ASEO against OGD/R injury in HT22 cells. CONCLUSION: ASEO exerts its anti-ischemic stroke effect by attenuating apoptosis via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK signaling pathway, providing a scientific foundation for its clinical application in ischemic stroke therapy.

title: Pharmacological basis of Suhexiang Wan in ischemic stroke: identification and functional characterization of piperlongumine as a brain-distributed bioactive constituent associated with STAT3-mediated blood-brain barrier protection.
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Suhexiang Wan (SHXW) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula that has been traditionally used for stroke-related disorders, including sudden loss of consciousness, neurological dysfunction, and hemiplegia. Although modern pharmacological studies have suggested its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory properties, the brain-distributed constituents potentially associated with its therapeutic effects in ischemic stroke (IS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to elucidate the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by identifying brain-distributed constituents and investigating a candidate constituent potentially associated with its protective effects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI), with particular emphasis on blood-brain barrier (BBB) protection. MATERIALS AND METHODS: SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue under middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) conditions were characterized using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Integrated network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways. Piperlongumine (PIP) was further confirmed and quantified in SHXW and brain tissue using an authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS approach. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, biophysical binding assays, and cellular target-engagement experiments were used to investigate the interaction between PIP and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). The protective effects and associated mechanisms were evaluated in a mouse MCAO/R model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-induced brain microvascular endothelial cell injury model. RESULTS: Among 1991 putatively annotated constituents of SHXW, 55 SHXW-derived constituents were detected in brain tissue under MCAO/R conditions. In the MCAO/R mouse model, SHXW significantly improved neurological deficits, reduced infarct volume and brain edema, decreased BBB permeability, and restored tight junction protein expression. Among the brain-detected constituents, PIP, a natural alkaloid derived from Piper longum L., was selected for further investigation based on its detection in brain tissue, network topology characteristics, predicted association with STAT3, and reported pharmacological relevance to ischemic injury. Authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS confirmed PIP in SHXW and brain tissue, with a PIP content of 48.21 ± 1.10 μg/g in SHXW and a brain concentration of 159.67 ± 8.37 ng/g at 2 h after SHXW administration. Biophysical and cellular target-engagement assays supported the interaction between PIP and STAT3. PIP partially recapitulated the protective effects of SHXW by alleviating neurological deficits, preserving BBB integrity, restoring endothelial barrier function, and suppressing STAT3-associated inflammatory responses. STAT3 knockdown partially phenocopied the endothelial protective effects of PIP, whereas restoration of STAT3 expression in STAT3-knockdown cells reversed the protective phenotype. PIP treatment attenuated the injury-associated changes following STAT3 restoration, supporting the functional involvement of STAT3-associated signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides new insights into the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by integrating chemical profiling, brain distribution analysis, and pharmacological validation. SHXW exerted protective effects against CIRI and preserved BBB integrity. Among the SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue, PIP was identified and functionally characterized as a bioactive candidate associated with BBB protection. The findings support the involvement of PIP-STAT3 interaction and STAT3-associated inflammatory signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. These results provide pharmacological evidence linking the traditional application of SHXW with its modern molecular mechanisms while highlighting brain-distribution-guided approaches for investigating the therapeutic basis of complex TCM formulas.

title: Heterogeneity and risk assessment in minor ischemic stroke.
abstract: Minor ischemic stroke is often defined by a low National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, yet patients with similar scores may have very different vascular lesions, tissue injury, and stroke mechanisms. This narrative review examines four domains that modify prognosis and management: symptom relevance, vascular and hemodynamic status, tissue status, and etiologic subtype. Adverse trajectories differ in timing. Early neurological deterioration (END) or infarct growth usually occurs within hours to days, recurrent ischemia clusters over days to weeks, and incomplete recovery may persist for months. A low NIHSS score may occur despite a disabling posterior-circulation or eloquent deficit, large- or medium-vessel occlusion, poor collateral flow, hypoperfusion, branch atheromatous disease, or an active embolic source. These outcomes are distinct from the mechanisms that drive them; high-risk minor stroke is not limited to large-vessel occlusion. PRISMS did not demonstrate benefit of alteplase over aspirin in selected patients with minor nondisabling stroke, ARAMIS found dual antiplatelet therapy noninferior to alteplase in a similarly selected population, and TEMPO-2 did not support routine tenecteplase in minor stroke selected by intracranial occlusion or focal perfusion abnormality. At ESOC 2026, MILD-MT investigators reported a higher proportion of patients achieving 90-day mRS 0-1 with endovascular therapy (EVT) plus best medical management than with best medical management alone in a selected group with anterior-circulation LVO, NIHSS <6, and favorable perfusion imaging. These findings are not directly comparable with TEMPO-2 because the intervention, imaging selection, reperfusion mechanism, time window, and outcome context differed. Short-course dual antiplatelet therapy remains supported for eligible non-cardioembolic minor stroke, while longer-term prevention should be tailored to the identified etiologic subtype. The modified Rankin Scale may miss residual deficits after minor stroke; measures such as the Canadian Outcome Scale for Minor Stroke (COSMOS) may capture performance, participation, and personally meaningful activities more sensitively. The four-domain framework is intended to organize clinical assessment, not to serve as a validated prediction score or treatment algorithm.

title: Brain cytoprotection in acute ischemic stroke in the reperfusion era: neuroimmune networks, clinical evidence, and translational barriers.
abstract: Intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy have transformed acute ischemic stroke (AIS) care, yet angiographic recanalization does not guarantee adequate tissue reperfusion or long-term functional independence. Brain cytoprotection has therefore expanded from neuron-centered rescue to preservation of the ischemic penumbra, neurovascular unit, blood-brain barrier (BBB), and microcirculation. Using a systems-immunology perspective, this clinically oriented narrative review examines ischemia-reperfusion injury as a dynamic network linking danger-associated molecular pattern sensing, microglia and astrocytes, circulating leukocytes, platelets and complement, endothelium and pericytes, cytokine signaling, edema, no-reflow, and regulated cell-death programs. We integrate classic and recent evidence for excitotoxic, redox and mitochondrial, inflammatory, barrier, microvascular, and cell-death targets; evaluate representative pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic interventions; and distinguish negative primary endpoints from exploratory subgroup or surrogate signals. Confirmatory excitotoxicity trials have remained negative overall. Selected multitarget agents have shown benefit in specific Chinese populations, whereas immune-, edema-, and no-reflow-directed approaches have yielded stage-specific but inconsistent safety, imaging, and functional results. Statins, nitric oxide donors, and phosphodiesterase inhibition have plausible vascular or immunomodulatory actions, but available trials do not establish them as acute cytoprotective therapies. Future development should align the right mechanism, tissue phenotype, treatment time, exposure, target-engagement measure, and patient-centered endpoint, followed by multicenter preclinical testing and independent cross-regional clinical replication. This end-to-end framework reframes brain cytoprotection as precision modulation of a spatially and temporally evolving neuroimmune-vascular system rather than a single undifferentiated treatment class.

title: Shenqi Granules Ameliorate Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Glucocerebrosidase and Uridine Metabolism in Microglia.
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p Shenqi Granules is a traditional Chinese medicine formula derived from the classic prescription Shenqi Formula (SQF), composed of Astragali Radix (Huangqi) and Codonopsis Radix (Dangshen). SQF shows neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.The rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was established using the suture method to evaluate the neuroprotective effect of SQF. Blood-absorbed components were identified via UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, and potential targets and pathways were predicted through network pharmacology. Non-targeted metabolomics of serum and feces was performed using UHPLC-Orbitrap MS, and core metabolic pathways were selected based on regulation magnitude (RM). Gut microbiota structure was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, with associations between microbiota and metabolites assessed via the Mantel test and redundancy analysis (RDA). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to screen core Hub genes for ischemic stroke (IS). Based on single-cell RNA data, a uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional signature score (Uridine_Score) was constructed, and cell type-specific coupling between glucocerebrosidase (GBA) and this transcriptional signature was analyzed. Microglial temporal trajectory analysis was conducted using Monocle3. Molecular docking between core components and GBA was verified by AutoDock, and GBA mRNA expression was confirmed by RT-qPCR.High-dose SQF reduced infarct volume and neuronal damage and improved behavior. A total of 28 absorbed components and 31 shared IS targets were identified. Metabolomics revealed nucleotide metabolism as a core pathway common to both serum and fecal samples. SQF restored gut-blood uridine balance (serum uridine 0.41× Sham → 0.85× post-SQF), reduced fecal dTMP and hypoxanthine. 16S rRNA sequencing demonstrated that the overall correlation between microbial community structure and nucleotide metabolites was statistically significant (Mantel r = 0.307-0.321,< 0.01). WGCNA highlighted GBA, MMP9, and PYGL. Single-cell analysis showed a microglia-specific uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional signature post-stroke, with GBA most correlated with this signature (ρ = 0.377). Pseudotime revealed microglial state transitions (Homeostatic → Acute_Reactive → DAM), with positive GBA-uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional coupling in the Homeostatic and DAM states. Riboflavin showed the strongest GBA binding (-9.83 kcal/mol), and SQF upregulated GBA mRNA in the penumbra (< 0.0001).SQF reprograms nucleotide metabolism via the gut-blood axis and enhances microglial GBA-uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional coupling.

title: Impact of chronic antiplatelet therapy on clinical outcomes of posterior circulation acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Posterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (PCS) is a leading cause of neurologic disability, yet the hospital course of patients receiving chronic antiplatelet therapy (cAPT) remains unclear. This study evaluates the effect of cAPT on PCS outcomes, including patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study used the National Inpatient Sample (2015-2022), including adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations in the United States for PCS with reported NIH Stroke Scale. Outcomes included inpatient mortality, routine discharge, complications, and receipt of reperfusion therapy. Propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjusted for confounding factors, including stroke severity. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: p p p p p p p p p Among 148,740 PCS hospitalizations, 46,125 (31.0%) were receiving cAPT. These patients demonstrated reduced likelihood of undergoing intravascular thrombolysis (aOR: 0.902, 95% CI [0.835-0.975], = 0.009) and EVT (0.868 [0.764-0.987], = 0.031) compared to patients not on cAPT. Following IPTW, cAPT was associated with reduced inpatient mortality (0.581 [0.496-0.680], < 0.001) and increased routine discharge (1.14 [1.08-1.21], < 0.001). These patients also demonstrated reduced hemorrhagic transformation (0.767 [0.695-0.846], < 0.001) and cerebral edema/herniation (0.761 [0.698-0.831], < 0.001). Among hospitalizations undergoing EVT, cAPT was associated with reduced inpatient mortality (0.556 [0.408-0.757], < 0.001), increased routine discharge (1.60 [1.18-2.16], = 0.003), and reduced hemorrhagic transformation (0.778 [0.705-0.858], < 0.001). DISCUSSION: cAPT was associated with favorable inpatient outcomes in PCS, including lower mortality without an increased risk of serious neurological complications. Positive associations persisted among patients undergoing EVT. Prospective research is needed to confirm these results and guide therapeutic strategies.

title: Hydrogen sulfide inhibits neuroinflammation following cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury via regulating glial polarization.
abstract: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 Hydrogen sulfide (HS), an endogenous gasotransmitter, exerts potent anti-neuroinflammatory effects. Both endogenous and exogenous HS attenuate cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury by suppressing neuroinflammatory responses. Microglia play a pivotal role in post-ischemic neuroinflammation. Upon activation, microglia polarize toward either the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype or the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. The progression of neuroinflammation is closely associated with M1 polarization, while HS has been demonstrated to inhibit M1 polarization and promote the protective M2 phenotype. Similarly, astrocytes undergo phenotypic transformation following ischemic stroke, with A1 reactive astrocytes exacerbating neuronal injury and A2 reactive astrocytes exerting neuroprotective effects. Our previous studies have shown that both endogenous and exogenous HS promote astrocytic polarization toward the neuroprotective A2 phenotype. This review provides a comprehensive overview of ischemic stroke and the anti-neuroinflammatory effects of HS and its donors in cerebral I/R injury, with particular emphasis on their roles in regulating microglial and astrocytic polarization toward neuroprotective phenotypes. Additionally, we discuss the intracellular signaling pathways involved in HS-mediated suppression of neuroinflammation. Collectively, this review highlights the therapeutic potential of HS donors as novel agents for the treatment of cerebral I/R injury. We propose that HS donors exert their neuroprotective effects primarily through coordinated regulation of microglial and astrocytic polarization toward anti-inflammatory phenotypes, and that this dual-cell targeting strategy represents a viable therapeutic approach for cerebral I/R injury.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of reocclusion after endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.

abstract: A 35-year-old woman with migraine and oral contraceptive use presented with pontine stroke and right vertebral artery occlusion following cervical manipulation by a lay practitioner. title: EXPRESS: Reperfusion-sensitive induction of endothelial NDRG1 identifies a dynamic vascular stress response to thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
abstract: 3 Ischemic stroke (IS) outcome critically depends on the neurovascular unit's capacity to respond to ischemia-reperfusion stress within the salvageable penumbra. Here, we characterize the spatiotemporal regulation of N-myc downstream-regulated gene 1 (NDRG1) and identify it as an early, reperfusion-sensitive marker of endothelial stress. Under physiological conditions, NDRG1 is primarily expressed in neurons and oligodendrocytes, with minimal endothelial expression. Following middle cerebral artery occlusion, NDRG1 undergoes marked spatial and cellular redistribution, becoming strongly induced in endothelial cells across the cerebrovascular tree.Endothelial NDRG1 induction was detectable as early as 6 hours after ischemia and evolved from a vesicular pattern to diffuse vascular labeling by 24 hours. Importantly, recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator (rtPA) selectively enhanced endothelial NDRG1 expression in peri-lesional vessels in the rtPA-sensitive thrombin model, but not in the rtPA-resistant FeClmodel, indicating that NDRG1 induction is linked to effective reperfusion. In vitro, oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) recapitulated endothelial NDRG1 induction, further enhanced by rtPA through a pathway involving the LDL receptor family.Collectively, these findings identify endothelial NDRG1 as a dynamic molecular readout of reperfusion-sensitive vascular stress. NDRG1 may serve as a biomarker of endothelial responsiveness to thrombolytic therapy, providing new insight into cerebrovascular adaptations associated with successful reperfusion.

title: Therapeutic potential analysis of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury is a core pathological process underlying further neurological deterioration after reperfusion therapy for acute ischemic stroke. Developing more effective neuroprotective agents is therefore a current priority in neuroscience research. Sertoli cells possess unique immunoprivileged and nutritional support functions within the testes and secrete exosomes that serve as important mediators of intercellular communication, with substantial potential for neuroprotection. This review addresses the protective mechanisms of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Through a comprehensive literature review, we systematically summarize their neuroprotective effects, including the modulation of immune and inflammatory responses, inhibition of cellular apoptosis, promotion of neurovascular repair, regulation of autophagy, and influence on epigenetic modifications and related signaling pathways. By synthesizing the latest findings in this field, we aim to provide insights into the development and translation of novel neuroprotective strategies based on Sertoli cell-derived exosomes.

title: Intranasal administration of enalapril confers acute neuroprotection by mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis in a rat model of ischemic stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, with effective treatments hindered by its complex pathophysiology. This study is the first to explore the neuroprotective potential of intranasal enalapril, in mitigating ischemic stroke outcomes through its influence on mitochondrial function. METHODS: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), followed by the intranasal administration of enalapril (0.03 mg/kg) post-ischemia. Neurological function was evaluated after 24 hours of reperfusion through the modified neurological severity score (mNSS), grip strength, and hot plate tests. Brain infarct volume was quantified via Triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining. Blood- brain barrier (BBB) integrity was evaluated via the Evans Blue extravasation assay. Additionally, we employed immunofluorescence techniques to assess apoptosis through TUNEL staining and evaluated mitochondrial function by examining mitochondrial swelling, succinate dehydrogenase activity, mitochondrial membrane potential and reactive oxygen species production. RESULTS: Intranasal administration of enalapril significantly reduced the infarct volume, preserved BBB integrity, and attenuated sensorimotor deficits in MCAO rats. These protective effects were closely associated with enhanced regional cerebral blood flow, a significant reduction in neuronal apoptosis, and improved mitochondrial function. CONCLUSION: Intranasal enalapril may provide a novel approach to neuroprotection in ischemic stroke, potentially through mechanisms that enhance mitochondrial function and reduce neuronal apoptosis.

title: Role and mechanism of ATF6-mediated endoplasmic reticulum stress in ITLN-1 against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract: AIMS: Intelectin-1 (ITLN-1), a novel adipocytokine, exerts neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), yet its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study focused on activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6), a key endoplasmic reticulum stress sensor, to explore its role in CIRI-induced neuronal injury and determine whether ITLN-1 mediates neuroprotection through ATF6 regulation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We established an N2a cell hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) model and a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model. Using protein-protein molecular docking, in situ proximity ligation assay, Western blotting, mitochondrial membrane potential assays, and TUNEL staining, we investigated ATF6 activation in neuronal apoptosis and its upstream regulatory mechanisms. KEY FINDINGS: H/R injury markedly induced ATF6 activation in N2a cells, triggering mitochondrial dysfunction and promoting apoptosis. ATF6 overexpression further aggravated these effects, supporting its critical pathogenic role in CIRI. Mechanistic analyses revealed that ITLN-1 physically associates with ATF6. Both ITLN-1 overexpression and exogenous recombinant ITLN-1 administration significantly suppressed excessive ATF6 activation, modulated the JNK signaling pathway, improved cell viability, reduced intracellular calcium overload and reactive oxygen species accumulation, and attenuated neuronal apoptosis. In vivo, ITLN-1 ameliorated neurological deficits, reduced neuronal damage, and alleviated demyelination, whereas ITLN-1 knockdown produced opposite effects. SIGNIFICANCE: Excessive ATF6 activation underlies CIRI-induced neuronal injury. ITLN-1 exerts neuroprotection by inhibiting ATF6 and modulating JNK signaling, thereby alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction and reducing apoptosis. These findings highlight the ITLN-1/ATF6 axis as a promising therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

title: Sex differences in lipid-lowering therapy after atherothrombotic ischemic stroke: The multicenter MaLIC study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Women have poorer outcomes after ischaemic stroke. The primary objective was to assess sex-based differences in the management and intensity of lipid-lowering therapy following non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA). Secondary objectives were to analyse sex-based differences in vascular risk profile, pre-event functional status, and stroke severity. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Subanalysis of the second phase of the MaLIC study (Management of Stroke in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands), a prospective, multicentre study conducted in 20 hospitals. Adults with non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or TIA were included. Vascular risk factors, stroke severity, lipid profile, and intensity of lipid-lowering therapy at hospital discharge were compared according to sex. RESULTS: A total of 591 patients were included, of whom 223 (37.7%) were women. Women were older (76 vs. 70 years; P<.0001), had greater pre-event functional dependence (mRS>2: 16.1% vs. 7.9%; P=.003), and a lower prevalence of ischaemic heart disease (4.9% vs. 14.4%; P<0001) and peripheral arterial disease (6.3% vs. 13.0%; P=.01). Although women had higher LDL cholesterol levels at admission (103.5 vs. 92mg/dl; P=.004), they were less frequently prescribed high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy at discharge (64.1% vs. 72.3%; P=.04). No differences were observed in stroke code activation or reperfusion therapies. CONCLUSIONS: Women were less frequently prescribed high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy at discharge than men, despite having higher LDL cholesterol levels. These findings highlight an opportunity to optimise lipid-lowering therapy after the cerebrovascular event.

title: Y-Configuration Dual Stent Retriever Thrombectomy for Bifurcation Occlusions in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bifurcation occlusions present unique technical challenges during mechanical thrombectomy. We evaluated the angiographic, clinical, and safety outcomes of Y-configuration dual stent retriever thrombectomy in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by bifurcation occlusions. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 32 consecutive patients treated with Y-configuration dual stent retriever thrombectomy between April 2018 and January 2025. The technique was used as a rescue strategy after failed single-device attempts or as a first-line approach in selected bifurcation occlusions. Angiographic outcomes, procedural metrics, complications, and 90-day clinical outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: The middle cerebral artery was the most common occlusion site (81.3%). Successful reperfusion (TICI ≥2b) was achieved in 97% of patients, with complete reperfusion (TICI 3) in 91% of cases. Following the first Y-configuration thrombectomy attempt, successful reperfusion (TICI ≥2b) was achieved in 87% of cases, irrespective of prior thrombectomy attempts. Median NIHSS improved from 16 at baseline to 7 at 24 hours. At 90 days, 53% of patients achieved functional independence (mRS ≤2). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 6.3%; any intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 9.4%, and no vasospasm, vessel dissection, device-related perforation, or subarachnoid hemorrhage was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Y-configuration dual stent retriever thrombectomy appears feasible as a rescue option for selected complex bifurcation occlusions refractory to conventional thrombectomy. Prospective comparative studies are needed to further establish its safety, efficacy, and optimal indications.

title: Impact of RapidAI® Implementation on Workflow Metrics and Access to Reperfusion Therapies in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A 10-Year Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Artificial intelligence‑assisted perfusion imaging can support selection and coordination in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study assessed institutional changes in access to reperfusion therapies and workflow metrics before and after RapidAI® implementation. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive AIS admissions (July 2014-October 2024) at a single comprehensive stroke center, comparing pre‑implementation and post‑implementation periods (RapidAI® introduced June 2018). Primary outcomes were utilization of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) and mechanical thrombectomy (MT), mRS 0-1 at discharge, and decompressive craniectomy (DC). Secondary outcomes were 90‑day mRS, door‑to‑needle (DTN) time, and hospital length of stay (LOS). Analyses were adjusted for key confounders and sensitivity analyses were made. RESULTS: Among 2,144 patients, adjusted analyses showed no significant differences in IVT (adjusted OR 0.93; 95% CI 0.52-1.69; p = 0.822) or MT (adjusted OR 2.73; 95% CI 0.70-10.61; p = 0.147) between periods. Rescue decompressive craniectomy was lower in the post period (adjusted OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.03-0.82; p = 0.029) and hospital length of stay was reduced (adjusted B -2.33 days; 95% CI -3.62 to -1.03; p < 0.001). No significant adjusted differences were observed for door to needle time (B -0.56 minutes; 95% CI -32.44 to 31.32; p = 0.972), discharge mRS 0-1 (adjusted OR 1.47; 95% CI 0.90-2.39; p = 0.126), discharge mRS ordinal (B -0.29; 95% CI -0.62 to 0.05; p = 0.091), or 90 day mRS ordinal (B -0.26; 95% CI -0.64 to 0.12; p = 0.174). Sensitivity analyses after multiple imputation produced consistent results. CONCLUSIONS: RapidAI® implementation coincided with improved metrics in hospital length of stay and the need for decompressive craniectomy. Given low software utilization and potential secular trends, findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio and Neurological Outcome in Ischemic Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours: A Post Hoc Analysis of TRACE-III Trial.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Whether neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), as a marker of increased inflammatory response, modifies the efficacy and safety of tenecteplase is uncertain in patients 4.5-24 h after stroke onset. We investigated this in the Tenecteplase Reperfusion Therapy in Acute Ischemic Cerebrovascular Events-III (TRACE-III) trial. METHODS: TRACE-III was a phase 3, multicenter, prospective, open-label, randomized, blinded-endpoint trial that enrolled 516 patients from 58 centers in China between January 2022 and November 2023. Patients had anterior large vessel occlusion and evidence of salvageable brain tissue on perfusion imaging, presented 4.5-24 h after symptom onset, and were randomized 1:1 to intravenous tenecteplase (intervention) or standard medical treatment (control). The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were modified Rankin scale score of 0-1 at 90 days and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or death, respectively. This post hoc analysis in 513 patients with complete admission NLR data compared outcomes in patients with elevated NLR (> first quartile) and non-elevated NLR (≤ first quartile). RESULTS: In the elevated NLR group (> 3.0), tenecteplase was associated with increased functional independence (61 [30.2%] vs. 36 [19.6%]; adjusted relative rate [aRR] 1.51; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-2.17; P = 0.03) compared to standard medical treatment. This benefit was not observed in the non-elevated NLR group (26 [41.9%] vs. 25 [38.5%]; aRR 1.12; 95% CI 0.73-1.73). Safety outcomes did not differ in either the elevated or non-elevated NLR groups. CONCLUSION: Baseline NLR may provide a potential signal for differential treatment response to intravenous tenecteplase in patients with acute ischemic stroke, although these exploratory findings require further validation in independent studies. TRIAL REGISTRATION: TRACE-III is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05141305.

title: Tenecteplase, alteplase, and endovascular thrombectomy in extended-window acute ischemic stroke with intracranial large-vessel occlusion: a Bayesian network meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The comparative effects of intravenous thrombolytic agents, endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), and bridging therapy in imaging-selected patients with acute ischemic stroke treated beyond 4.5 hours remain uncertain. We compared these strategies while distinguishing confirmed large-vessel occlusion (LVO) evidence from broader mixed populations. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for randomized trials evaluating reperfusion treatments administered 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset or last known well. The primary network included trials requiring confirmed intracranial LVO or basilar artery occlusion (BAO). An anterior-circulation LVO network and an all-available network were examined as sensitivity and exploratory analyses. Bayesian random-effects consistency models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). The primary outcome was functional independence, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 at 90 days. RESULTS: Fifteen randomized trials were included, of which 8 contributed to the primary confirmed LVO/BAO network. Compared with placebo or best medical care, EVT significantly improved functional independence (OR, 2.93 [95% CrI, 1.40-6.53]) and excellent functional outcome, defined as mRS 0 to 1 (OR, 2.22 [95% CrI, 1.30-4.11]), reduced 90-day mortality (OR, 0.71 [95% CrI, 0.50-0.98]), and increased trial-defined recanalization or reperfusion at approximately 24 hours (OR, 5.27 [95% CrI, 1.83-16.04]); sICH was also increased (OR, 2.65 [95% CrI, 1.28-5.81]). Compared with EVT, tenecteplase plus EVT showed numerically favorable but statistically inconclusive estimates for functional independence (OR, 1.10 [95% CrI, 0.34-3.52]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.16 [95% CrI, 0.52-2.64]). Direct pairwise analyses of 2 trials were similarly inconclusive. Tenecteplase alone did not show clear differences from placebo or best medical care. Findings were directionally consistent in the anterior-circulation sensitivity and all-available exploratory networks. CONCLUSIONS: Among imaging-selected patients with confirmed intracranial LVO or BAO treated 4.5 to 24 hours after onset or last known well, EVT had the most consistent evidence of benefit versus placebo or best medical care. Tenecteplase plus EVT showed favorable but imprecise estimates, and neither network nor direct pairwise analyses established superiority over EVT alone. The incremental benefit of bridging tenecteplase remains uncertain.

We compared these strategies while distinguishing confirmed large-vessel occlusion (LVO) evidence from broader mixed populations. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for randomized trials evaluating reperfusion treatments administered 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset or last known well.

title: Translating Stroke Microenvironment Cues Into Materials Design: Intelligent Nanomaterials for Ischemic Stroke Therapy.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS), caused by cerebral blood vessel occlusion, leads to ischemia, hypoxia, and irreversible brain tissue damage. Current treatments primarily rely on thrombolytic agents like alteplase, urokinase, and streptokinase for rapid reperfusion. However, these therapies are limited by narrow therapeutic windows, rapid clearance, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, off-target effects, and the complex ischemic microenvironment. These have led to increased interest in nanomaterial-based platforms to improve the precision and efficacy of IS treatment. The IS microenvironment, characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation, ionic imbalance, acidosis, and BBB disruption, provides valuable cues for designing responsive nanomaterials. Nanomaterials engineered to respond to reactive oxygen species, pH, enzymes, light, ultrasound, or magnetic fields can enable targeted drug delivery, controlled release, and multi-modal interventions, enhancing therapeutic precision. This review discusses the IS microenvironment, limitations of traditional therapies, recent advances in intelligent nanomaterials for IS treatment, and the major barriers that currently limit clinical translation.

title: Cerebral Oedema After Ischaemic Stroke: Pathogenesis, Natural History, and Potential Medical Treatments From Bench to Bedside.
abstract: The development of cerebral oedema after ischaemic stroke is a common and potentially devastating complication associated with increased mortality and disability. Despite this, there currently exists no definitive medical treatment for cerebral oedema, and the efficacy of commonly used agents is unclear. In recent decades there has been a significant amount of research attempting to describe the pathogenesis of cerebral oedema in ischaemic stroke which has begun to lead to the development of new potential treatments. In this review we will aim to, firstly, provide a comprehensive overview of the pathogenesis and natural history of cerebral oedema in ischaemic stroke, including cellular mechanisms, breakdown of the blood-brain barrier, the role of the immune system, and potential effects of reperfusion. We will then summarise the evidence base for currently used treatments for cerebral oedema in ischaemic stroke such as hyperosmolar agents, as well as emerging treatments which are still under investigation. Where available, this review will highlight outcomes of clinical trials for these proposed treatments.

title: Integrated multi-omics reveals gut microbiota-metabolic mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effects of Xijiao Dihuang Decoction against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remains a major barrier to functional recovery after reperfusion therapy for ischemic stroke. Increasing evidence indicates that gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolic disturbance are closely involved in post-stroke neuroinflammation and secondary brain injury. Xijiao Dihuang Decoction (XDD), a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula, has shown protective effects in cerebrovascular disorders; however, whether its effects against CIRI are associated with coordinated regulation of the gut microbiota and host metabolism remains unclear. METHODS: Circulating XDD-derived components were characterized by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to predict potential targets and signaling pathways associated with CIRI. A middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rat model was established, and rats were treated with low-, medium-, or high-dose XDD for 7 days, with edaravone as a positive control. Neurological deficits, cerebral infarct volume, hemorheological parameters, histopathological changes, and serum inflammatory cytokines were assessed. Cecal microbiota composition was analyzed by 16S rDNA sequencing, and cecal metabolic profiles were investigated using untargeted LC-MS metabolomics. Multi-omics integration and Spearman correlation analysis were performed to explore associations between differentially abundant bacterial genera and characteristic metabolites. RESULTS: A total of 54 XDD-derived circulating components were identified. Network pharmacology analysis indicated that the putative targets of XDD were mainly enriched in pathways related to inflammation, lipid and energy metabolism, and regulated cell death, with AKT1 and NLRP3 were predicted as potential hub targets. In MCAO/R rats, XDD improved neurological deficits, reduced cerebral infarct volume, alleviated hemorheological abnormalities, and attenuated neuronal injury. XDD also reduced serum IL-6 levels and lowered IL-1β levels mainly at medium and high doses. In addition, XDD partially restored gut microbial diversity and remodeled CIRI-associated microbial dysbiosis. Metabolomics analysis revealed marked metabolic disturbances after MCAO/R, and XDD reversed part of these alterations, particularly those related to lipid metabolism. Integrated analysis further linked specific bacterial genera with lipid mediators and fatty acid-related metabolites, indicating coordinated remodeling of the gut microbiota and host metabolism. CONCLUSION: XDD exerts neuroprotective effects against CIRI through multi-target and multi-pathway actions. Its therapeutic effects may be associated with coordinated regulation of gut microbial homeostasis, metabolic reprogramming, and inflammatory/cell death signaling. These findings provide new evidence supporting the potential application of XDD in ischemic stroke and offer insight into microbiota-related mechanisms underlying its neuroprotective effects.

title: Clinical Characteristics and In-Hospital Course of Symptomatic Intracranial Hemorrhage After Intravenous Alteplase in Older Adults with Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives Methods Results Conclusions : This study describes symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) after intravenous alteplase in older adults with acute ischemic stroke.: This retrospective single-center cohort included 95 unique patients aged ≥65 years treated in Galati, Romania, in 2020-2024. The binary hemorrhage variable was verified against clinical and computed tomography (CT) records. Study-defined sICH required new or increased CT hemorrhage with attributed deterioration, comprising a ≥4-point National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) increase or other clinically relevant worsening. Comparisons and Firth models were exploratory, with admission NIHSS adjustment.: All 14 recorded hemorrhages met this definition (14.7%; 95% CI 9.0-23.2%): 10 met the NIHSS threshold and four had relevant worsening below it. Ten were detected before 24 h and four at the 24-48 h range; morphology included hemorrhagic infarction and parenchymal hematoma. All adjusted intervals included the null. Median hospitalization was five days longer with sICH. The mortality difference was 2.6 percentage points (conservative exact 95% CI range from -31.6 to 45.9).: Adjusted association estimates are inconclusive and do not justify altering guideline-based eligibility. Prospective multicenter studies require standardized definitions, stroke-severity measures, reperfusion data, and functional outcomes.

title: FLAIR vascular hyperintensities in acute ischemic stroke: from collateral-related imaging findings to a candidate dynamic hemodynamic imaging phenotype.
abstract: With advances in reperfusion therapies for acute large vessel occlusion (LVO), stroke imaging evaluation has progressively shifted from time-based treatment selection toward comprehensive assessment of tissue status and hemodynamic adaptation. However, current imaging approaches primarily characterize vascular patency, perfusion status, and tissue injury, while remaining limited in their ability to directly capture the dynamic regulatory processes of cerebral circulation after arterial occlusion. In patients with LVO, ischemic tissue outcome is determined not only by the occlusion site and time to reperfusion but also by collateral circulation capacity, cerebral hemodynamic status, and tissue tolerance to ischemia. Therefore, imaging biomarkers capable of reflecting cerebral circulatory adaptation under ischemic conditions are of substantial research interest. FLAIR vascular hyperintensities (FVHs) are MRI findings characterized by linear or serpentine hyperintense signals along the cortical surface, within cortical sulci, or along the Sylvian fissure on fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences. They are generally associated with reduced distal blood flow velocity, prolonged blood transit time, and hemodynamic alterations mediated by leptomeningeal collateral pathways. In recent years, numerous studies have investigated the role of FVHs in the diagnosis of acute ischemic stroke, evaluation of reperfusion therapy, and prediction of clinical outcomes. However, the clinical significance of FVHs remains incompletely understood. Some studies have suggested that FVHs are associated with favorable collateral status and smaller infarct volumes, whereas others have demonstrated that FVHs may also occur in patients with more pronounced hemodynamic impairment. These discrepancies suggest that FVHs may not simply represent favorable collateral circulation or ischemic severity, but may instead reflect the dynamic hemodynamic response of the cerebral circulation to reduced perfusion following arterial occlusion. From the perspective of precision stroke imaging, this review systematically summarizes the mechanisms underlying FVH formation, their biological significance, and clinical implications. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationships between FVHs and collateral circulation, FVHs-DWI mismatch, ischemic tissue status, and potential benefit from reperfusion therapy. Furthermore, current challenges related to FVH standardization and clinical translation are discussed, with particular emphasis on their potential role as a candidate dynamic hemodynamic imaging phenotype reflecting physiological hemodynamic adaptation.

title: Tongxinluo is associated with neurovascular changes following rt-PA-treated ischemic stroke: associations with inflammation, vascular remodeling, and neural plasticity.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) is the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke but is often limited by microvascular obstruction and reperfusion injury. Tongxinluo (TXL) has demonstrated neuroprotective potential, yet its association with neurovascular responses during rt-PA-associated reperfusion remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: Because reperfusion was achieved by filament withdrawal before rt-PA administration, this model evaluates TXL-associated effects during mechanically induced reperfusion with rt-PA exposure rather than enhancement of rt-PA-mediated thrombolysis. Animals were randomized into Sham, MCAO, MCAO + rt-PA, and MCAO + rt-PA + TXL (low/high dose) groups. Neurological outcomes were assessed longitudinally. Cerebral perfusion was monitored using laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI). Mechanistic analyses included assessments of blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, oxidative stress, microglial activation, angiogenesis, mitochondrial function, apoptosis, and synaptic plasticity markers (BDNF, GAP-43, and Synapsin I) using histological, biochemical, and molecular techniques. RESULTS: Adjunctive TXL treatment was associated with improved neurological outcomes and reduced infarct volume compared with rt-PA alone, with dose-dependent trends observed. TXL was associated with improved cortical microvascular perfusion and reduced severity of the no-reflow phenomenon. Mechanistically, TXL suppressed microglia-mediated neuroinflammation (downregulating TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) and preserved BBB integrity. This anti-inflammatory environment facilitated angiogenic maturation, evidenced by increased microvessel density and lumen formation. Furthermore, TXL stabilized mitochondrial function, inhibited neuronal apoptosis, and upregulated BDNF, GAP-43, and Synapsin I, leading to significant restoration of dendritic spine density. CONCLUSION: TXL may provide adjunctive neuroprotective effects in the context of rt-PA treatment by modulating inflammatory, vascular-associated, and neuronal recovery responses. These findings support further investigation of TXL as a complementary therapy following reperfusion. By concurrently suppressing neuroinflammation and promoting vascular and synaptic reconstruction, TXL translates multi-target modulation into robust functional recovery, supporting its potential as a strategic combination therapy for acute ischemic stroke.

title: Exogenous hydrogen sulfide alleviates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury via inhibiting RIPK1-mediated neuronal necroptosis and ROS overaccumulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: 2 Cerebral I/R injury is a significant pathological factor contributing to neuronal death and neurological dysfunction following stroke. Necroptosis and excessive oxidative stress are pivotal mechanisms that drive ischemic neuronal damage. HS has been identified as a neuroprotective gaseous signaling molecule; however, its regulatory role in neuronal necroptosis during cerebral I/R injury remains inadequately understood. METHODS: In vitro In vivo , we established a cell OGD model to simulate neuronal I/R injury. Following pretreatment with NaHS or Necrostatin-1, we assessed cell viability, the necroptotic rate, intracellular ROS levels, mitochondrial membrane potential, and the expression of necroptosis-related proteins., we established a mouse model of MCAO/R. After NaHS and Nec-1 intervention, we evaluated neurological deficit scores, cerebral blood perfusion, brain water content, cerebral infarct volume, neuronal ultrastructure, and the expression of RIPKs proteins. RESULTS: In vivo OGD treatment resulted in a time-dependent decline in SH-SY5Y cell viability, a significant increase in the rate of neuronal necroptosis, excessive accumulation of ROS, mitochondrial dysfunction, and elevated expression levels of RIPKs and MLKL. Pretreatment with moderate doses of NaHS significantly enhanced cell viability, mitigated ROS overproduction, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and inhibited OGD-induced neuronal necroptosis. Both NaHS and Nec-1 effectively suppressed the activation of the RIPK1 mediated signaling pathway., MCAO/R induced severe neurological dysfunction, cerebral hypoperfusion, brain edema, extensive cerebral infarction, and neuronal ultrastructural damage. NaHS or Nec-1 treatment significantly improved neurological deficits, restored regional cerebral blood flow, reduced brain edema and infarct volume, and alleviated neuronal morphological damage by downregulating the expression of RIPK1 and RIPK3. CONCLUSION: in vitro in vivo 2 Necroptosis played a crucial role in acute cerebral I/R injury, bothand, mediated by RIPK1. Exogenous HS or Nec-1 exhibited significant neuroprotective effects against cerebral I/R injury by suppressing RIPK1-mediated neuronal necroptosis and inhibiting ROS. These findings provided a novel theoretical basis for the clinical management of ischemic stroke.

title: Prognostic Evaluation of Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients After Mechanical Thrombectomy Incorporating Imaging, Inflammatory, and Rehabilitation Aspects.
abstract: AIM: We aimed to perform a prognostic evaluation for patients with acute ischemic stroke after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) incorporating imaging, inflammatory, and rehabilitation aspects. METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) was conducted, systematically evaluating baseline demographics, neuroimaging features, hematological inflammatory indices, and time to start rehabilitation. Prognostic correlations were examined using multivariate logistic regression, with poor functional outcome defined as 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) >2. Model discrimination was assessed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis of the composite prediction framework. RESULTS: The analytical cohort comprised 144 subjects. Five independent predictors of unfavorable outcomes emerged: pre-existing hypertension (adjusted Odds Ratio [aOR] 6.48, 95% Confidence Interval [CI] 1.03-40.80), lower baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) (aOR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06-0.49), elevated NLR (aOR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.46), extended onset-to-reperfusion time (OTR) (per minute aOR 1.01, 95% CI 1.01-1.02), and delayed starting rehabilitation (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.52-3.46). The multivariable model demonstrated excellent discriminative capacity (area under the curve [AUC] 0.964, 95% CI 0.940-0.988). CONCLUSIONS: Beyond successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 2b-3), functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy were independently influenced by factors across the three core domains of our prognostic framework: imaging (baseline ASPECTS), inflammation (elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, NLR), and rehabilitation (delayed starting rehabilitation). Additional significant clinical variables included pre-existing hypertension and longer onset-to-reperfusion time (OTR). These findings support the potential value of a multidimensional prognostic assessment integrating imaging, inflammatory, and rehabilitation aspects in patients with acute ischemic stroke after mechanical thrombectomy.

title: High-frequency rTMS attenuates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and modulates mTOR-related signaling and brain-gut-immune phenotypes in MCAO/R rats.
abstract: BACKGROUND: High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) may promote neurological recovery after ischemic stroke, but its protective effects after MCAO/R and associations with neurotrophic factors, mTOR-related autophagy markers, systemic inflammation, and gut microbiota phenotypes remain unclear. METHODS: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury was induced by right MCAO/R. Rats were assigned to Sham, MCAO/R, and MCAO/R + high-frequency rTMS groups. rTMS was initiated on postoperative day 3. Neurological and motor functions were assessed behaviorally. Western blotting, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and 16S rRNA sequencing were used to examine related proteins, inflammatory cytokines, and gut microbiota, followed by multivariate and correlation analyses. RESULTS: High-frequency rTMS improved neurological and motor functions, reduced infarction and histopathological injury, decreased TUNEL positivity, and increased the number of Nissl-positive neurons. It upregulated FGF-2, BDNF, and the p-mTOR (Ser2448)/mTOR ratio, attenuated abnormal changes in Beclin-1, LC3-II/LC3-I, and p62, and reduced serum TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels. 16S rRNA sequencing showed altered gut microbiota β-diversity and genus-level composition, with several genera associated with motor or inflammatory indices. CONCLUSION: High-frequency rTMS alleviated cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and promoted neurological recovery after MCAO/R, accompanied by enhanced neurotrophic support, improvement in mTOR-related autophagy marker abnormalities, and lower serum pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Gut microbiota alterations were also observed following rTMS treatment, although their functional significance remains exploratory.

title: Mobile Stroke Units in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Thrombectomy Efficiency, Workflow Models, and Implementation Considerations: A Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a time-critical emergency in which the benefit of reperfusion depends not only on treatment speed but also on accurate large-vessel occlusion (LVO) recognition, destination selection, and coordination between prehospital and hospital teams. Mobile stroke units (MSUs) move imaging, laboratory testing, specialist assessment, and thrombolysis into the prehospital setting, but their effect on thrombectomy depends substantially on onboard vascular-imaging capability and local routing protocols. SUMMARY: This narrative review evaluates MSUs through the broader construct of thrombectomy efficiency, encompassing LVO identification, destination accuracy, avoidance of secondary transfer and duplicate imaging, in-hospital parallel processing, puncture and reperfusion times, and downstream clinical outcomes. Evidence for earlier intravenous thrombolysis is retained as an important upstream benefit but is distinguished from thrombectomy-specific efficiency. The available literature indicates that non-contrast-CT-based MSUs can accelerate hospital workflows through early diagnosis and prenotification, whereas CTA-enabled models can additionally confirm LVO in the field and support direct routing to a thrombectomy-capable center or, in selected systems, direct-to-angiography pathways. The magnitude of benefit is therefore configuration- and system-dependent. Economic evaluations likewise show that value is highly sensitive to annual patient volume, catchment population, staffing model, operating hours, analytic time horizon, and baseline patient disability. KEY MESSAGES: MSUs should not be treated as a uniform intervention. Their thrombectomy value is determined by how effectively prehospital imaging and specialist assessment are linked to destination decisions, interfacility-transfer avoidance, and receiving-center activation. CTA-enabled pathways provide the clearest mechanism for thrombectomy-specific time savings, while non-contrast-CT-based models may still improve in-hospital efficiency. Implementation is most defensible when local geography, case volume, workforce, dispatch integration, downstream thrombectomy capacity, and cost-effectiveness are considered together.

title: NAD+ Attenuates Neuroinflammation in Ischemic Stroke by Suppressing the cGAS- STING Pathway via Mitochondrial Homeostasis Restoration.
abstract: + + + + + + + + Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide, with neuroinflammation playing a critical role in its pathogenesis. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is a major driver of innate immune responses activated by endogenous DNA, including mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), and contributes significantly to post-ischemic neuroinflammation. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD), a vital metabolic coenzyme, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory potential in various diseases, including stroke; however, its specific role in regulation of neuroinflammation following stroke remains unclear. In this study, we examined the protective effects of NADagainst ischemic stroke and explored its role in modulating cGAS-STING-mediated neuroinflammatory responses. Utilizing a transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion mouse model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation BV2 microglia model, we observed that NADtreatment significantly reduced infarct volume and brain edema, and improved neurological outcomes. NADreduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and facilitated the polarization of microglia from pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. This effect was associated with the inhibition of cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway activation. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockdown of STING largely abrogated the anti-inflammatory effects of NADin BV2 microglia, indicating a STING-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, NADrestored mitochondrial respiratory function and reduced cytoplasmic mtDNA leakage, suggesting that the improvement of mitochondrial homeostasis may underlie the suppression of cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway by NAD. Our findings indicate that NADalleviates neuroinflammation following brain ischemia/reperfusion injury by regulating mitochondrial homeostasis and attenuates the cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway activation in microglia, thereby providing new therapeutic insights for ischemic stroke.

title: Self-adaptive copper-enriched Prussian blue nanozymes for cascade ROS scavenging and neurofunctional recovery in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract: 2+ -1 In vitro 2 Ischemic stroke (IS) and the subsequent reperfusion induce severe oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction through the excessive generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, most existing therapeutic strategies target only a single pathological pathway, thereby limiting their therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we developed a multifunctional mesoporous copper-enriched Prussian blue nanozyme (Meso-Cu-PBMc) by synergistically integrating Cuactive sites within a Prussian blue framework, exhibiting robust multi-enzymatic mimetic activities, including superoxide dismutase (SOD)-, catalase (CAT)-, and peroxidase (POD)-, facilitating efficient ROS scavenging and the restoration of intracellular redox homeostasis.studies demonstrated that Meso-Cu-PBMc effectively protects neuronal cells against CoCl-induced oxidative injury and significantly reduces intracellular ROS accumulation. In a middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAo/R) rat model, intranasal administration of Meso-Cu-PBMc (20 mg kg) at the onset of reperfusion markedly reduced infarct volume from 54.32% to 13.03%, significantly improved neurological function, and enhanced locomotor recovery in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistically, the nanozyme exerted dual therapeutic effects through both direct ROS scavenging and activation of the Nrf2/xCT/GPX4 antioxidant signaling pathway, thereby maintaining glutathione homeostasis and cellular redox balance. Furthermore, treatment restored the expression of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95), increased the levels of SIRT1 and PGC-1α, and reduced the expression of GFAP and iNOS, indicating the preservation of neuronal plasticity and mitochondrial homeostasis, together with the attenuation of reactive gliosis. Collectively, these findings highlight Meso-Cu-PBMc as a promising therapeutic platform for the treatment of ischemia-reperfusion injury and other oxidative stress-associated neurological disorders.

title: Current and emerging neuromodulation techniques for motor recovery after ischemic stroke: a 2026 update.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neuromodulation technologies have emerged as promising tools to enhance motor recovery following ischemic stroke. Acute reperfusion therapy remains highly time-dependent, underscoring the need for interventions that augment post-stroke neuroplasticity. Brain stimulation techniques aim to modulate cortical excitability and promote adaptive reorganization of motor networks during the critical recovery period after stroke. AREAS COVERED: The authors review recent advances in neuromodulation strategies for post-stroke motor recovery, as well as the key principles underlying neuromodulation. Major noninvasive modalities, including transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), and low-intensity focused ultrasound stimulation (LIFUS), are reviewed alongside emerging applications of invasive techniques such as deep brain stimulation (DBS) and vagus nerve stimulation (VNS). Recent randomized clinical trials and translational studies are also highlighted. This article is based on literature obtained through PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov searches for content published between 1 January 2020 and 30 March 202630 March 2026 and was supplemented by earlier landmark studies relevant to stroke recovery and neuromodulation. EXPERT OPINION: Although neuromodulation technologies demonstrate encouraging safety profiles, clinical trial results feature notable neutral results. Future studies bear the burden of refining stimulation paradigms, patient selection, and rehabilitation dosing, possibly leveraging personalized, biomarker-driven patient selection.
