title: Added Prognostic Value of MRI to CT in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients Undergoing Mechanical Thrombectomy in the Extended Time Window.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In the 6-24-hour window, imaging must identify patients with salvageable tissue while avoiding delays and reperfusion of large established infarcts. The optimal imaging strategy remains controversial. Although computed tomography (CT) is widely used because of its accessibility and speed, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides more sensitive tissue characterization. This study evaluated whether adding MRI to CT was associated with clinical outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of consecutive patients with AIS due to large vessel occlusion who underwent MT between January 2022 and December 2024. Patients were grouped according to pre-procedural imaging: CT alone or MRI plus CT. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to reduce measured baseline imbalances. The primary outcomes were excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1) and 3-month mortality; symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (SICH) was the secondary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations. RESULTS: P P P P After propensity score matching, 364 patients (182 pairs) were included in the final analysis. Compared with CT alone, the MRI plus CT group demonstrated significantly lower 3-month mortality (7.1% vs 18.7%,< 0.01) and reduced incidence of SICH (2.2% vs 7.7%,= 0.02). No significant difference was observed in excellent functional outcome at 3 months between groups. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that MRI plus CT was independently associated with lower risks of mortality (adjusted OR=0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.72;< 0.01) and SICH (adjusted OR=0.23, 95% CI 0.05-0.96;=0.04). CONCLUSION: Among patients with AIS undergoing MT within the 6-24-hour window, MRI plus CT was associated with lower 3-month mortality and SICH than CT alone, without a significant difference in excellent functional outcome. Because imaging allocation was non-randomized and quantitative infarct-core and perfusion data were unavailable, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require prospective multicenter validation.

The optimal imaging strategy remains controversial. Although computed tomography (CT) is widely used because of its accessibility and speed, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides more sensitive tissue characterization.

title: RAPID perfusion CT in acute ischemic stroke: an educational pictorial review of common patterns, pearls, and pitfalls.
abstract: Rapid processing of Perfusion and Diffusion (RAPID) software for CT perfusion (CTP) is a valuable tool for the evaluation of acute ischemic stroke and therapeutic decision-making in extended therapeutic windows. However, automated maps should not be interpreted in isolation. A structured, pattern-based approach, integrating qualitative visual assessment with automated quantitative output and clinical information to refine therapeutic selection, remains essential to mitigate pitfalls and optimize patient care. The aim of this article is to provide an educational pictorial review based on selected illustrative cases of the most common imaging patterns, interpretive pitfalls, and technical features of CTP processed with RAPID software in acute ischemic stroke, that may serve as a practical guide for radiologists and neuroradiologists. KEY POINTS: Question How can radiologists effectively interpret automated RAPID CT perfusion maps in acute ischemic stroke while avoiding common technical traps, diagnostic pitfalls, and anatomical limitations? Findings Integrating qualitative visual assessment, quantitative RAPID outputs, and clinical-vascular data within a structured workflow minimizes diagnostic errors and optimizes patient selection for reperfusion. Critical relevance statement This educational pictorial review provides a practical, pattern-based approach to RAPID CT perfusion interpretation, highlighting clinical applications, technical limitations, software variability, and diagnostic pitfalls to advance everyday neuroradiological practice and personalized stroke management.

title: Prognostic performance of blood neurofilament light chain for functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: This meta-analysis aimed to assess the association between blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) and functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke. METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure database were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled to quantify the association between blood NfL and functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke. We pooled the area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity; conducted meta-regression and sensitivity analyses; and assessed publication bias. RESULTS: p I p p p 2 A total of 18 studies involving 3,448 patients were included in this meta-analysis. The pooled results demonstrated that blood NfL was associated with poor functional outcomes after ischemic stroke (OR = 1.78, 95% CI: 1.41-2.24, < 0.001, = 87.5%, < 0.01). The pooled AUC for blood NfL in predicting functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.82), with 71% (95% CI: 62-79%) sensitivity and 74% (95% CI: 67-80%) specificity. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression revealed that participant age, sample size, study design, blood sample type, assay method, proportion of poor functional outcomes, blood sampling time, reperfusion therapy rate, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, definition of poor functional outcome, and the proportion of large artery atherosclerosis were not identified as significant sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis indicated that the pooled estimate was robust. Begg's test also showed no evidence of publication bias ( = 0.753), although Egger's test suggested the presence of publication bias ( < 0.001). The trim-and-fill method showed that the overall effect of this meta-analysis was stable. CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis showed that elevated blood NfL levels may have prognostic value for functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke. However, given the substantial between-study heterogeneity and the presence of publication bias, these findings should be interpreted with caution. title: USP11 Drives Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Via Promoting Ferroptosis by Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing ASK1.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying ischemic cerebrovascular disorders including cerebral stroke. Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family. It has been shown that USP11 plays diverse and significant roles in a variety of diseases, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer, and intervertebral disc degeneration. However, its precise function and molecular mechanisms involvement in CIRI remain unknown. METHODS: USP11 knockout (USP11-KO) and adeno-associated virus 9-mediated USP11 over-expression (USP11-OE) mice were established as a mouse model of CIRI, and USP11 knockdown and overexpression adenovirus were used to establish a cell model, to investigate the effect of USP11 on CIRI in vivo and in vitro. Molecular biological studies were used to clarify the mechanism of USP11 mediated ferroptosis during CIRI. RESULTS: The expression of USP11 is increased during CIRI. Functionally, USP11 deficiency attenuated neurological deficits, cerebral infarction, neuroinflammation, and ferroptosis during CIRI, whereas specific overexpression of USP11 exacerbated these pathological processes. Furthermore, USP11 knockdown inhibited neuronal injury, inflammatory response and ferroptosis, while USP11 overexpression promoted these processes. Mechanistically, USP11 bind to ASK1 and inhibit its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby enhancing the activity of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling pathway. More importantly, the regulation of USP11 on neuronal ferroptosis and CIRI relied on its regulation of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling axis. CONCLUSIONS: Our study clarified the new functions and mechanisms of USP11 during CIRI. Targeting USP11-ASK1-JNK/p38-ferroptosis may be a new promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of CIRI.

Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family.

title: Pre-Stroke Disability, Stroke Severity and Systemic Inflammation Outweigh Malignancy as Determinants of 90-Day Outcome After Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives Methods Results Conclusions n p p : Patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and coexisting malignancy have worse outcomes, but it is unclear how much of this reflects malignancy itself rather than pre-stroke function, stroke severity and systemic inflammation.: We retrospectively studied consecutive adults with MRI-confirmed AIS admitted to a neurology department in Warsaw, Poland (2020-2024): 130 with documented malignancy and 100 without. Because every patient with a pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score above 2 had a poor outcome by definition, the primary analysis was restricted to patients with pre-stroke mRS 0-2 (= 161; 80 versus 81). Logistic models were adjusted sequentially for age, sex, admission NIHSS, pre-stroke mRS and log-transformed C-reactive protein (CRP).: Groups were comparable in age and vascular comorbidities. Good 90-day outcome was less frequent with malignancy (40.0% versus 58.0%;= 0.028), but the association was no longer significant after adjustment for age, sex and admission NIHSS (odds ratio [OR] 1.55, 95% CI 0.69-3.51) and was null after adding pre-stroke mRS and log-CRP (OR 0.67, 0.25-1.81). Admission NIHSS and log-CRP were the consistent independent predictors. Return to within one mRS point of baseline was achieved by 41.5% versus 59.0% (= 0.011). Among patients with pre-stroke mRS ≤ 2, intravenous thrombolysis rates were similar (22.5% versus 22.2%) and hemorrhagic transformation did not differ (17.4% versus 18.9%).: Malignancy added little prognostic information beyond baseline function, stroke severity and systemic inflammation, although a clinically meaningful residual effect cannot be excluded. Among eligible patients, reperfusion appeared equally safe.

title: Acid-sensing ion channels in ischemic stroke: amplifying and constraining neuronal injury in a phase-specific framework.
abstract: For decades, ischemic neuronal death was understood largely as a story about glutamate. Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) have revised that account. When cerebral blood flow stops, the penumbra can develop prolonged extracellular acidosis, and experimental studies implicate ASIC1a in mediating sufficient Ca²⁺ entry to injure neurons even when glutamate receptors are blocked, a contribution shaped by channel expression, subunit composition, and the intracellular signaling context. However, sustained acidosis does not necessarily imply sustained channel opening, given ASIC1a desensitization. Besides acidosis, glutamate, polyamines, a paradoxical intracellular alkalization, and oxidative stress can enhance ASIC1a activity or expression, and the channel also signals through a non-conducting route, recruiting RIPK1 to trigger necroptosis independently of ion flux. The relative contributions of these conducting and non-conducting mechanisms in vivo remain incompletely defined. Endogenous mechanisms may constrain injury by internalizing the channel, altering subunit expression, including conditioning-associated ASIC2a upregulation, and degrading ASIC1a through estrogen signaling. We argue that these responses are better understood as constraints on injury than as a genuine survival program, a distinction with mechanistic and therapeutic consequences. Critically, the contribution of these mechanisms may vary over time. The same channel acts as a target of homeostatic regulation before stroke, a driver of death during ischemia, a potential target at reperfusion when acidosis persists but restored flow finally permits drug delivery, and an impediment to repair for weeks afterward. The question in ASIC-targeted neuroprotection is not only whether to inhibit the channel, but also when and for how long.

title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activity was comprehensively assessed using five scoring algorithms, including UCell and AUCell. A combined machine learning framework incorporating Boruta algorithm, LASSO regression, and random forest was employed to screen for reliable diagnostic biomarkers. Furthermore, immune infiltration profiles were evaluated using CIBERSORT, regulatory networks were constructed, and molecular subtypes were identified through consensus clustering. Single-cell analysis revealed high CARG activity in endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, and astrocytes. Machine learning identified four robust diagnostic biomarkers (Itgb1, Fn1, Pdlim5, Kdr) with excellent predictive accuracy (AUC, 1) across multiple datasets. These biomarkers strongly correlated with immune cell infiltration, particularly macrophage polarization and mast cell activation, and successfully stratified CIRI samples into two distinct molecular subtypes. By integrating single-cell and transcriptomic data, this study systematically reveals the critical role of CARGs in CIRI. It identifies four core diagnostic genes that are closely associated with immune microenvironment remodeling and neuronal damage, thereby providing new molecular markers and a theoretical foundation for clinical diagnosis and treatment.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Extracellular lactate enhances IL-10 transcription via H4K5 lactylation and promotes an A2-like reactive-astrocyte phenotype after ischemic stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke triggers a rapid rise in lactate levels in the brain tissue. The neuroprotective role of exogenous lactate administered during the reperfusion phase has recently garnered attention. A neuroprotective A2 phenotype of reactive astrocytes (RACs) is characterized by interleukin-10 (IL-10) upregulation, which mitigates neuroinflammation. However, whether exogenous lactate drives A2-like polarization of RACs remains unknown. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which lactate regulates this process. METHODS: Rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and in vitro primary RACs models were established. Western blotting, immunofluorescence staining, and RT-qPCR were used to assess A1/A2 polarization markers, IL-10 expression, histone lactylation, and related neuroimmune signaling molecules. Ubiquitination, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed to clarify the mechanism by which lactate regulates IL-10 expression and A2-like polarization of RACs. RESULTS: Our results demonstrated that increased lactate levels after ischemic stroke correlated with A2 polarization of RACs. Lactate treatment significantly enhanced A2 polarization and reduced infarct volume in the rat MCAO model. Mechanistically, lactate activated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling while suppressing sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) expression and synergistically enhancing H4K5 lactylation (H4K5la) and IL-10 expression, thereby driving RACs toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that elevated extracellular lactate in the acute phase of ischemic stroke drove RACs toward an A2-like phenotype through the Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1)/STAT3/IL-10 and YAP1/SIRT1/H4K5la signaling axes. These findings provide a theoretical basis for targeting RAC lactylation as a potential therapeutic strategy to limit inflammatory damage after stroke.

title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

title: Case Report: Multidisciplinary and individualized management of periprocedural arterial thrombosis and ischemic stroke in children: a three-case series.
abstract: Pediatric arterial thromboembolism is rare but may cause limb loss, extensive cerebral infarction, permanent disability, or death. Evidence guiding reperfusion therapy in children remains limited. We describe three periprocedural events treated according to their vascular territory, threatened tissue, and bleeding risk. A male neonate born at 37 weeks' gestation developed catheter-associated left external iliac-femoral arterial thrombosis after umbilical arterial catheterization during treatment for shock and respiratory illness. Intravenous urokinase and low-molecular-weight heparin achieved complete thrombus resolution on ultrasonography six days after diagnosis. A 5-year-and-5-month-old boy developed acute left internal carotid-middle cerebral artery occlusion with extensive left hemispheric infarction three days after thoracoscopic resection of pulmonary sequestration. Emergency stent-retriever thrombectomy with aspiration achieved immediate recanalization, which persisted at one week; independent ambulation was restored after rehabilitation, although mild right upper-limb symptoms remained at discharge. A 4-month-old boy developed right frontotemporal-insular ischemic infarction after balloon angioplasty for recurrent aortic coarctation. Because no retrievable intracranial large-vessel occlusion was identified and the recent cardiac intervention increased the bleeding risk, aspirin, low-molecular-weight heparin, and supportive treatment were administered. Follow-up MRI one week after diagnosis showed regression of the initial lesion but revealed a new right thalamic lesion suspicious for acute infarction. These heterogeneous cases highlight the need for prompt vascular imaging and individualized multidisciplinary management based on the vascular territory, threatened tissue, patient size, recent procedures, bleeding risk, and procedural feasibility. As a descriptive case series, this report does not establish the comparative efficacy of the treatment strategies.

title: Barriers to intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective case report series from Honduras.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Intravenous (IV) thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is time-dependent and frequently underused in resource-limited settings. We aimed to characterize patients with AIS who did not receive IV thrombolysis at a national referral center in Honduras and to document the barriers to treatment. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center, consecutive case report series of all eligible patients with AIS who were not thrombolyzed at Hospital Escuela Universitario between 1 October and 30 November 2025. We gathered demographics, socioeconomic status, admission severity, process-of-care intervals, contraindications, neuroimaging and thrombolytic availability, complications, and discharge outcomes. Contraindications were classified as absolute or relative according to the 2019 American Heart Association and American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines. A thrombolysis eligibility cascade was the principal analysis. The study was approved by the institutional review board. RESULTS: A total of 23 patients were included (median age 70 years; 14 [60.9%] male). Extreme poverty (≥2 unsatisfied basic needs [UBN]) was present in 14 patients (60.9%). All 23 AIS presentations screened during the period were included, and no patient received thrombolysis (institutional thrombolysis rate 0%). The median onset-to-door time was 10.0 h (IQR 7.0-15.0), and only 1 of 22 patients with a recorded time (4.5%) arrived within 4.5 h. Late or unknown onset was the most frequent absolute contraindication (21 [91.3%]); neuroimaging was available in 22 (95.7%) patients, but the thrombolytic agent was unavailable in every patient (availability 0%). In the eligibility cascade, the single patient within the window had no absolute contraindication and could not be treated because no thrombolytic agent was available. The in-hospital mortality rate was 2 (8.7%), and a good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score 0-2) occurred in 5 of 20 patients with an assessable score. CONCLUSION: Non-administration of thrombolysis reflected late presentation and, above all, the complete unavailability of the thrombolytic agent, whereas imaging and organizational capacity were largely in place. Drug supply was the proximate, modifiable obstacle to reperfusion in this setting.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center, consecutive case report series of all eligible patients with AIS who were not thrombolyzed at Hospital Escuela Universitario between 1 October and 30 November 2025.

title: Recent Advances in Mitochondria-Targeted Delivery Strategies for Ischemic Stroke Therapy.
abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and disability, and mitochondrial dysfunction links bioenergetic failure, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) injury, and cell death. Despite extensive preclinical neuroprotection research, translation has often failed because candidate interventions show inadequate brain exposure and mitochondrial target engagement, are tested under pretreatment or simplified experimental conditions, emphasize short-term infarct reduction rather than durable functional recovery, and are difficult to integrate with time-critical reperfusion care. This Review analyzes mitochondria-targeted delivery as a sequential cascade spanning systemic stability, BBB or nose-to-brain entry, lesion and cell selection, endosomal escape, mitochondrial access, and functional rescue. We compare brain-targeted, intranasal, biomimetic, and organelle-transplantation platforms; place recent examples alongside established mitochondria-targeted antioxidant and mitochondrial-transfer literature; and distinguish localization evidence from causal mitochondrial recovery. The most tractable next steps are a standardized, disease-relevant validation framework and simplified delivery designs compatible with acute stroke workflows. Translational success will require integrated systems that address the complete sequential delivery cascade with the minimum necessary complexity, reproducible manufacturing, clinically relevant treatment windows, and long-term functional and safety endpoints.

title: Mitochondria-associated ferroptosis in ischemic stroke: Pathophysiological evolution, interorganelle crosstalk, and therapeutic targeting.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) results from an acute interruption of cerebral blood flow and the ensuing collapse of energy metabolism. Although vascular recanalization can salvage the ischemic penumbra, its overall benefit remains constrained by a narrow therapeutic window and reperfusion injury. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, contributes to neuronal injury after IS and can amplify ischemia/reperfusion injury. By integrating energy metabolism, iron homeostasis, and redox balance, mitochondria can shape ferroptosis susceptibility within the energy-depleted, iron-dysregulated, and oxidatively stressed ischemic brain. However, most studies have examined iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation at the whole-cell level, leaving the temporal and interorganelle dimensions of mitochondrial regulation of ferroptosis insufficiently integrated. Here, we organize mitochondria-associated ferroptosis across the pathological course of IS, from metabolic reprogramming and substrate accumulation during ischemia to the reverse electron transport-associated reactive oxygen species burst during early reperfusion and subsequent disruption of mitochondrial quality control. We further examine mitochondrial crosstalk with the endoplasmic reticulum, lysosomes, lipid droplets, and nucleus, compare ferroptosis susceptibility across neurovascular unit cell populations, and map these mechanisms onto pharmacological interventions and mechanistically plausible therapeutic windows. Finally, we assess barriers to the clinical translation of mitochondria-targeted therapies and provide a stage-resolved framework for developing neuroprotective strategies in IS.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Prognosis and Emergency Treatment of Patients with Ischemic Stroke in Suzhou, China: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted stroke care globally. This study aimed to assess the impact of COVID-19 on the clinical characteristics, acute treatment, and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in Suzhou, China. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed 506 hospitalized AIS patients from four stroke centers between December 10, 2022, and January 20, 2023. Patients were grouped by COVID- 19 infection status and timing. Clinical data and outcomes were compared with a pre-pandemic cohort from the SUMMITS-II Study. RESULTS: Among included AIS patients, 54.3% were COVID-19-positive. Infected patients had higher baseline NIHSS scores, elevated inflammatory markers, and more in-hospital complications. Intravenous thrombolysis rates increased slightly during the pandemic, despite longer prehospital delays. Emotional disorders were more frequent post-stroke. COVID-19 infection, particularly concurrent with stroke onset, was linked to worse outcomes at 90 days and 1 year. DISCUSSION: The findings suggest that the COVID-19 pandemic significantly influenced the clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke in Suzhou. Patients with AIS with concomitant COVID-19 infection presented with a higher prevalence of vascular risk factors and elevated inflammatory and coagulation markers. Moreover, COVID-19 infection occurring within one week of stroke onset was associated with more severe neurological deficits and poorer short- and long-term prognosis, highlighting the potential role of COVID-19 in worsening stroke outcomes. CONCLUSION: The COVID-19 pandemic adversely affected stroke severity and prognosis. While in-hospital workflows were preserved, delayed presentation and increased systemic burden contributed to unfavorable stroke outcomes. Strengthening stroke care delivery and psychological support during public health crises is essential.

This study aimed to assess the impact of COVID-19 on the clinical characteristics, acute treatment, and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in Suzhou, China. title: Post-Ingestion Blood Hydrogen Kinetics Following Oral Hydrogen-Rich Water Intake in Healthy Adults: A Pilot Pharmacokinetic Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Molecular hydrogen (H2) has gained attention as a therapeutic agent due to its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. However, human Pharmacokinetic (PK) data remain limited, particularly for Hydrogen-Rich Water (HRW). This study aimed to characterize blood hydrogen kinetics following oral HRW intake in healthy adults. METHODS: Twelve healthy participants (mean age 28.8 ± 3.8 years; BMI 23.4 ± 3.2 kg/m²; 50% female) were enrolled in the study. After an overnight fast, participants consumed a single dose of HRW. Blood samples were collected at baseline and at multiple time points up to 120 minutes postingestion. Hydrogen concentrations were measured using a Clark-type microsensor. PK parameters were calculated using non-compartmental analysis, and time-dependent changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects modeling. RESULTS: Baseline hydrogen concentration was 0.25 ± 0.05 μg/L. Peak concentration (Cmax) reached 0.83 ± 0.18 μg/L at 42.9 ± 8.4 minutes (Tmax). The elimination half-life was 144.8 ± 41.7 minutes, and total systemic exposure (AUC₀-∞) was 128.6 ± 27.1 μg/L·min. Hydrogen levels were significantly elevated at 15, 60, and 90 minutes compared to baseline. Notable inter-individual variability was observed, and no sex-related differences were detected. DISCUSSION: Oral HRW intake resulted in measurable systemic hydrogen exposure, with a biphasic concentration pattern, suggesting rapid absorption possibly followed by redistribution. Observed concentrations approached proposed minimal effective levels but were not sustained, raising questions about optimal dosing strategies. CONCLUSION: HRW ingestion produces detectable and biologically relevant increases in blood hydrogen levels. These findings support HRW as a viable route of H2 administration and provide a foundation for future studies investigating dosing, kinetics, and therapeutic applications.

title: Molecular hydrogen in biomedicine: A comprehensive review of mechanisms, multi-system therapeutic effects, and emerging delivery strategies.
abstract: 2 2 Molecular hydrogen (H) has attracted increasing interest as a potential therapeutic agent because of its redox-modulating and anti-inflammatory properties. This review summarizes current evidence regarding its biological mechanisms, multisystem effects, and emerging delivery strategies. Experimental studies suggest that Hmay attenuate oxidative injury and inflammatory signaling through both direct interactions with highly reactive species and indirect modulation of pathways involving nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB), NLRP3, mitochondrial function, and immune regulation. Protective effects have been reported across cardiovascular, neurological, respiratory, digestive, renal, musculoskeletal, and metabolic disease models. However, the available evidence remains predominantly preclinical, whereas human studies are comparatively limited and heterogeneous. The optimal route of administration, dose, treatment duration, pharmacokinetic profile, and long-term safety and efficacy also remain insufficiently defined. Emerging delivery platforms may improve local retention and controlled release but remain largely experimental. Overall, molecular hydrogen represents a promising adjunctive therapeutic strategy, although further mechanistic validation and well-designed clinical studies are required before routine clinical application.

title: Clusterin interference decreases cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by suppressing TFR1-dependent ferroptosis.
abstract: Ferroptosis plays a crucial role in the pathological process of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury, but the specific regulatory mechanism of Clusterin in this process remains unclear. This study aims to investigate whether interfering with Clusterin can alleviate cerebral I/R injury by regulating neuronal ferroptosis. A cerebral I/R injury mouse model was established and the adeno-associated virus (AAV-sh-Clusterin) was stereotactically injected into the brain. Brain tissue damage was evaluated using TTC and HE staining. The expressions of blood-brain barrier proteins (Occludin, ZO-1) and inflammatory factors (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6) were detected. Downstream differentially expressed genes were analyzed through mRNA transcriptome sequencing. The expression changes of iron death-related indicators (Fe2 +, MDA, GSH, NRF2, GPX4, ACSL4, SLC7A11) were evaluated by means of biochemical methods and WB/qPCR. Subsequently, an in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) model of HT22 cells was constructed to analyze the effects of Clusterin interference on the proliferation and ferroptosis of HT22 cells. The interaction between Clusterin and TFR1 was detected, and a rescue experiment was carried out by overexpressing TFR1. Clusterin was significantly upregulated in both in vitro and in vivo models. Interference with Clusterin effectively reduced the volume of cerebral infarction, upregulated the expressions of Occludin and ZO-1, and inhibited the inflammatory response. Besides, interference with Clusterin significantly decreased the ferroptosis level in mouse brain tissue. There is a protein interaction between Clusterin and TFR1, and the rescue experiment indicated that overexpression of TFR1 could counteract the inhibitory effect of sh-Clusterin on ferroptosis and the proliferation protection effect of HT22 cells. In summary, interfering with Clusterin by inhibiting TFR1-dependent neuronal ferroptosis significantly mitigates neuronal damage and inflammatory responses induced by cerebral I/R.

title: Activatable MRI-Trackable Spherical Nucleic Acids for Idebenone Delivery Against Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
abstract: 2 Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a key driver of poor prognosis in ischemic stroke. Idebenone (IDBN) shows promise for mitigating IRI, but its efficacy is limited by poor brain accumulation. Moreover, IDBN cannot be visually tracked, making it difficult to confirm whether it reaches the ischemic brain and exerts therapeutic effects. Here, IDBN functionalized with a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-cleavable bond is grafted onto phosphorothioate-modified DNA strands and co-assembled with ultrasmall superparamagnetic iron oxide (USPIO) to form USPIO-IDBN-SNAs, where SNAs stands for spherical nucleic acids. Exploiting upregulated class A scavenger receptors, USPIO-IDBN-SNAs target the ischemic area without targeting modifications and increase local IDBN concentration. Hydrophobic IDBN inside the SNAs limits water access to USPIO clusters, suppressing their contrast-enhancing ability. Under oxidative stress, IDBN is rapidly released and exerts remarkable protection. This release allows USPIO clusters to re-establish contact with water, activating their contrast-enhancing ability on T-weighted imaging. Collectively, USPIO-IDBN-SNAs provide significant neuroprotection against IRI and offer a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-visible platform to monitor IDBN release in the ischemic brain, presenting a promising theranostic approach for precise, trackable stroke therapy.
englishSummary: 2 Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a key driver of poor prognosis in ischemic stroke. Idebenone (IDBN) shows promise for mitigating IRI, but its efficacy is limited by poor brain accumulation. Moreover, IDBN cannot be visually tracked, making it difficult to confirm whether it reaches the ischemic brain and exerts therapeutic effects.

title: 18β-Glycyrrhetinic Acid-Loaded ROS-Responsive Liposomes Enhance the Neuroprotective Efficacy against Cerebral Ischemic Stroke in Mice via a Microenvironment-Responsive Strategy.
abstract: 18β-Glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) exhibits excellent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, and has attracted considerable attention in the field of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury therapy. However, it is plagued by problems of low bioavailability and dose-dependent toxicity. As a drug delivery platform for the treatment of ischemic stroke, microenvironment-responsive liposomes can cross the impaired blood-brain barrier, efficiently deliver drugs to the lesion sites, and improve therapeutic efficacy. Herein, to address the challenges posed by the highly oxidative-stress microenvironment of I/R and the intrinsic physicochemical properties of GA, we encapsulated GA into liposomes and incorporated thioketal (TK) linkages into the phospholipid bilayer to fabricate GA@TK-Lip. GA@TK-Lip can effectively target damaged neurons, attenuate neuroinflammation, scavenge excessive ROS, ameliorate cellular oxidative stress via the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway, reduce neuronal apoptosis and cerebral infarct volume to 43.2% and 23.3% of that in the MCAO group, and restore neurological function. Collectively, this study provides novel insights into the development of promising therapeutic strategies for ischemic stroke.

title: CYTIP promotes pro-inflammatory activation of microglia through interaction with LRRFIP2 following ischemic stroke.
abstract: Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is a critical contributor to cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. However, the functional heterogeneity of microglia presents significant challenges in defining therapeutic signatures. By integrating single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) of a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model with bulk RNA sequencing of BV2 microglia subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), we identified Cytip as a highly upregulated core regulator within a transient "primed" microglial subpopulation upon I/R insult. Functional validation demonstrated that Cytip promotes a pro-inflammatory microglial phenotype and exacerbates oxidative stress, whereas its knockdown ameliorates these OGD/R-induced dysfunctions. Mechanistically, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry revealed that CYTIP directly interacts with LRRFIP2. Overexpression of LRRFIP2 counteracted CYTIP-mediated pathogenic effects, significantly suppressing microglial inflammation and IL-1β production. These findings suggest that CYTIP promotes microglial inflammatory responses via the NLRP3/LRRFIP2 axis, highlighting the CYTIP-LRRFIP2 interaction as a promising therapeutic target for post-stroke recovery.

title: Intraoperative Hypotension During Endovascular Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke and Functional Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal blood pressure management during endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. Intraprocedural hypotension may compromise cerebral perfusion and worsen neurological outcomes, yet existing evidence is inconsistent, and no prior meta-analysis has synthesized observational data on intraoperative hypotension during EVT. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating the association between intraoperative hypotension and outcomes in patients undergoing EVT for acute ischemic stroke. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to May 2024 without language restrictions. Eligible studies enrolled adult patients undergoing EVT with reported intraoperative blood pressure data and prespecified clinical outcomes. The primary outcome was favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included failure of reperfusion (Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction <2b), early neurological improvement, final infarct volume, and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Pooled odds ratios with 95% CIs were estimated using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with the Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions tool and certainty of evidence with the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) framework. RESULTS: 2 Nine studies comprising 1737 patients were included in the systematic review, of which 7 contributed to quantitative synthesis. Intraoperative hypotension was significantly associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome (odds ratio, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.41-0.74]; I=0%). No significant association was found between hypotension and failure of reperfusion (odds ratio, 1.36 [95% CI, 0.85-2.18]). Evidence regarding early neurological improvement was limited. Narrative synthesis indicated that greater cumulative exposure to hypotension correlated with larger final infarct volumes. Certainty of evidence was rated high for favorable functional outcome and low for failure of reperfusion. CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative hypotension during EVT, defined as mean arterial pressure below 60 to 70 mm Hg or a relative decrease of ≥20% to 40% from baseline, is associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes, independent of reperfusion status. These findings support hemodynamic monitoring during EVT and suggest that intraoperative hypotension is associated with worse functional outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Optimal blood pressure management during endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. Intraprocedural hypotension may compromise cerebral perfusion and worsen neurological outcomes, yet existing evidence is inconsistent, and no prior meta-analysis has synthesized observational data on intraoperative hypotension during EVT. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating the association between intraoperative hypotension and outcomes in patients undergoing EVT for acute ischemic stroke.

title: Hydrogen gas and olfactory dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease: the Hydrogen-Olfactory-Limbic hypothesis.
abstract: Olfactory dysfunction is increasingly recognized as an early clinical feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD), often preceding measurable cognitive impairment and associated with subsequent cognitive decline. Despite this relatively consistent clinical association, the anatomical, cellular, and physiological substrates underlying olfactory dysfunction in AD remain poorly understood. Post-mortem human studies have identified amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau pathology in olfactory structures, including the olfactory epithelium and anterior olfactory nucleus. However, the available anatomical evidence remains limited, and the presence of these pathological proteins does not establish that they cause olfactory dysfunction. Likewise, it remains uncertain whether early olfactory impairment reflects peripheral sensory dysfunction, neuronal loss, synaptic or circuit abnormalities, altered higher-order olfactory processing, disruption of olfactory-limbic networks, or a combination of these processes. Although the olfactory epithelium possesses lifelong regenerative capacity, whether this capacity is altered during AD progression remains unresolved. Molecular hydrogen (H₂) has demonstrated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, mitochondrial-modulatory, and cytoprotective effects in diverse experimental systems. However, direct evidence that hydrogen modifies AD-associated olfactory dysfunction is currently lacking. In this Perspective, we propose the Hydrogen-Olfactory-Limbic hypothesis as an experimentally testable framework rather than an established therapeutic mechanism. We suggest that molecular hydrogen can serve as an experimental intervention to determine whether modulating oxidative, inflammatory, and metabolic processes affects olfactory function and olfactory-limbic circuit physiology during AD progression. This framework integrates behavioral, anatomical, molecular, electrophysiological, regenerative, and connectivity measurements to address two fundamental questions: what causes early olfactory dysfunction in AD, and can molecular hydrogen modify biologically relevant processes associated with this phenotype?

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of cerebral edema in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective observational single-centre study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral edema (CED) is a common complication of acute ischemic stroke, associated with increased mortality and poor functional outcomes. While infarct size is a known predictor, the role of sodium homeostasis remains unclear. This study evaluated risk factors for CED and its impact on outcomes. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 178 patients with acute non-lacunar ischemic stroke. Cerebral edema was assessed and graded using the SITS-MOST edema scale over the first seven days. Sodium concentration and variability were monitored daily. Risk factors for CED were identified through multivariate logistic regression, and the impact of CED on mortality, functional outcomes, hemorrhagic transformation, and seizures was analyzed. RESULTS: CED occurred in 38.2% of patients and was associated with larger infarcts (> 3 cm), higher NIHSS, lower ASPECTS, lack of reperfusion, and multi-territory involvement. No differences were observed in demographics or cardiovascular risk factors. Sodium levels were higher on days 3 and 5 in CED patients, with greater variability, while baseline levels were not predictive. Infarct size and day 3 sodium were independent predictors. CED was linked to worse outcomes, including higher 1-month mortality (23.5% vs. 1.8%), increased hemorrhagic transformation, and reduced functional independence. No association with seizures was found. CONCLUSIONS: Infarct size remains the strongest risk factor for cerebral edema after ischemic stroke. Baseline sodium levels were not determining CED development. CED worsens outcomes but is not linked to seizure risk. These findings underscore the importance of early imaging and suggest a potential role for targeted anti-edema therapies in patients with larger strokes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Cerebral edema (CED) is a common complication of acute ischemic stroke, associated with increased mortality and poor functional outcomes. While infarct size is a known predictor, the role of sodium homeostasis remains unclear. This study evaluated risk factors for CED and its impact on outcomes.

title: Astrocytic NOX2 contributes to ROS-associated mitochondrial dysfunction in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury: modulation by electroacupuncture.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) causes severe neuronal damage, in which oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction are major pathological events. Astrocytes are important regulators of redox homeostasis in the injured brain, yet whether astrocytic NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) contributes to mitochondrial impairment after ischemia remains poorly understood. Electroacupuncture (EA) has been reported to protect against ischemic brain injury, but the cellular mechanisms involved remain unclear. METHODS: In this study, a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model was combined with astrocyte-specific NOX2 knockdown using stereotactic viral delivery. Neurological deficits, infarct size, cerebral blood flow, reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) levels, mitochondrial morphology, and mitochondrial dynamics-associated proteins were examined. RESULTS: MCAO/R resulted in increased astrocytic NOX2 expression, excessive ROS generation, mitochondrial fragmentation, impaired energy metabolism, and neurological dysfunction. EA treatment alleviated these changes by reducing NOX2 activation and ROS accumulation, improving mitochondrial morphology and ATP production, and restoring the balance between mitochondrial fission and fusion. These effects were reflected by decreased Drp1 and Fis1 expression and increased Mfn2 and Opa1 expression. Notably, astrocytic NOX2 knockdown produced similar protective effects and further strengthened the benefits of EA. CONCLUSION: Astrocytic NOX2 contributes to ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ischemic brain injury. EA treatment is accompanied by reduced astrocytic NOX2 expression, attenuated oxidative stress, and restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis, suggesting that regulation of astrocytic NOX2 may contribute to the protective effects of EA. Targeting astrocytic NOX2 may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.

Electroacupuncture (EA) has been reported to protect against ischemic brain injury, but the cellular mechanisms involved remain unclear.

title: Guaianolide-type sesquiterpenes from Rhaponticum repens (L.) Hidalgo with anti-ischemic stroke activity.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a severe central nervous system disorder with high mortality and disability rates, and microglia-mediated neuroinflammation exacerbates ischemic brain injury. In this study, the traditional ethnic medicine Rhaponticum repens (L.) Hidalgo was found to significantly inhibit lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced microglial overactivation and to alleviate cerebral injury in middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats, suggesting its therapeutic potential against IS. Bioactivity-guided fractionation of its active fraction led to the isolation and identification of 44 compounds, including 22 guaianolide-type sesquiterpenes (1-22) and 22 other types (23-44), among which five were previously undescribed compounds (1-5). Activity screening revealed that most of the guaianolide-type sesquiterpenes markedly suppressed microglial overactivation, representing the principal pharmacologically active constituents responsible for the anti-neuroinflammatory effects of this plant. High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis further indicated that cynaropikrin (8), the most active compound (IC₅₀ = 3.8 μM), was the most abundant component in the active fraction, accounting for approximately 14.39% of its content. In vivo experiments confirmed that cynaropikrin at a dose of 5 mg/kg attenuated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in MCAO/R rats, and acute toxicity tests demonstrated its favorable in vivo safety profile. Target prediction, molecular docking, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analyses indicate that cynaropikrin directly targets NLRP3. Western blot analysis further shows that cynaropikrin reduces NLRP3 protein expression, caspase-1 activation and IL-1β maturation, thereby alleviating neuroinflammation and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.

title: Danhong Injection combined with t-PA attenuates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and reduces hemorrhagic transformation: association with NF-κB/MMPs signaling.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Ischemic stroke, caused by cerebral arterial thrombosis and interrupted blood supply, is a leading cause of brain dysfunction. Tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) is the standard thrombolytic agent but is limited by hemorrhagic transformation (HT) and blood-brain barrier (BBB) damage. This study explored the beneficial effects of Danhong Injection (DHI, a Traditional Chinese Medicine) as an adjuvant combined with t-PA for the treatment of ischemic stroke. METHODS: Based on cell viability assays, optimal concentrations were 20 μl/ml DHI + 20 μg/ml t-PA. In vitro (mouse brain microvascular endothelial cell, OGD/R model) and in vivo (MCAO rat model) experiments were conducted to assess relevant parameters. KEY FINDINGS: In vitro, the combination improved cell morphology, reduced apoptosis, and downregulated phosphorylated NF-κB p65, MMP-2, MMP-9, and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α expression. In vivo, DHI + t-PA decreased P-Selectin, 6-keto-PGF1a, TXA2, PAI-1, MMP-2, and MMP-9 levels, alleviated cerebral infarction and HT, and enhanced neurological recovery. CONCLUSIONS: These protective effects were accompanied by downregulation of the NF-κB/MMPs pathway, suggesting a plausible correlation linked to BBB-related protective phenotypes. Our findings provide preliminary evidence supporting DHI as a promising adjuvant to optimize t-PA-based stroke therapy.

title: Dynamics of Serum Amyloid A Levels in the Blood, Brain and Liver in a Mouse Model of Focal Cerebral Ischemia.
abstract: This study examined the dynamics of serum amyloid A (SAA) levels in the blood, brain, and liver over time using a mouse model of focal cerebral ischemia induced by occlusion of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) for 4 h followed by reperfusion. Blood SAA concentrations increased transiently after cerebral infarction, coinciding with changes in brain and liver SAA gene expression and protein levels. SAA concentrations in the brain, liver, and blood increased at similar time points after cerebral infarction, suggesting that SAA may serve as an important indicator of the associated pathological condition.

title: Bridging Thrombolysis Versus Direct Endovascular Thrombectomy in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients With ASPECTS ≤5: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) caused by large vessel occlusion (LVO). However, the efficacy and safety of bridging thrombolysis (BT) compared to direct EVT (dEVT) remain controversial, particularly in patients with large core infarcts (Alberta stroke program early CT score [ASPECTS] ≤5). This meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of BT versus dEVT in this population. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from January 1, 2010, to September 21, 2024, for studies comparing BT and dEVT in AIS patients with ASPECTS ≤5. Outcomes included functional outcomes (mRS 0-2 and 0-3), intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), symptomatic ICH (sICH), 90-day mortality, and successful reperfusion. Data were pooled using random-effects models. RESULTS: Twelve studies (3907 patients) were included. BT significantly improved favorable (OR: 1.43, 95% CI: 1.17-1.76) and moderate functional outcomes (OR: 1.28, 95% CI: 1.10-1.48) compared to dEVT. No significant differences were observed in sICH, ICH, 90-day mortality, or successful reperfusion. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that BT may be associated with better functional outcomes in patients with ASPECTS ≤5, without increasing major safety events compared with dEVT. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the evidence is mainly observational, and residual confounding cannot be excluded. Further well-designed randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.

However, the efficacy and safety of bridging thrombolysis (BT) compared to direct EVT (dEVT) remain controversial, particularly in patients with large core infarcts (Alberta stroke program early CT score [ASPECTS] ≤5). This meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of BT versus dEVT in this population.

title: Design, Synthesis of 3-n-Butylphthalide-Hydrazine/Hydrazide Derivatives as Potential Anti-Ischemic Stroke Agents.
abstract: 3 To identify novel therapeutic candidates for ischemic stroke, a series of hydrazine- and hydrazide-derived analogs based on 3-n-butylphthalide (NBP) were designed and synthesized in this study, and their anti-ischemic stroke activities were systematically assessed. Among all synthesized derivatives, the compound NBP-HY exerted potent antiplatelet aggregation and antioxidant activities in vitro. Consistent in vivo results revealed that NBP-HY significantly alleviated thrombus formation in both carrageenan-induced tail thrombosis and FeCl-induced carotid artery thrombosis models. In a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) injury model, NBP-HY markedly reduced cerebral infarct volume, improved cerebral blood perfusion, and protected hippocampal CA1 and cortical neurons, exhibiting superior therapeutic efficacy compared with the lead compound NBP. Further pharmacological experiments showed that NBP-HY exhibits moderate metabolic stability in liver microsomes, good blood-brain barrier permeability in the PAMPA-BBB model, and minimal impact on mice's physiological hemostatic function. Collectively, this work indicates that NBP‑HY has potential as a therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke and warrants further in‑depth investigation.

Among all synthesized derivatives, the compound NBP-HY exerted potent antiplatelet aggregation and antioxidant activities in vitro. Consistent in vivo results revealed that NBP-HY significantly alleviated thrombus formation in both carrageenan-induced tail thrombosis and FeCl-induced carotid artery thrombosis models.

title: Discovery of metabolite biomarkers for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury based on metabolomics: neurotoxic mechanism and functional validation of a flavopiridol -related metabolite.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the role and potential mechanism of metabolite alterations during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) and to explore novel candidate molecular markers for the diagnosis of this disease. METHODS: A rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion was established using the modified Longa EZ intraluminal suture method. The infarct status was comprehensively evaluated by neurological deficit score (mNSS), TTC staining, HE staining, and Nissl staining. Serum metabolite changes after CIRI were detected using non-targeted metabolomics, and the potential toxic effects of significantly altered metabolites were predicted using the ProTox tool. Subsequently, bioinformatics analysis was employed to identify core targets and key pathways associated with the metabolite of interest, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to predict their interactions. RESULTS: Metabolomic analysis identified 41 significantly upregulated and 232 downregulated metabolites. Among the significantly altered metabolites, a flavopiridol-related metabolite (FRM) exhibited potential neurotoxic characteristics. A total of 193 CIRI-related core targets were associated with this metabolite, from which 10 core targets and 15 key pathways were further screened. ROC analysis suggested that this metabolite possessed good discriminatory ability (AUC = 0.94). Molecular docking results showed binding energies of less than -7 kcal/mol for all core targets. A 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation indicated that the complex formed by the FRM and SRC remained structurally stable, as evidenced by balanced RMSD, Rg, SASA, and P-L-RMSD values. The calculated binding free energy was -32.48 kcal/mol, with key residues LEU-393, MET-341, and GLU-339 contributing significantly to the interaction, suggesting potential biological activity. CONCLUSION: This study reveals a complex metabolic reprogramming phenomenon during CIRI and preliminarily identifies a FRM as a potential candidate molecular marker and possible interventional target, providing a new theoretical basis and directions for future research on the diagnosis and treatment of CIRI.

title: Comparative Effectiveness of Intravenous Tenecteplase versus Alteplase in Posterior Circulation Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Posterior circulation ischemic stroke (PCIS) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, and the optimal intravenous thrombolytic strategy in this subgroup remains unclear. METHODS: We searched databases for studies comparing intravenous tenecteplase with alteplase in adults with PCIS. The primary outcome was functional independence at 90 days (mRS 0-2). Secondary outcomes included other functional outcomes, reperfusion, hemorrhagic complications, and mortality. RESULTS: Five studies involving 997 patients were included. Regarding efficacy outcomes, tenecteplase was associated with a significantly greater likelihood of achieving an ambulatory functional outcome at 90 days (mRS 0-3) [RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.03-1.60; p = 0.02] and improved pre-EVT perfusion [RR 2.18, 95% CI 1.06-4.46; p = 0.03]. No significant differences were observed for excellent functional outcome (mRS 0-1) [RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.91-1.56; p = 0.20], functional independence (mRS 0-2) [RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.89-1.37; p = 0.39], or post-EVT perfusion [RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.89-1.40; p = 0.34]. Regarding safety outcomes, no significant differences were observed between tenecteplase and alteplase for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) [RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.36-2.22; p = 0.81], any intracranial hemorrhage [RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.59-1.78; p = 0.94], parenchymal hematoma [RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.24-2.38; p = 0.64], or 90-day mortality [RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.66-1.17; p = 0.39]. CONCLUSION: Tenecteplase may improve reperfusion and ambulatory recovery without increasing hemorrhagic complications or mortality compared with alteplase in PCIS, although larger PCIS-specific studies are needed.

title: Classical and intermediate monocytes and their ratios in the natural immune course of ischemic stroke.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Monocytes contribute to the immune response to ischemic stroke (IS), participating in both acute inflammation and post-ischemic repair. However, classical (cMo), intermediate (intMo), and non-classical (ncMo) monocytes differ in function, and composite indices such as the lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR) do not distinguish between them. We characterized the dynamics of monocyte subpopulations and of two subset-derived ratios, the lymphocyte-to-classical monocyte ratio (LMRclas) and the lymphocyte-to-intermediate monocyte ratio (LMRint), in patients with acute IS who did not undergo reperfusion therapy, allowing assessment of the natural immune response. METHODS: We prospectively studied 31 patients and 16 controls, obtaining complete blood counts and/or flow cytometry in patients at admission, 24 h, and 48 h, and relating these findings to the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) through 90 days, and the development of stroke-associated infection (SAI). Correlations were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction applied within four prespecified families. RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients showed reduced lymphocyte counts at admission, 24 h, and 48 h, whereas total monocyte counts did not differ at any time point. Within the monocyte compartment, intMo counts increased at 24 h and 48 h, and LMRint decreased at 48 h, while cMo and ncMo counts remained unchanged. A lower LMR at 48 h was associated with greater stroke severity and with poorer functional outcome; higher cMo counts at 48 h and a lower LMRclas at 24 h were associated with poorer outcome at 90 days; and a lower LMRclas at admission was associated with the development of SAI. None of these associations retained significance after correction for multiple comparisons, and neither ratio remained independently associated with 90-day outcome after adjustment for age, sex, and baseline NIHSS. DISCUSSION: Taken together, these exploratory findings suggest a reorganization of the monocyte compartment after ischemic stroke despite an unchanged total monocyte count, a shift that composite indices cannot capture but that LMRclas and LMRint might reflect. The estimates reported here may serve as a basis for evaluating these ratios in larger, adequately powered cohorts.

title: Tenecteplase for Acute Ischemic Stroke: From Molecular Bioengineering to Phase III Pivotal Trials.
abstract: Intravenous thrombolysis with alteplase is a primary reperfusion therapy for acute ischemic stroke, yet its clinical utility is constrained by a short half-life, continuous infusion requirements, and susceptibility to plasminogen activator inhibitor-1. Tenecteplase, a bioengineered variant of alteplase, was developed to address these limitations through a prolonged half-life, increased fibrin specificity, and enhanced resistance to plasminogen activator inhibitor-1. These structural modifications enable single-bolus administration and reduce systemic fibrinolytic disturbance. In this review, we examine how the targeted molecular modifications of tenecteplase shaped its stepwise translational development in acute ischemic stroke. We first detail the limitations of alteplase, which motivated the transition to alternative agents, the molecular rationale for tenecteplase, and its preclinical evidence. Furthermore, we synthesize the phase II dose-finding trials that established 0.25 mg/kg as providing the optimal efficacy and safety balance, distinguishing it from the excess intracranial hemorrhage observed with the 0.4 mg/kg dose. Finally, we review the pivotal phase III trials across diverse populations demonstrating that tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg is non-inferior to alteplase and represents a practical, evidence-based alternative, particularly where single-bolus administration may facilitate workflow or transfer for endovascular thrombectomy. Viewed through this molecular-to-clinical framework, the development of tenecteplase illustrates how targeted protein engineering can translate into pharmacological, operational, and clinical advantages in stroke reperfusion therapy.

title: Precision Oxygen Modulation in the Reperfusion Era: Conditioning and Therapeutic Strategies in Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) and advanced perfusion imaging have transformed acute ischemic stroke (AIS) treatment, yet tissue hypoxia may persist because of delayed presentation, incomplete reperfusion, microvascular no-reflow, and secondary injury. Oxygen is an essential substrate for cerebral metabolism and a modifiable therapeutic exposure; however, clinical studies of oxygen-based interventions have yielded inconsistent results because of heterogeneity in timing, dose, delivery, and patient selection. Here we propose precision oxygen modulation (POM) as a stage-, phenotype-, and tissue-informed framework for the reperfusion era-treating oxygen exposure as a dose-titrated therapy that must be matched to the right patient, time window, physiological target, and safety boundary. POM integrates oxygen conditioning strategies that may prime neurovascular resilience before or around ischemia, time-limited therapeutic oxygen strategies deployed around reperfusion to support tissue at risk, and recovery-stage strategies paired with rehabilitation. We synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence linking oxygen tension to excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and repair, while emphasizing the context-dependent risks of hyperoxia. We outline an operational decision framework and translational roadmap based on phenotype- and imaging-guided selection, biomarker validation, protocolized dosing, predefined safety boundaries, and phenotype-enriched randomized trials. POM is presented as a testable translational framework for organizing heterogeneous evidence and guiding the prospective validation of stage-specific oxygen modulation in modern stroke care.

title: Deterioration of Peri-Infarct Microvascular Hemodynamics Following Successful Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Predicts Infarct Growth.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion. METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study from the University of California, Los Angeles, patients with acute ischemic stroke from 2015 to 2020 were included if they had excellent reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2c) and diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MRIs at baseline, immediately PT, and 24 to 48 hours after thrombectomy. Peri-infarct regions were defined as time to maximum ≥6-second regions on baseline MRI that were not infarcted on immediate PT MRI. Following image coregistration, quantitative values of perfusion parameters, including RTH, were obtained from peri-infarct regions on immediate PT MRI. Two primary outcomes were assessed: (1) infarct growth ≥10 mL and (2) poor functional outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale score >2). Associations between clinical and imaging parameters and outcomes were evaluated using univariate analysis. Age, sex, and covariates that were significant in univariate analysis were included in logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: P P P P Among 47 patients included in the analysis (62% women; mean age, 72±13 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 14), 20 (43%) patients had substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcome. Peri-infarct RTH was significantly (=0.005) higher in patients with infarct growth >10 mL than those without and remained as an independent predictor (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-2.0];=0.04). Similarly, the peri-infarct RTH was significantly higher (<0.001) in patients with poor functional outcomes than those with good functional outcomes and remained as a significant predictor of poor functional outcome (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-1.9];=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Increased peri-infarct RTH on immediate PT MRI predicts substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcomes in successfully reperfused patients with acute ischemic stroke. Results highlight the role of microvascular dysfunction depicted by elevated RTH as a potential marker of no-reflow phenomenon despite excellent macrovascular reperfusion.

title: Nationwide Analysis of Palliative Care Utilization Among Ischemic Stroke Hospitalizations.
abstract: Background/Objectives Methods Results Conclusions : Palliative care (PC) is an integral component of ischemic stroke management, yet contemporary nationwide data on its utilization, recent utilization rates, and associated disparities are lacking. This study examined PC utilization rates, demographic disparities, and clinical factors associated with receipt of PC (PC) across ischemic stroke hospitalizations in the United States (US) from 2016 to 2022.: This retrospective cross-sectional study used data extracted from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) to identify adult hospitalizations primary for ischemic stroke, identified via validated International Classification of Disease-10th Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. PC use was identified using the code Z51.5. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with PC, adjusting for demographics, hospital characteristics, clinical severity (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] category, Charlson Comorbidity Index), complications, and receipt of thrombolysis/thrombectomy.: Among 4350,924 weighted ischemic stroke hospitalizations, 253,555 (5.83%) received PC, ranging from 5.34% in 2016 to 6.40% in 2022. Hospitalizations involving Black (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.71; 95% CI, 0.69-0.74) and Hispanic (aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.70-0.77) individuals had significantly lower odds of PC receipt compared with those involving White individuals. Lower-income quartiles, rural hospitals, and non-teaching hospitals were independently associated with reduced odds of PC receipt. Compared with NIHSS scores of 0-9, higher NIHSS scores demonstrated a graded association with PC use (NIHSS 20-29: aOR, 8.53; NIHSS 30-39: aOR, 12.22). Malignant neoplasm (aOR, 3.83), respiratory failure (aOR, 3.04), and cerebral edema (aOR, 2.82) showed clinically large statistically significant associations with PC. Receipt of reperfusion therapies were inversely associated with PC use (aOR, 0.85 for thrombolysis; aOR, 0.71 for thrombectomy).: PC utilization among ischemic stroke hospitalizations remains low, with persistent racial/ethnic, socioeconomic, and institutional disparities. System-level interventions are needed to expand equitable PC access across all stages of ischemic stroke care, including patients who receive reperfusion therapies.

title: Longxue tongluo capsule enhances ischemic stroke recovery via microbiota-metabolite-gene interactions.
abstract: The gut-brain axis represents an emerging therapeutic target. This study seeks to investigate the regulatory effects of LXTL on the brain-gut axis and to elucidate its mechanism of action during the ischemic stroke recovery period. This study investigated the effects of LXTL on a middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion model. The assessment of recovery effects was conducted through the evaluation of brain injury scores, Y-maze performance, open field tests. Furthermore, comprehensive analyses were conducted on the gut microbiota, damaged brain tissue, cecal contents, and brain samples using metagenomic sequencing, transcriptomic sequencing, and non-targeted metabolomics. And the selected targets were verified. Integrated analyses were conducted by constructing correlation networks and performing joint pathway enrichment to elucidate the connections between microbial alterations, metabolite changes, and gene expression modifications. LXTL improved cognitive and exploratory behaviors, reduced brain damage and neuron loss, and enhanced gut health by increasing beneficial bacteria like Eubacterium and Kurthia. It boosted SCFAs, neuroactive metabolites, and altered nucleotide metabolism. LXTL is linked to genes involved in neurorepair and immune homeostasis, correlates with microglial polarization, and is associated with genes such as Ngfr, Card9, Chat, Nkg7, and Gch1 within the pertinent pathways. The integrated network linked LXTL-enhanced microbiota, gut and brain metabolites, and repair genes, facilitating recovery through a neurorepair-immune-metabolic triad. LXTL aids ischemic stroke recovery by altering gut microbiota and gut-brain metabolite profiles, while regulating brain gene networks related to neuroplasticity, inflammation, and metabolism. This demonstrates LXTL's multi-target effects through the gut-brain axis, underscoring the potential of herbal medicine in stroke rehabilitation.

title: Barbaloin Attenuates Cerebral Ischemia and Reperfusion Injury in Rats and Inhibits Lipopolysaccharide-Stimulated Inflammatory Responses in BV2 Microglial Cells.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Barbaloin (BAR) is a naturally occurring bioactive anthracycline derived from the leaf exudates of aloe plants with a variety of biological and pharmacological properties. The aim of the present study was to investigate the neuroprotective effects of BAR against cerebral ischemia and reperfusion (I/R) injury in rats and the possible underlying mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Middle cerebral artery occlusion followed by reperfusion was used to induce cerebral I/R injury in rats, and BAR was administered intraperitoneally after the onset of ischemia. RESULTS: In vitro We found that BAR remarkably improved neurological scores, reduced brain infarct volume, and inhibited neuronal apoptosis in cerebral I/R rats. Furthermore, BAR upregulated Bcl-2 protein levels and downregulated cleaved caspase-3, Bax, and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) in the ischemic cortex. I/R injury-induced increases in malondialdehyde content, and decreases in glutathione, glutathione peroxidase, and superoxide dismutase activities were significantly attenuated by BAR administration., BAR pretreatment inhibited the release of proinflammatory cytokines (iNOS, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interleukin-6) and reduced protein levels of iNOS and nuclear expression of nuclear factor-κB p65 in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV-2 microglial cells. CONCLUSION: Taken together, our data suggest that BAR possesses neuroprotective effects against cerebral I/R injury through antiapoptotic, antioxidative, and anti-inflammatory properties.
