title: Augmentation of nitric oxide, superoxide, and peroxynitrite production during cerebral ischemia and reperfusion in the rat.
abstract: The effect of ischemia produced by bilateral occlusion of the common carotid arteries (30 min) followed by 4 hours of reperfusion on total and inducible nitric oxide synthase (NOS) activity and the production of nitric oxide (NO), superoxide and peroxynitrite in the cerebral hemispheres was determined in the rat. Compared to sham-operated controls, cerebral ischemia-reperfusion resulted in a significant increase in total and inducible NOS activity and a significant increase in the production of NO and superoxide in the cerebral hemispheres. The level of NO in the plasma and the peripheral leukocyte count were also significantly increased. Immunohistochemical staining for nitrotyrosine (a marker of peroxynitrite production) showed that ischemia-reperfusion resulted in increased synthesis of cerebral peroxynitrite. Administration of the irreversible NOS inhibitor, Nomega-nitro-L-arginine (L-NA), increased superoxide levels in the brain and significantly reduced plasma NO. Total and inducible NOS activity as well as NO and immunoreactive nitrotyrosine, in the cerebral hemispheres were reduced with L-NA administration. The number of leukocytes in the plasma was unaffected by administration of L-NA. These findings suggest that cerebral ischemia-reperfusion causes increased production of reactive oxygen species in the cerebral hemispheres and that the production of peroxynitrite, and not superoxide, may be dependent upon the availability of NO.

title: Trends and future developments in the pharmacological treatment of acute ischaemic stroke.
abstract: Stroke stands as the third leading cause of death. It makes great demands on patients, who must not only survive the complications of the acute stages, but must cope then with the great physical and economic costs of long-term disabilities. Therefore, there is urgent need to establish generally useful regimens for the acute treatment of ischaemic stroke. Three treatment approaches are based upon pathophysiologic concepts derived from experimental work with focal cerebral ischaemia. These include pharmacologic strategies for arterial recanalisation, inhibition of inflammatory processes and neural protection. Focal cerebral ischaemia secondary to occlusion of a brain-supplying artery initiates neuronal and microvascular events, and the simultaneous processes of inflammation which further injure tissue. The use of plasminogen activators to mediate thrombus and lysis in the acute setting has been shown to be clinically beneficial. Further work with arterial reperfusion strategies is under way. Early clinical studies with polymorphonuclear leukocyte-dependent endothelial adhesion receptor antagonists are being completed, but a strategy has yet to emerge. A large effort examining the potential efficacy of agents which may stabilise or protect neurons from ischaemic injury has shown promise in experimental models, and has been translated into clinical trials. Experimental work, and limited clinical experience, have indicated that: (a) the time window for intervention is important in limiting ischaemic and inflammatory injury, and for reducing the risk of haemorrhagic transformation; (b) putative neuroprotective strategies may potentially elongate the time interval for treatment; and (c) limitations from the adverse effects of plasminogen activators and of agents which beneficially affect neuronal dysfunction during ischaemia must yet be overcome. This review surveys pharmacological approaches currently undergoing evaluation which provide the goal of establishing effective strategies for the treatment of patients with acute cerebral ischaemia.

It makes great demands on patients, who must not only survive the complications of the acute stages, but must cope then with the great physical and economic costs of long-term disabilities. Therefore, there is urgent need to establish generally useful regimens for the acute treatment of ischaemic stroke.

title: Influence of cerebral ischemia and post-ischemic reperfusion on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.
abstract: Unilateral ischemia in the right cerebral hemisphere of the rat was induced by ligation of the right common carotid artery coupled with controlled hemorrhage to produce hypotension (25 +/- 8 mm/Hg). Where indicated after 30 min of ischemia, the withdrawn blood was reinfused to restore arterial pressure to normal. Mitochondria isolated from the ipsilateral hemisphere after 30 min of ischemia showed significantly lower respiratory rates than the organelles isolated from the contralateral side. Oxidation of NAD(+)-linked substrates was more sensitive to inhibition in ischemia (30%) than was of ferrocytochrome c (12%), succinate oxidation being intermediate. The activities of membrane-bound dehydrogenases (both NADH and succinate-linked) were also significantly lowered. Ischemia did not affect the cytochrome content of mitochondria. Respiratory activity (NAD(+)-linked) of mitochondria isolated from the ipsilateral hemisphere was twice as sensitive to inhibition by fatty acid as was of preparations from the contralateral side. Mitochondria isolated from cerebral cortex after 90 min of post-ischemic reperfusion showed no significant improvement in the rate of substrate oxidation. Adenine nucleotide translocase activity and energy-dependent Ca2+ uptake, both of which decreased significantly in mitochondria isolated from the ischemic brain, showed little recovery, on reperfusion. These observations suggested the strong possibility that the deleterious effects of ischemia on mitochondrial respiratory function might be mediated by free fatty acids that are known to accumulate in large amounts in ischemic tissues. The pattern of inhibition of ATPase activity was consistent with this view.

title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors. RESULTS: p p p Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52,= 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58,= 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11,= 0.049). DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored.

title: Not all endothelium is equal: regional and sex-dependent roles of DDAH1 in regulating endothelial function.
abstract: En-/- En-/- fl/fl En-/- En-/- En-/- En-/- ex vivo PRMT DDAH PRMT1 DDAH Asymmetrical dimethylarginine (ADMA), an endogenous inhibitor of nitric oxide synthases (NOS), is primarily metabolized by dimethylarginine dimethylaminohydrolases (DDAH1 and 2). This study used endothelial-specific DDAH1 knockout (DDAH1) mice to test whether reduced endothelial DDAH1 activity impairs cerebral endothelial function and worsens outcomes after cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion. Using male and female, DDAH1and control (DDAH1) mice, we assessed vasoreactivity of middle cerebral (MCA), common carotid (CCA), and systemic arteries (thoracic aortae and first-order mesenteric arteries); and quantified CCA expression of genes associated with vascular smooth muscle (VSM) contractility. ADMA concentrations, and mRNA expression of protein arginine methyltransferases (), andwere quantified in human cerebral (hCMEC/D3) and aortic (HAEC) endothelial cells. Outcomes following transient MCA occlusion (tMCAo) were also evaluated in male mice. In male DDAH1mice, NO-dependent vasodilator responses in MCA and CCA were significantly impaired compared to controls, while responses in systemic arteries were unaffected. Vasoconstrictor responses were paradoxically reduced in CCA from male DDAH1mice in association with altered expression of genes involved in VSM contractility. In contrast to males, vasoreactivity was unaltered in MCA and CCA from female DDAH1mice. BothandmRNA expression were higher in hCMEC/D3 compared with HAEC cells, in association with no change in ADMA concentrations. Lastly, in male DDAH1mice, infarct volumes and functional outcomes post-tMCAo were comparable with controls. These findings underscore a role for endothelial DDAH1 in maintaining endothelial function in cerebral arteries from male but not female mice. However, endothelial DDAH1 does not influence stroke outcomes.

title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear. METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS). RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory. DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT. METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion.

title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke. METHODS: Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone. RESULTS: Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70). CONCLUSIONS: Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

title: Regulatory roles and molecular mechanisms of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification in ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) represents a prevalent internal epitranscriptomic modification of mRNA that influences post-transcriptional gene regulation. Clinically, ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury contributes to tissue damage in acute kidney injury, ischemic stroke, and myocardial infarction, particularly after blood flow is restored. METHODS: We searched Google Scholar, Web of Science, and PubMed for literature published through May 2026. The retrieval focused on articles detailing how m6A effector proteins-specifically writers, erasers, and readers-mediate I/R pathogenesis within hepatic, renal, cardiac, and cerebral tissues. RESULTS: m6A-associated regulation influences RNA metabolism during I/R injury. Context-dependent changes in m6A regulators and target transcripts are linked to oxidative stress, inflammatory cascades, and specific programmed cell death pathways, including ferroptosis and pyroptosis, across various organ systems. CONCLUSION: Profiling these organ-specific m6A molecular networks may inform future research on targeted epitranscriptomic interventions for IRI.

title: Intrinsic Redox-Responsive NIR-II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon-Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo.
abstract: 4 4 4 4 4 4 4 2 2 Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emitters well suited to long-term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface-installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long-term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox-regulated phonon-assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF:Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice-mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF@NaCeF:Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF:Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation-induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce-mediated quenching and restore NIR-II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF:Yb@NaLuF@NaCeF:Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible HO/glutathione responses, with second-scale activation, concentration-dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof-of-concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR-II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial.
abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. (Funded by Shenyang Science Tech Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657470).

title: Temporal trend and geographic variation in anticoagulation of patients hospitalized with acute pulmonary embolism: the RIETE registry 2013-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: A recent U.S. study of initial anticoagulation in adults with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring hospitalization found intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) use exceeded 50%. Guidelines, however, recommend low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) over UFH for most patients requiring parenteral anticoagulation. Use patterns in other geographic regions are unclear. METHODS: We analyzed data from RIETE, a prospective multinational registry of consecutive patients with venous thromboembolism. We included adults hospitalized for acute PE from 2013 through 2024 in 273 hospitals across 31 countries. We assessed temporal trend and regional variation in initial anticoagulation. Using multivariable regression, we identified variables independently associated with UFH. RESULTS: Among 36,210 adults, 83.2% received subcutaneous LMWH, 7.1% UFH, and 6.8% direct oral anticoagulants. LMWH use decreased slightly from 2013 to 2024 (85.8% to 79.2%; unadjusted), while UFH increased (8.9% to 10.4%). Wide geographic variation was observed in overall use of LMWH (37%--95%) and UFH (2%--39%). When adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates, increased weight, recent surgery, recent major bleeding, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, severe renal dysfunction, abnormal vital signs, and early reperfusion therapy were positively associated, whereas age >80 years, active cancer, chronic lung disease, prior ischemic stroke, and year were negatively associated with UFH. Compared with Spanish hospitals, hospitals in other European countries, the United States, and Asia were independently associated with UFH use. CONCLUSIONS: Results highlight opportunities for some geographic regions to align anticoagulation practices more closely with evidence-based guidelines recommending LMWH as the preferred parenteral agent in most patients with PE requiring hospitalization.

title: ISLES'24: Final stroke infarct prediction with multimodal imaging and clinical data. Where do we stand?
abstract: Accurate estimation of brain infarction (i.e., irreversibly damaged tissue) is critical for guiding treatment decisions in acute ischemic stroke. Reliable infarct prediction informs key clinical interventions, including the need for patient transfer to comprehensive stroke centers, the potential benefit of additional reperfusion attempts during mechanical thrombectomy, decisions regarding secondary neuroprotective treatments, and, ultimately, prognosis of clinical outcomes. This work introduces the Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation (ISLES) 2024 challenge, which focuses on the prediction of final infarct volumes from pre-interventional acute stroke imaging and clinical data. ISLES'24 provides a comprehensive, multimodal setting where participants can leverage all clinically and practically available data - including full acute CT imaging, sub-acute follow-up MRI, and structured clinical information - across a train set of N=150 cases. On the hidden test set (N=98), the top-performing model, a multimodal nnU-Net-based architecture, achieved a Dice score of 0.285 ± 0.213 and an absolute volume difference of 21.2 ± 37.2 mL, underlining the significant challenges posed by this task and the need for further advances in multimodal learning. This overview of the ISLES'24 challenge offers two primary contributions: first, it provides a standardized, clinically realistic benchmark for post-treatment infarct prediction, built on a comprehensive, open, and multimodal longitudinal stroke imaging dataset; second, it provides insights into the strengths and limitations of current algorithms and delineates key research directions to guide the development of next-generation infarct prediction models.

title: Inhibition of Ptbp1 in microglia alleviates neuroinflammation by the Cbx5-Ifitm3 axis.
abstract: Polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1 (Ptbp1) is a member of the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins that govern numerous aspects of the messenger RNA life cycle, including splicing, stability, and translation. This study investigated its role in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) with a focus on microglia. A model of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion in mice and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) model in mouse BV2 cells were used. Ptbp1 was significantly upregulated in microglia following CIRI. Inhibition of Ptbp1 attenuated the inflammatory response in BV2 cells and reduced damage to co-cultured neurons under OGD/R conditions; it also reduced tissue inflammation, mitigated brain tissue damage, and improved neurological function on days 1, 3 and 7 after reperfusion in vivo. Mechanistically, Ptbp1 destabilized chromobox protein homolog 5 (Cbx5), thereby attenuating Cbx5/Suv39h1-mediated H3K9me3 enrichment and transcriptional repression at the interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 (Ifitm3) promoter, promoting Ifitm3 expression and enhancing Tlr4/p65 signaling. The regulation of Cbx5 mRNA stability by Ptbp1 and the inhibitory effect of Cbx5 on Ifitm3 were also confirmed in IMG cells. The present findings suggest that Ptbp1 reduces the stability of Cbx5 mRNA, thereby attenuating Cbx5/Suv39h1-mediated transcriptional repression of Ifitm3, enhancing Tlr4/p65 signaling and the inflammatory response, and exacerbating neuronal damage and CIRI.

title: Reperfusion enhances treg-mediated neuroprotection and IL-10 signaling in a mouse model of large vessel occlusion.
abstract: The indications for acute reperfusion therapies in ischemic stroke have recently expanded to include patients with large ischemic cores, highlighting an urgent need for targeted neurotherapeutics that maximize tissue salvage. Preclinical studies suggest that early reperfusion, even after extensive ischemic injury, can mitigate infarct expansion and activate endogenous regenerative pathways, though the precise mechanisms driving these therapeutic benefits remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying successful reperfusion to identify novel avenues for immunotherapy. Using transient (t-MCAO) and permanent (p-MCAO) middle cerebral artery occlusion mouse models, we comprehensively analyzed central and peripheral immune cell dynamics. Our analysis revealed that successful reperfusion significantly elevates regulatory T cell (Treg) proportions compared to non-reperfused controls. Across experimental groups, higher interleukin-10 (IL-10) levels generally accompanied greater Treg abundance and better motor performance. Targeted intra-arterial delivery of IL-10 at the exact time of reperfusion directly attenuated cerebral injury and improved neurological outcomes. These findings suggest that amplifying anti-inflammatory signaling post-reperfusion may provide neuroprotection, positioning intra-arterial IL-10 as a potential adjunctive neurotherapeutic strategy to enhance the efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy.

In this study, we investigated the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying successful reperfusion to identify novel avenues for immunotherapy.

title: Blocking FOXO4 confers neuroprotection against oxidative stress and ischemia-reperfusion caused neuronal injury.
abstract: Previous studies suggest that FOXO4 facilitates inflammation and oxidative stress in non-brain tissues under stress or disease conditions, indicating that downregulation of FOXO4 may be neuroprotective in ischemia-reperfusion-induced brain injury. This possibility has not been tested in a cerebral ischemia-reperfusion context, however. Here, we exposed FOXO4 knockout (KO) primary neuronal cultures to oxidative stress or oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), and subjected KO mice to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). We also used a structure-based approach combined with cell-based assays to identify a FOXO4 inhibitor and evaluated its effects in tMCAO-treated wild-type (WT) mice. Our results showed that FOXO4 KO reduced oxidative stress- and OGD-induced neuronal death, attenuated tMCAO-induced infarct volume, improved animal survival, decreased neurological deficits, and enhanced functional recovery compared with WT cells or mice. Immunohistochemical staining and Western blot analyses further indicated reduced neuroinflammation in the KO brain. The identified FOXO4 inhibitor Actinomycin D suppressed FOXO4 activity at a low dose, reduced brain injury, and improved functional recovery in WT mice following tMCAO. Together, these findings indicate that FOXO4 is a potential therapeutic target and that suppression of its activity may promote neuronal survival after ischemic stroke-induced brain injury.

title: Spatiotemporal Core-Shell Microspheres Enable Hydrogen-Mediated Redox Priming and Kartogenin-Induced Cartilage Regeneration for Osteoarthritis Bio-Rescue.
abstract: 2 2 The effective management of osteoarthritis (OA) remains a formidable clinical challenge due to a chronically inflamed joint microenvironment and the limited self-regenerative capacity of articular cartilage. To address these barriers, we developed an ultrasound-responsive core-shell microsphere platform engineered via a customized microfluidic capillary device. This system features a kartogenin (KGN)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) core encapsulated within a sodium alginate shell enriched with tin disulfide (SnS) nanosheets (SSN). Following intra-articular injection, non-invasive ultrasound stimulation triggers the localized SSN to generate low-concentration hydrogen gas (H). This in situ Hgeneration rapidly scavenges excess reactive oxygen species to restore redox homeostasis, thereby mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction and preserving chondrocyte viability. Consequently, this targeted antioxidative intervention suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion and polarizes synovial macrophages toward a pro-regenerative M2 phenotype. Within this newly stabilized microenvironment, the sustained release of KGN from the PLGA core successfully reverses extracellular matrix metabolic imbalances to promote cartilage repair. In a rat model of OA, this dual-functional, spatiotemporally controlled platform profoundly halted joint degeneration and preserved histological cartilage integrity. Collectively, this ultrasound-triggered core-shell microsphere system offers a highly promising, disease-modifying strategy for comprehensive OA therapy.

title: Scutellarin as a multi-target neuroprotective agent: Analytical evidence, pharmacokinetic insights and translational strategies across neurodegenerative disorders.
abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are a leading cause of disability and mortality globally, but effective disease-modifying therapeutic strategies are still largely unavailable. Scutellarin is a flavonoid glycoside extracted from Erigeron breviscapus (Vant.) Hand-Mazz. It has been widely studied in preclinical models of neurodegenerative disorders. In this study, we performed a systematic review of preclinical animal studies. We combined comprehensive database retrieval with quantitative synthesis of eligible outcomes. The pooled results demonstrated that scutellarin significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume and improved neurological deficit scores in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion models. It also ameliorated learning and memory impairments in experimental Alzheimer's disease (AD) models. Consistent neuroprotective effects were also found in models of depression, anxiety, Parkinson's disease, etc. Mechanistic analysis indicated that scutellarin produces multi-level neuroprotective effects. It acts by reducing oxidative stress, inhibiting neuroinflammation, suppressing apoptosis, stabilizing the neurovascular unit and other neurobiological processes. This review first evaluated the preclinical efficacy of scutellarin through systematic review and meta-analysis. It then integrated cross-disease mechanisms with network pharmacology, reverse virtual screening and molecular docking to identify computationally predicted targets. Although scutellarin shows promising preclinical effects, its clinical translation faces major limitations. These limitations include low oral bioavailability, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and insufficient data on brain exposure. Overall, scutellarin is a multi-target neuroprotective candidate. Future studies should focus on target validation, exposure-response modeling, delivery optimization and clinically relevant translational evaluation.

title: An immediate reperfusion sign might increase the likelihood of favourable outcomes in patients with intracranial atherosclerotic disease-related stroke who received stent-retriever-based thrombectomy.
abstract: OBJECTS: To investigate the relationship between the presence of an "immediate reperfusion sign (IRS)" during retrievable stent-based thrombectomy and clinical outcomes in patients with large vessel-occluded acute ischaemic stroke related to intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) treated with stent retrievers. METHODS: Consecutive ICAD-LVO stroke patients who were treated with stent retrievers and whose imaging records were available for the assessment of the IRS were included. The sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes were calculated. Univariate analysis and partial correlation analysis were also performed. RESULTS: Eighty-two ICAD-LVO patients were identified from 421 endovascularly treated AIS patients from 2015 to 2024. Fifty-four of them were ultimately included in the analysis, and an IRS was observed in 41 of these patients (75.9%). Favourable outcomes were significantly more frequent in the IRS (+) group (51.2% versus 7.7%, p=0.005). The sensitivity of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes was 95.5% (21/22), the specificity was 37.5% (12/32), the positive predictive value was 51.2% (21/41), and the negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.3% (12/13). Additionally, the presence of an IRS, as well as age, baseline NIHSS score and successful final reperfusion, was significantly different between the favourable and unfavourable groups. Partial correlation analysis revealed a moderate correlation (r=0.412; p=0.002) between the comprehensive reperfusion score (in which the presence of an IRS and successful final reperfusion was counted as 1 point) and favourable outcomes. CONCLUSION: In our respective cohort of patients, the presence of an IRS during stent-retriever-based thrombectomy appeared to indicate a higher rate of first-pass-effect and a 3-month favourable outcome in acute LVO stroke patients with ICAD.

METHODS: Consecutive ICAD-LVO stroke patients who were treated with stent retrievers and whose imaging records were available for the assessment of the IRS were included. The sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes were calculated.

title: Residual SYNTAX score and optical coherence tomography-derived thin-cap fibroatheroma in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: an exploratory descriptive pilot study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. While percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the definitive reperfusion strategy, residual disease burden and plaque vulnerability both influence clinical recovery. The residual SYNTAX score (rSS) quantifies untreated macroscopic coronary artery disease, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) resolves microscopic plaque architecture, notably thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA). This pilot study explored the descriptive characteristics and short-term outcomes associated with combining rSS and OCT-derived TCFA in a highly selected STEMI cohort. METHODS: ≤ ≤ ≤ This retrospective observational pilot study included 30 patients with STEMI who underwent primary PCI and culprit lesion OCT evaluation at a tertiary care center. Patients were stratified into four groups according to the presence of culprit TCFA and the post-PCI rSS threshold (4 vs. > 4): group 0 (TCFA absent, rSS > 4), group 1 (TCFA absent, rSS4), group 2 (TCFA present, rSS > 4), and group 3 (TCFA present, rSS4). The primary clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE)-a composite of all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularization, heart failure hospitalisation, and ischemic stroke-assessed over 3 months. RESULTS: The cohort (mean age, 54.5 ± 10.1 years; 83.3% male, 40% with diabetes mellitus) had a 53.3% prevalence (16 of 30) of culprit lesion TCFA. Complete or reasonable revascularization (rSS ≤ 4) was achieved in 12 patients (40.0%). The overall cumulative 3-month MACE rate was 30.0% (9 of 30). MACE occurred in 1 of 7 patients (14.3%) in group 0, 1 of 7 (14.3%) in group 1, 4 of 11 (36.4%) in group 2, and 3 of 5 (60.0%) in group 3 (Fisher exact test, P = 0.23; log-rank P = 0.38). Patients with TCFA accounted for 7 of 9 clinical events (77.8%). Given the small subgroup sizes (n < 12), multivariable predictive risk modeling was not performed. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory pilot cohort of STEMI patients undergoing PCI, the presence of OCT-derived TCFA was descriptively associated with higher short-term adverse event rates across both complete and incomplete revascularization strata. Given the small sample size and clear indication bias, these findings are strictly hypothesis-generating and support the need for adequately powered prospective registries to evaluate dual anatomical-biological risk stratification.

The residual SYNTAX score (rSS) quantifies untreated macroscopic coronary artery disease, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) resolves microscopic plaque architecture, notably thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA).

title: Cavitation jet treatment-assisted glycosylation of hemp seed protein: Structural regulation and emulsion stability.
abstract: 2 This study employed cavitation jet treatment to facilitate the effective glycosylation of hemp seed protein (HSP) with chitosan (CS). Initially, the treatment disrupted intra- and inter-molecular hydrogen bonds, inducing HSP structural unfolding. This critical conformational transition exposed internal reactive amino groups, enabling them to interact with CS carbonyl groups and achieving a maximum grafting degree of 34.54%. Consequently, the secondary structure of HSP was reorganized from an ordered state into a more relaxed, disordered configuration. The subsequent covalent attachment of hydrophilic CS chains effectively shielded exposed hydrophobic regions, significantly enhancing the complex's water affinity. Therefore, overall functional performances were markedly improved: solution properties were enhanced through increased solubility and decreased turbidity, while emulsion performance was optimized, evidenced by a superior EAI (55.89 m/g), an extended ESI (84.35 min), and improved apparent viscosity and viscoelasticity. This approach provides a practical strategy for the high-value utilization of hemp by-products.

Initially, the treatment disrupted intra- and inter-molecular hydrogen bonds, inducing HSP structural unfolding. This critical conformational transition exposed internal reactive amino groups, enabling them to interact with CS carbonyl groups and achieving a maximum grafting degree of 34.54%.

title: False patency, true occlusion: perfusion imaging and dual stent-retriever thrombectomy for a calcified carotid terminus embolus.
abstract: Calcified cerebral emboli are an uncommon cause of acute ischemic stroke and may produce a false-patency sign on computed tomography angiography because their high attenuation can mimic intravascular contrast material. We report the case of a 77-year-old woman who presented with a wake-up stroke approximately 14 hours after she was last known well, with right hemiplegia and global aphasia. Noncontrast computed tomography showed a markedly hyperattenuating intraluminal focus at the left carotid terminus and proximal M1 segment, suggesting a calcified cerebral embolus. Computed tomography angiography appeared to show severe stenosis with residual luminal patency, whereas computed tomography perfusion demonstrated extensive hypoperfusion involving the left middle cerebral artery and bilateral anterior cerebral artery territories. Because the severe neurologic deficit and perfusion abnormality were discordant with the apparent patency on computed tomography angiography, cerebral angiography was performed. Digital subtraction angiography demonstrated complete occlusion of the left M1 origin and near-complete occlusion of the left A1 segment; the right A1 segment was congenitally hypoplastic. A rigid calcified embolus spanning the carotid-terminus bifurcation was retrieved using a balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent technique under proximal flow arrest, achieving complete reperfusion in a single pass. Histopathologic examination confirmed calcified embolic material. This case highlights the value of multimodal imaging and confirmatory angiography when clinical and imaging findings are discordant. In this patient, balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent retrieval was a tailored and feasible strategy; however, a single case cannot establish its superiority over other thrombectomy approaches.

title: Exosomes in remote ischemic preconditioning-mediated organ protection: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
abstract: Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is an endogenous protective strategy that confers resistance against sustained ischemia-reperfusion injury in distant organs. RIPC induces protective responses through complex neuronal, humoral, and systemic signaling pathways. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes may serve as important mediators of humoral inter-organ communication during RIPC. Exosomes are small extracellular vesicles released by donor cells that transport biologically active molecules, including lipids, proteins, messenger RNAs, and microRNAs, to recipient cells, thereby modulating cellular responses to injury. Emerging evidence indicates that RIPC-associated exosomes and their molecular cargo contribute to protection against ischemia-reperfusion injury in organs such as the heart, brain, kidney, and spinal cord. Several exosomal molecules, including miRNAs, HSP90, HIF-1α, and NOX2, have been implicated in the regulation of cellular pathways associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, mitochondrial function, and tissue survival. In particular, alterations in exosomal miRNAs and protein and metabolite profiles following RIPC suggest that exosomes may participate in the transmission of protective signals from remote ischemic tissues to target organs. The therapeutic potential of exosomes is further supported by their ability to transport multiple bioactive molecules and their potential application as biomarkers or delivery vehicles for therapeutic cargo. However, the specific exosomal components responsible for RIPC-mediated protection and their causal contribution to inter-organ signaling remain to be fully established. Therefore, the present review summarizes the emerging evidence on the role of exosomes in RIPC-mediated organ protection, with particular emphasis on cardiovascular and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, the molecular cargo involved, underlying protective mechanisms, and their potential therapeutic and translational applications.

RIPC induces protective responses through complex neuronal, humoral, and systemic signaling pathways. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes may serve as important mediators of humoral inter-organ communication during RIPC.

title: β-Asarone Alleviates Post-stroke Neuroinflammation and Improves Mitochondrial Quality Via the BNIP3/BNIP3L-dependent Mitophagy Pathway.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, with mitophagy playing a central role in post-stroke neurological dysfunction. β-Asarone, a major bioactive component derived from the traditional herb Acorus tatarinowii, possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties. However, whether β-asarone ameliorates IS by regulating mitophagy and its underlying mechanisms remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether β-asarone exerts neuroprotective effects against IS by modulating BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy. A middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) cell model were established. Neuroprotective effects were evaluated using neurological behavioral scores, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining, hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining, and Nissl staining. Mitochondrial function was assessed by measuring reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). Mitophagy was observed via transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and fluorescence microscopy. Western blot (WB) analysis was performed to detect BNIP3/BNIP3L pathway proteins. Results showed that β-asarone enhanced mitophagy, improved mitochondrial function, and alleviated post-stroke neuroinflammation. Conversely, the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA) impaired mitophagic function, exacerbating ischemia-induced brain injury and inflammation, while β-asarone treatment reversed these detrimental effects. In summary, β-asarone mitigates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury after IS, at least partly through promoting BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy, highlighting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for IS.

However, whether β-asarone ameliorates IS by regulating mitophagy and its underlying mechanisms remains unclear.

title: Inhibition of miR-140-5p attenuates OGD/R-induced neuronal injury by targeting IL1RAPL1.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to neuronal damage and long-term neurological dysfunction after stroke. Our previous studies demonstrated that miR-140-5p expression is markedly upregulated following cerebral ischemia and that in vivo overexpression of miR-140-5p exacerbates cognitive impairment, suppresses neurogenesis, and promotes neuronal death in ischemic mouse models; however, its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the downstream molecular targets of miR-140-5p and to elucidate the mechanisms by which miR-140-5p regulates neuronal injury after I/R. METHODS: We established an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in primary cortical neurons and assessed viability via Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8). miR-140-5p expression after OGD/R was examined, and loss-of-function experiments evaluated the effects of miR-140-5p inhibition. Synaptic integrity was assessed by immunofluorescence, and inflammatory cytokines by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Proteomic analysis identified potential downstream targets, which were validated via Western blotting and dual-luciferase reporter assays. RESULTS: Il1rapl1 We found that miR-140-5p expression was significantly upregulated in mouse cortical neurons after OGD/R. Functional inhibition of miR-140-5p markedly enhanced neuronal survival, promoted synaptic remodeling, and attenuated inflammatory responses following OGD/R injury. Mechanistically, miR-140-5p was shown to directly targetand modulate downstream c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) signaling, thereby regulating neuronal viability, inflammation, and synaptic plasticity under ischemia-reperfusion conditions. CONCLUSION: This study reveals a novel miR-140-5p-mediated regulatory mechanism in neuronal injury following cerebral ischemia-reperfusion and suggests a potential therapeutic target for ischemic brain injury.

title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression. RESULTS: p p p p Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624). CONCLUSIONS: Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables.

title: Metal-based hydrogen-generating therapeutic systems: From reactive chemistry to route-specific exposure and translational design.
abstract: 2 2 2 2 2 2 Molecular hydrogen (H) has shown broad therapeutic relevance in oxidative injury, inflammation, metabolic dysfunction and tissue repair, yet its clinical translation remains limited by rapid diffusion, poor retention and a poorly defined dose-exposure relationship. Metal-based H-generating systems offer an engineering strategy to produce or release Hat pathological sites or material-tissue interfaces, where local exposure can be shaped by material design. This review reframes these platforms as material-formulation-route-indication systems rather than isolated material classes. The field now extends from classical metal hydrides to broader metal-containing platforms that generate or release Hthrough hydrolysis, corrosion, electrochemical reactions or hydrogen storage-mediated release. Their therapeutic behavior is governed by route-specific exposure fields shaped by Hrelease, accompanying reaction chemistry, formulation-defined compartments and tissue environments. Accordingly, route-oriented evaluation is essential because the same reactive core can produce distinct exposure profiles, safety boundaries and translational requirements across oral, local, vascular and implantable contexts. Mechanistically, H-dependent redox and cytoprotective biology provides an important entry point, but therapeutic outcomes arise from a multi-effector local chemical milieu involving metal-derived species, coupled physicochemical changes and, in some platforms, external activation. Translational development therefore requires controlled materials engineering, route-specific exposure metrics, mechanism-matched validation, a PK/PD-like exposure-response framework adapted for reactive material systems and manufacturing strategies aligned with chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) requirements. The field should advance toward route-specific, exposure-defined and mechanism-validated local reaction therapy.
englishSummary: 2 2 2 2 2 2 Molecular hydrogen (H) has shown broad therapeutic relevance in oxidative injury, inflammation, metabolic dysfunction and tissue repair, yet its clinical translation remains limited by rapid diffusion, poor retention and a poorly defined dose-exposure relationship. Metal-based H-generating systems offer an engineering strategy to produce or release Hat pathological sites or material-tissue interfaces, where local exposure can be shaped by material design. This review reframes these platforms as material-formulation-route-indication systems rather than isolated material classes.

title: Diagnostic delay and predictors of true stroke among patients with suspected in-hospital stroke: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Timely diagnosis is essential for acute treatment of in-hospital stroke. We aimed to investigate factors associated with diagnostic delay and clinical predictors of true stroke among patients with suspected in-hospital stroke. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we screened head computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging orders between Jan 2023 and Jan 2026 for patients hospitalized outside the Departments of Neurology and Neurosurgery who developed new neurological symptoms within 24 h of symptom onset or last known well and were clinically suspected of having in-hospital stroke. Multivariable analyses were performed to identify factors associated with diagnostic delay and true stroke. RESULTS: A total of 183 patients (110 men, median age 77 years) were included. Median time from last known well to imaging-based final diagnosis was 292 min. Overall, 77 patients (42.1%) had true stroke, including 70 ischemic strokes, 5 intracerebral hemorrhages, and 2 subarachnoid hemorrhages. Wake-up symptom onset [Exp (β) 3.34, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.61-4.28] and initial medical emergency team activation [Exp (β) 0.71, 95% CI 0.56-0.91] were associated with diagnostic delay. Persistent neurological symptoms [odds ratio (OR) 1.44, 95% CI 1.24-1.68] and FAST-positive symptoms (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.12-1.46) were associated with true stroke. Among the 70 patients with ischemic stroke, 17 (24.3%) underwent reperfusion therapy. CONCLUSION: Wake-up symptom onset and medical emergency team activation were associated with diagnostic delay, whereas persistent and FAST-positive symptoms were associated with true stroke. These findings may facilitate earlier recognition and improve triaging patients with suspected in-hospital stroke.

title: Endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction in the setting of mechanical thrombectomy: a conceptual link between cardiometabolic vulnerability and microvascular reperfusion failure.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has made macrovessel reopening achievable in acute ischemic stroke, but angiographic success does not ensure effective tissue-level reperfusion or microvascular oxygen delivery. This narrative review examines endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction as a plausible blood-facing interface that may connect pre-existing cardiometabolic vulnerability with post-thrombectomy microvascular dysfunction. Targeted English-language literature from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar through 30 April 2026 was synthesized, with emphasis on MT, impaired microvascular reperfusion (IMR), no-reflow, blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular-unit (NVU) biology, glycocalyx-related biomarkers, cardiometabolic risk, perfusion imaging, and microcirculatory rescue. The evidence base is heterogeneous and is explicitly separated into direct human MT/LVO evidence, indirect human biomarker or imaging evidence, experimental cerebral evidence, non-cerebral/cross-disease vascular evidence, and hypothesis-generating mechanistic inference. Ischemic priming, abrupt reperfusion, oxidative and inflammatory stress, complement activation, metabolic stress, distal embolization, device-endothelial trauma, and host vulnerability may converge on the luminal endothelial surface. Glycocalyx dysfunction may amplify leukocyte adhesion and capillary plugging, platelet adhesion and microthrombosis, impaired mechanosensing and nitric-oxide signaling, BBB destabilization, and heterogeneous capillary flow; however, direct causal proof in human MT is lacking. Circulating syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan are therefore best interpreted as time- and compartment-dependent systemic signals rather than direct readouts of the cerebral glycocalyx. Post-EVT microcirculatory rescue trials show that downstream perfusion may remain therapeutically actionable, but they do not demonstrate glycocalyx repair as the operative mechanism. A practical translational strategy is to combine serial, compartment-annotated biomarkers with prespecified early perfusion/barrier imaging and tissue endpoints, while explicitly modeling cardiometabolic vulnerability and competing microvascular mechanisms. The glycocalyx framework should therefore be considered a testable network hypothesis rather than an established primary cause of post-thrombectomy no-reflow or futile recanalization.

title: Acute creatine-guanidinoacetate supplementation improves regional brain oxygenation following sleep deprivation: A randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Background: Aim: Methods: Summary: P d P d P P P 2 2 2 Sleep deprivation impairs cognitive performance and may alter regional cerebral oxygenation. Nutritional strategies that preserve brain oxygenation could help mitigate these adverse effects.To compare the acute effects of creatine-guanidinoacetate (GAA), molecular hydrogen inhalation, caffeine, and placebo on regional brain oxygenation and attention-related performance following sleep deprivation.Twenty-two healthy young adults completed a 24-hour sleep deprivation protocol and were randomly assigned to receive creatine-GAA, molecular hydrogen inhalation, caffeine, or placebo. Brain oxygenation was assessed using functional near-infrared spectroscopy over the frontal, temporal, and occipital cortices during a modified attention network test. Alertness, executive control, orienting, reaction time, and accuracy were also evaluated.Creatine-GAA significantly increased frontal oxygen saturation (50.8% ± 4.1% to 61.0% ± 5.9%, = 0.01; Cohen's = 2.00) and temporal oxygen saturation (63.1% ± 4.8% to 70.2% ± 2.6%, = 0.01; Cohen's = 1.83). Significant time-by-treatment interactions were observed for frontal oxygen saturation ( = 0.043; ηp = 0.331), temporal oxygen saturation ( = 0.021; ηp = 0.428), and occipital total hemoglobin ( = 0.022; ηp = 0.405). No significant between-group differences were observed in attention-related outcomes. Acute creatine-GAA supplementation improved regional brain oxygenation following sleep deprivation, particularly in the frontal and temporal cortices, without measurable improvements in attention-related performance. These preliminary findings support further investigation of creatine-based nutritional strategies in larger randomized controlled trials.

title: Diabetes-Associated Fibrin Enrichment in Cerebral Thrombi and Its Procedural Implications for Mechanical Thrombectomy.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p Diabetes is associated with altered fibrin biology, but its relationship with fibrin content in cerebral thrombi and the procedural relevance of this relationship during mechanical thrombectomy remain unclear. We investigated the association between diabetes and fibrin content in thrombectomy-retrieved cerebral thrombi and whether diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content mediated procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy.We retrospectively analyzed patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had retrieved thrombi available for histological analysis. Red blood cell, platelet, and fibrin contents were quantified immunohistochemically. The association between diabetes and fibrin content was evaluated using multivariable linear regression, with complementary sensitivity analyses based on intravenous tissue-type plasminogen activator administration and atrial fibrillation status. Mediation analyses were performed to estimate the indirect effects of diabetes on procedural outcomes through diabetes-associated changes in fibrin content.Among 312 patients, 98 (31.4%) had diabetes. Patients with diabetes had greater fibrin content than those without diabetes (median, 37.0% [interquartile range, 26.4-52.9] vs. 30.9% [17.7-45.0];= 0.004), whereas red blood cell and platelet contents did not differ significantly between the groups. Diabetes remained associated with greater fibrin content in the primary adjusted analysis (β = +6.68 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.19-11.18;= 0.004), and the association persisted after additional conditioning on initial glucose and in sensitivity analyses. Among patients with diabetes, neither HbA1c nor initial glucose was associated with fibrin content. Mediation analyses did not identify a detectable indirect effect of diabetes through fibrin content on successful reperfusion, complete reperfusion, first-pass effect, number of passes, or the requirement for ≥3 passes.Diabetes was independently associated with greater fibrin content in cerebral thrombi retrieved during mechanical thrombectomy, supporting the presence of a diabetes-associated fibrin-enriched thrombus phenotype. However, no detectable indirect effect of diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content on the examined procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy was identified. These findings suggest that although diabetes is associated with a distinct quantitative change in cerebral thrombus composition, a corresponding procedural consequence was not detectable in the present study.

title: Microglial Ring1 enhances post-phagocytic myelin debris processing: Attenuation of cognitive dysfunction after hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion induces myelin injury, resulting in cognitive impairment. Efficient clearance of myelin debris is important for neural repair. The E3 ubiquitin ligase Ring1 (RING finger protein 1) participates in ubiquitin signaling and gene expression regulation, However, whether Ring1 ameliorates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury-induced cognitive impairment by promoting microglial post-phagocytic myelin debris processing remains unknown. In this study, we employed a hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion model, a hippocampal myelin debris injection model, and an in vitro microglia-myelin debris co-culture model to simulate cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, and combined these models with proteomic and transcriptomic analyses and Ring1 gain- and loss-of-function approaches. Hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion induced hippocampal myelin injury and cognitive dysfunction, while hippocampal administration of myelin debris further impaired cognition. Transcriptomic analysis identified Ring1 as a candidate regulator associated with postphagocytic myelin debris processing. Ring1 overexpression alleviated cognitive deficits and hippocampal myelin injury and restored mitochondrial DNA-encoded gene expression and adenosine triphosphate levels after hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion. In contrast, Ring1 knockdown in the microglia-myelin debris co-culture model reduced mitochondrial DNAencoded gene expression and adenosine triphosphate levels and delayed post-phagocytic myelin debris processing. Mechanistically, Ring1 interacted with mitochondrial transcription factor B2, with K27-linked ubiquitin signals detected in Ring1- and mitochondrial transcription factor B2-containing immunocomplexes. Ring1 depletion reduced mitochondrial transcription factor B2-associated K27-linked ubiquitin signaling, mitochondrial DNA-encoded gene expression, adenosine triphosphate levels, and post-phagocytic myelin debris processing. Collectively, our findings suggest that Ring1 attenuates hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion-related cognitive impairment by promoting microglial post-phagocytic myelin debris processing through mitochondrial transcription factor B2-associated K27-linked ubiquitin signaling and mitochondrial regulation.

title: Factors associated with in-hospital mortality after stroke at a tertiary hospital in Angola.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Most Angolan patients with stroke reach hospital beyond the thrombolysis window, and many deaths occur within 72 h of admission. We investigated routinely recorded variables associated with in-hospital mortality at Hospital do Prenda. METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study at Hospital do Prenda, a public tertiary hospital in Luanda, from January 2023 to December 2025. The unit of analysis was the hospitalisation episode; four episodes ending in transfer were excluded. Hypertension and type 2 diabetes were extracted from free-text fields using predefined string rules. Univariable analyses used Pearson chi-square, crude odds ratios (OR; 95% CI), and Mann-Whitney tests. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, year, stroke subtype, recorded comorbidities, and head-CT status. Given the low events-per-variable ratio (~7) and poor calibration in some models, adjusted estimates were considered exploratory associations rather than independent prognostic effects. RESULTS: p p p p Among 479 episodes, 75 patients died (15.7%; 95% CI 12.7-19.2). Median age was 58.5 years among decedents versus 52.0 among survivors ( = 0.049). Median length of stay was 3 versus 6 days ( < 0.0001), reflecting early mortality rather than a prognostic exposure. Mortality increased from 6.7% at age 45-54 years to 28.0% at ≥75 years and remained graded after adjustment (≥75 years: adjusted OR 5.92, 95% CI 2.28-15.38; = 0.0003). Mortality among patients <45 years was also elevated (17.2%; adjusted OR 2.97, 95% CI 1.28-6.87), predominantly among haemorrhagic strokes (22.2% versus 10.8% for ischaemic stroke; age-by-subtype interaction = 0.0009). Sex, year, stroke subtype, recorded hypertension, and diabetes were not associated with mortality. Absence of head CT showed higher crude mortality (30.0% versus 15.0%; OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.90-6.52). Recorded hypertension prevalence was only 19.8%, indicating substantial under-ascertainment. CONCLUSION: Older age was the strongest admission-available correlate of in-hospital mortality, while elevated mortality among younger patients was concentrated in haemorrhagic stroke. Under-ascertainment limits interpretation of comorbidities. Absence of stroke-severity, functional-status, ICU, ventilation, and reperfusion data further limits causal or independent prognostic inference.

We investigated routinely recorded variables associated with in-hospital mortality at Hospital do Prenda. METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study at Hospital do Prenda, a public tertiary hospital in Luanda, from January 2023 to December 2025.

title: The inhibitory effect of gadolinium-conjugated diflunisal on platelet function through regulating outside-in signaling of αIIbβ3 integrin.
abstract: 2 2 3 2+ In vivo The gadolinium-conjugated diflunisal derivative ETN102 has previously been shown to suppress cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) levels, reduce glial activation, and attenuate neuronal damage associated with stroke. In the present study, we investigated whether ETN102 modulates platelet aggregation and activation. ETN102 selectively inhibited thrombin-induced platelet aggregation while sparing platelet responses to other agonists, including collagen, adenosine diphosphate (ADP), and U46619. ETN102 also reduced adenosine triphosphate (ATP) secretion under aggregating conditions without altering thromboxane B(TXB) generation, suggesting that its antiplatelet effect is independent of the COX-1-dependent thromboxane signaling. Flow cytometric and biochemical analyses further demonstrated that ETN102 suppressed thrombin-induced αIIbβ3 integrin activation, platelet spreading, clot retraction, and the phosphorylation of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) and proline-rich tyrosine kinase 2 (Pyk2), without affecting granule secretion, intracellular Camobilization, or phosphorylation of Syk, PI3K, and AKT signaling molecules., ETN102 significantly prolonged carotid artery occlusion time in a ferric chloride (FeCl)-induced thrombosis model and increased tail bleeding time and hemoglobin content. In addition, ETN102 reduced infarct volume and improved neuronal survival markers in a murine model of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury. These findings demonstrate that ETN102 is a thrombin-context selective modulator of platelet integrin αIIbβ3 outside-in signaling, with antithrombotic and neuroprotective potential.

title: Novel acylation modifications in cerebrovascular disease: Molecular mechanisms, crosstalk and therapeutic potential.
abstract: Secondary injury in cerebrovascular disease involves energy failure, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Novel lysine acylations, including lactylation, succinylation, beta-hydroxybutyrylation and crotonylation, have emerged as interfaces through which metabolic changes in lactate, succinate, ketone bodies and short-chain acyl-CoA species are translated into transcriptional regulation and altered protein function. This review organizes the evidence according to a framework that links metabolic donors, writer and eraser enzymes, modification sites, cell types and disease stages. We distinguish relatively developed experimental evidence in acute ischemic stroke and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury from limited findings in haemorrhage and predominantly exploratory evidence in chronic hypoperfusion and vascular cognitive impairment. Proteomic studies have identified 1003 lactylation sites across 469 proteins in rats subjected to cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, although most sites have not undergone causal validation. Comparatively strong evidence has accumulated for sites or regulatory axes involving MeCP2, SOD2, NEK7, ACSL4, PLBD1 and ZO-1. Collectively, current findings indicate that the effects of a given acylation cannot be inferred from its global abundance because they depend on substrate function, cellular origin and the therapeutic window. Major limitations include insufficient site-specific causal evidence, difficulty in directly quantifying crosstalk among post-translational modifications, poor correspondence between animal models and clinical heterogeneity and the absence of effective delivery systems and pharmacodynamic biomarkers. Future studies should integrate spatiotemporally resolved multi-omics, endogenous site editing, cell-specific models, measurable target engagement and independent clinical cohorts to evaluate whether selected acylation sites can progress from experimental candidates to independently validated clinical markers or intervention targets.

title: Electroacupuncture Ameliorating Cerebral I/R-Induced Inflammatory Response through the TLR/TRAF6/NF-κB Pathway.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The inflammatory response plays a crucial role in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and may offer a new therapeutic approach for stroke. Electroacupuncture has shown potential in treating cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury. METHODOLOGY: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to four groups: the sham group, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) group, sham electroacupuncture (SEA) group, and electroacupuncture (EA) group. The SEA and EA groups received 30 min of treatment after 60 min of ischemia. Body weight was measured before and 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Neurological function and infarct volume were assessed 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) expression levels of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB were evaluated using western blot and reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The mRNA and protein expression of inflammatory markers was assessed using RT-PCR and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). RESULTS: Compared with the MCAO/R group, the EA group exhibited improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume, and down-regulated expression of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB. Additionally, in the EA group, the mRNA and protein expression of proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) were decreased, while the expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine (IL-10) was increased. CONCLUSIONS: Electroacupuncture exerts a neuroprotective effect on MCAO/R, potentially through the modulation of the TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB pathways. This treatment may reduce the cerebral I/R-induced inflammatory response by influencing the TLR/TRAF/NF-κB signaling pathway.

title: Endovascular treatment of tandem lesions: prognostic factors of functional outcome and the efficacy of emergent carotid stenting.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prognostic risk factors for endovascular therapy (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke with tandem lesions, and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of emergent carotid artery stenting. METHODS: Patients with acute internal carotid artery tandem occlusion who underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) were enrolled. Baseline clinical and procedural data were collected. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, and the safety endpoint was symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH). Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to balance covariates between patients receiving emergent carotid artery stenting (eCAS) and non-stenting controls. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors. Subgroup analyses were conducted on relevant risk factors. RESULTS: A total of 112 eligible patients were included, with a mean age of 66.19 ± 9.23 years; 76 (67.86%) were male. Fifty-eight patients (51.79%) achieved a favorable functional outcome (good prognosis group). Univariate analysis revealed significant differences (P < 0.05) between the two groups in baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, puncture-to-reperfusion time, history of hypertension, and history of atrial fibrillation. After multivariable adjustment, hypertension, baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, and puncture-to-reperfusion time were identified as independent risk factors for unfavorable 90-day functional outcomes in tandem lesion patients undergoing EVT. Emergent carotid artery stenting (eCAS) was not an independent predictor of 90-day favorable functional outcome (adjusted OR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.17-1.58, P = 0.246). Significant differences in stroke history and smoking history were found between the emergent stenting and non-stenting groups at baseline. Female sex and puncture-to-reperfusion time were independent risk factors for sICH in tandem lesion patients. Subgroup analysis indicated that in those aged ≥ 65 years, emergent stenting was associated with unfavorable 90-day functional prognosis (OR = 0.042, 95% CI 0.004-0.469, P = 0.01). CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, hypertension, baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, and puncture-to-reperfusion time may serve as independent predictors of 90-day favorable functional outcomes in tandem lesion patients treated with EVT. Female sex and longer puncture-to-reperfusion time appear to be potential risk factors for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Emergent carotid artery stenting was not found to be an independent predictor of 90-day functional prognosis in our cohort, and no significant increase in sICH risk was observed in association with eCAS. These preliminary findings require further validation in large-scale multicenter prospective studies.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prognostic risk factors for endovascular therapy (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke with tandem lesions, and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of emergent carotid artery stenting. title: Prehospital delay and thrombolysis rates in posterior circulation stroke: a multicenter Latin American study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the delay to emergency arrival in adults with acute Posterior circulation ischemic strokes (PCS) and the likelihood of receiving intravenous thrombolysis compared to anterior circulation ischemic strokes (ACS) across six different hospitals in Latin America. METHODS: p This multicenter study in Latin America hospitals including three hospitals in Peru (Cusco, Arequipa, and Lima City), one in Colombia (Bogotá), one in Chile (Valdivia), and one in Mexico City. We analyzed adult patients treated between 2018 and 2023 with a confirmed diagnosis of ischemic stroke (IS). We evaluated demographic characteristics, initial NIHSS score, onset-to-door time (ODT), rate of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), and other stroke-related characteristics. Medians with interquartile ranges (IQR) were calculated. IVT (yes/no) was evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression including stroke circulation, age, sex, admission NIHSS, ODT, previous stroke, and previous evaluation at another hospital as covariates. Continuous predictors were modeled per year, NIHSS point, and ODT hour, respectively. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% CI were reported, with< 0.05 considered statistically significant. RESULTS: p A total of 1,460 patients were included, 501 (34.3%) of whom had PCS, with a median age of 70 years (IQR 59-80). We found significant differences in median ODT between PCS and ACS (13 h, IQR 5-46 vs. 8.5 h, IQR 4-20;< 0.001) and in IVT rates. In the adjusted analysis, each additional hour of ODT was associated with lower odds of IVT (aOR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.92), whereas stroke circulation was not independently associated with IVT (PCS vs. ACS: aOR 0.66, 95% CI 0.39-1.11). Higher admission NIHSS was associated with higher odds of IVT (aOR 1.06 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.09). CONCLUSION: Patients with posterior circulation stroke had longer prehospital delays and lower observed rates of intravenous thrombolysis than those with anterior circulation stroke. However, stroke circulation was not independently associated with IVT after adjustment for ODT and other clinically relevant covariates. These findings highlight early recognition and reduction of prehospital delay as potential targets for improving access to reperfusion therapy in Latin America.
