title: Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion-induced Deficits in Fine Skilled Motor Movement and Its Recovery Following Combined Treatment with Sodium Valproate and CIMT.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Preclinical studies have shown that sodium valproic acid (VPA) has neuroprotective properties following ischaemic injury. However, its compatibility as an adjuvant therapy with physical rehabilitation in ischaemic stroke recovery, with underlying neurophysiological mechanisms, has not been explored yet. PURPOSE: The present study has investigated the advantage of combination therapy over monotherapy in ameliorating ischaemic stroke-induced deficits in skilled fine motor movements with associated changes in local and interhemispheric neural connectivity. METHODS: Cerebral ischaemic stroke was induced by 60 min of middle cerebral artery occlusion in adult male Sprague-Dawley rats. VPA (300 mg/kg, subcutaneously, twice daily) was administered within 3 h after reperfusion and continued for 7 days, followed by constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) for another week (6 h/day). The ischaemic stroke phenotype was assessed based on neurological deficits, gait, forelimb use, rotarod stay time, reach success and infarct volume. Functional recovery, with associated changes in neural activities, was carried out by analysing the local field potential signals from the first reach success during the reach-to-grasp task on day 8 and day 15 post-stroke. Cortical oscillations were analysed at delta (0-4 Hz), theta (4-8 and 8-12 Hz) and beta (12-20 Hz) during the first reach success. RESULTS: Combination therapy after ischaemic stroke significantly improved motor and neurological functions compared to monotherapy and vehicle controls. The neural oscillations revealed a significant increase in theta power in the injured motor cortex after combination therapy when compared to that with monotherapy and control groups. The significant increase in the cross-correlation between hemispheres in the combination therapy group over monotherapy indicating an increased synchronised functional connectivity between the injured (left) and uninjured motor (right) cortices. Interestingly, VPA as monotherapy did not significantly reduce infarct volume compared to the vehicle controls. Furthermore, the therapeutic efficacy of monotherapies with VPA and early-onset CIMT (initiated immediately post-stroke) showed limited efficacy in promoting motor and neurological recovery. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, the study demonstrates that VPA combined with physical rehabilitative training (CIMT) enhances functional recovery by enhancing inter-hemispheric functional connectivity and represents a promising therapeutic strategy to alleviate persistent post-stroke motor deficits.

title: IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis determines phosphodiesterase 1c activation inducing vascular endothelial cell damage, contributes to cerebral vascular injury and neuroinflammation.
abstract: Cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase 1 (PDE1) plays critical roles in mediating neuroinflammation, neuron degeneration, and cognitive impairment through suppressing the fundamental cAMP and cGMP signaling, presenting a promising therapeutic target in combating neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative disease. However, the crucial mechanism correlating PDE1 activation and how it regulates neuroinflammation are less studied. Here, we found that the level of PDE1c significantly increased in the cerebral tissue of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) rats, especially of the endothelial cell population. Treating the human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) or dithiothreitol (DTT) significantly increased the expression level of PDE1c at both transcription and translation levels and induced vascular cell damage. These were alongside IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis activation. Inhibition of IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis by pharmacological interventions such as TUDCA or PAIR2 or gene silencing efficiently decreased PDE1c level and ameliorated vascular cell damage. Moreover, deficiency or inhibition of PDE1c by its inhibitor PDE1-IN-4 suppressed vascular cell damage and inflammatory markers activation but marginally affected IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis. Also, no additive effects were observed when treating PDE1-IN-4 in the Xbp-1s knockdown cells. Collectively, our study revealed that IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis might be a crucial upstream regulator of PDE1c in controlling vascular endothelial barrier homeostasis, presenting a novel therapeutic strategy in ameliorating CIRI.

title: Electroacupuncture Inhibits Neuronal Ferroptosis in MCAO/R Model Mice by Regulating the GSK-3β/NRF2 Signaling Pathway.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neuronal ferroptosis following acute ischemic stroke (AIS) contributes to ischemic brain injury and is regulated by nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), a key regulator of antioxidant defense and iron homeostasis. Whether electroacupuncture (EA) suppresses neuronal ferroptosis by regulating NRF2 stability and nuclear translocation through upstream glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK-3β) remains unclear. We investigated whether EA inhibits neuronal ferroptosis and alleviates ischemic brain injury by modulating the GSK-3β/NRF2 axis. METHODS: Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) models were established in C57BL/6 and conditional Nrf2-knockout mice. The GSK-3β inhibitor laduviglusib (CHIR-99021; CHIR), the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1), and conditional Nrf2 knockout were used to investigate the anti-ferroptotic mechanism of EA and the regulatory hierarchy between GSK-3β and NRF2. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), western blotting, and immunofluorescence were used to examine the GSK-3β/NRF2 pathway and ferroptosis-related molecules. NRF2 nuclear localization, neuronal nuclei (NeuN) /acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) double immunofluorescence, and co-immunoprecipitation were used to assess NRF2 nuclear translocation, neuronal ferroptosis, and the GSK-3β-NRF2 interaction, respectively. RESULTS: 2+ EA inhibited GSK-3β activity after MCAO/R, restored NRF2 protein expression, promoted nuclear accumulation, and upregulated NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1). EA also downregulated ACSL4 and transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1), upregulated glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11), reduced NeuN/ACSL4-colocalized neurons, decreased ferrous iron (Fe) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and increased superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, glutathione (GSH) content, and the GSH/oxidized glutathione (GSSG) ratio. CHIR and Fer-1 produced similar anti-ferroptotic effects, and co-immunoprecipitation confirmed GSK-3β-NRF2 interaction. Conditional Nrf2 knockout did not affect EA- or CHIR-mediated GSK-3β phosphorylation but markedly attenuated their effects on NQO1, SLC7A11, GPX4, and TfR1. EA also alleviated mitochondrial ultrastructural damage, reduced cerebral infarction and Fluoro-Jade B (FJB)-positive neurons, and improved neurological function and motor coordination in MCAO/R mice. CONCLUSION: These findings identify the GSK-3β/NRF2 axis as an important regulatory mechanism of regulating neuronal ferroptosis after MCAO/R and support EA as a potential therapeutic strategy for alleviating neuronal ferroptosis and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury through GSK-3β inhibition and NRF2 activation.

title: From recanalization to recovery: inflammation and futile reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion. This clinical-angiographic mismatch may reflect persistent tissue injury, including inflammatory injury, alongside pretreatment damage and other determinants of outcome. Experimental findings and clinical associations implicate persistent inflammatory activation, thrombo-inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, microvascular no-reflow, and blood-brain barrier disruption as contributors to secondary tissue injury after MT. Here, we examine potential inflammatory contributions to futile reperfusion and consider how inflammatory biomarkers might inform risk stratification after MT. Ischemia activates microglia, endothelial cells, platelets, complement pathways, and circulating immune cells. Subsequent reperfusion may amplify oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, neutrophil-endothelial interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, matrix metalloproteinase activity, and barrier failure. Together, these processes can promote microvascular obstruction, cerebral edema, hemorrhagic transformation, infarct growth, and impaired neurological recovery despite successful angiographic reperfusion. Among circulating biomarkers, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio has been studied repeatedly, alongside platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, interleukin-6, matrix metalloproteinase-9, and other molecular markers. Their specificity, incremental predictive value, and clinical utility require further validation in standardized thrombectomy cohorts. We therefore view inflammation as a plausible biological link between macrovascular reperfusion and persistent tissue-level injury after MT. From a translational perspective, the immediate priorities are to standardize sampling protocols, characterize dynamic inflammatory trajectories, develop multimodal prediction models, and test biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.

However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. title: Edaravone for Potential Mitigation of Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Kidney Disease.
abstract: Edaravone (EDA) is a synthetic free-radical scavenger FDA-approved for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) treatment in the United States and is used clinically for treatment of acute ischemic stroke in Japan and other countries. While its antioxidant activity has been the primary focus of investigation in the mitigation of oxidative-stress-related injury, EDA exhibits anti-inflammatory, anti-fibrotic, anti-apoptotic, and anti-necrotic effects in animal models. These properties make it a potentially attractive therapeutic agent for kidney disease, where oxidative stress and inflammation contribute to renal cell injury, mitochondrial dysfunction, and progression of disease. In this review, we cover the underlying mechanisms of oxidative stress and inflammation in renal injury, and pharmacological and free-radical-scavenging mechanisms of EDA. Preclinical evidence in several kidney diseases, including ischemic/reperfusion injury, nephrotoxin-induced disease, and diabetic kidney disease, has been used to assess EDA for efficacy. In addition, we explore the modulatory roles of key signaling pathways, such as Nrf2 and NF-κB, in protective effects of EDA against oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, necrosis, and fibrosis. Finally, we highlight the potential of EDA as a therapy in future clinical applications for various kidney diseases such as acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). It should also be emphasized that as EDA's renal efficacy evidence described in this review is largely limited to animal studies, robust human clinical data are lacking. Therefore, additional clinical studies are still needed to fully elucidate the efficacy, safety, and benefits of EDA for prevention and treatment of human kidney disease.

title: Causal discovery and treatment effect heterogeneity of futile recanalisation (CADISTH) for large vessel occlusion stroke: protocol and rationale for a multicentre prospective cohort study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Endovascular therapy (EVT) achieves high rates of successful recanalisation (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction ≥2 b) in large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke; however, functional recovery remains limited. Futile recanalisation (FR)—defined as poor functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 3–6) despite successful reperfusion—occurs in over half of patients. The underlying causal mechanisms and inter-individual heterogeneity of FR remain poorly understood, hindering effective prevention and personalised management. This study aims to apply causal discovery algorithms to identify determinants of FR and to quantify heterogeneous treatment effects using causal forest models. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Causal discovery and treatment effect heterogeneity (CADISTH) is a multicentre prospective cohort study. Consecutive acute ischaemic stroke patients with LVO who achieve successful reperfusion after EVT initiated within 24 hours of onset will be enrolled. The primary outcome is FR (mRS 3–6 at 90 days). Secondary outcomes include: (a) efficacy—neurological status (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS)) and quality of life (EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level Version (EQ-5D-5L)) assessed at 24 hours, 7 days and 90, 180 and 365 days and (b) safety—symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage within 48 hours and all-cause mortality at 90, 180 and 365 days. The CADISTH study will: (1) explore candidate causal structures underlying FR by integrating real-world data with automated causal discovery algorithms and (2) characterise heterogeneity in treatment effects of modifiable factors across patient subgroups to inform prevention strategies and individualised patient selection. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study protocol has been approved by the Biomedical Research Ethics Committee of the Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University (No. [2025] 41) with local approval at each site. All participants will provide written informed consent prior to enrolment. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and conferences. title: Stroke thrombectomy of a mural thrombus in a severe dolichoectatic basilar artery with double parallel large stent retrievers and Sofia 88.
abstract: Dolichoectasia of the basilar artery poses significant challenges for endovascular therapy due to extreme vessel caliber and tortuosity, limiting the efficacy of conventional thrombectomy devices. We present the case of an older adult with severe acute ischemic stroke caused by a mid-basilar posterior wall mural thrombus within a markedly dolichoectatic basilar artery (diameter >10 mm, length >40 mm, suprasellar extension >15 mm).1-3 Following intravenous tenecteplase, mechanical thrombectomy was attempted using a single 6.5 mm stent retriever with aspiration via a Sofia 88 catheter, but failed to achieve sufficient recanalization. As a salvage strategy, two large stent retrievers (6.5 mm and 6 mm) were deployed in parallel, and mechanical thrombectomy was performed with concomitant aspiration (video 1).4 This approach achieved complete basilar artery recanalization and reperfusion (Thrombolysis In Cerebral Infarction (TICI) 3). The patient demonstrated rapid clinical recovery. This case highlights a practical salvage technique for thrombus removal in severe basilar dolichoectasia, emphasizing the need for tailored thrombectomy strategies in nonstandard vascular anatomies. neurintsurg;18/11/2202/V1F1V1Video 1 .

title: NE52-QQ57 attenuates post-ischemia protein phosphorylation in the mouse brain.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: in vivo Cerebral ischemia induces a reduction in brain pH. GPR4, a proton-sensing G protein-coupled receptor is highly expressed in vascular endothelial cells. Pharmacological inhibition of GPR4 with NE52-QQ57 (NEQQ) reduces ischemia-induced blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and brain injury. To facilitate targeting GPR4 in vivo, it is important to better define the effect of NEQQ on post-ischemia signaling and the pharmacokinetics of NEQQ. METHODS: We performed biochemical analysis following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). We used Liquid Chromatography-Mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to quantify the concentration of NEQQ in serum, brain, and peripheral tissues. RESULTS: NEQQ administration decreased the phosphorylation of PKA substrates, PKC substrates, ERK1/2, and CREB. LC-MS/MS analysis detected NEQQ in both ipsilateral and contralateral hemisphere of the brain at 5 h and 24 h after reperfusion, demonstrating that NEQQ crosses the BBB. In peripheral tissues, NEQQ exhibited highest level in kidney and lowest in the heart. In sham controls, average serum concentrations were ∼4 and 0.9 µg/g at 5 and 24 h, respectively. Following tMCAO, ipsilateral brain exhibited higher levels as compared to the contralateral side at 5 h while the difference diminished at 24 h. CONCLUSIONS: NEQQ attenuated the ischemia-induced activation of multiple signaling pathways. NEQQ exhibited broad distribution in peripheral organs, and its brain level was sufficient for GPR4 inhibition at 24 h after injection. These findings support the use of NEQQ as a pharmacological inhibitor of GPR4-mediated signaling following ischemic stroke.

title: Sustained hydrogen delivery enhances microbiome-associated cadmium and copper immobilization in co-contaminated soils.
abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H₂) is an important energy source for soil microbes and has been implicated in biogeochemical regulation; however, whether-and how-exogenous H₂ inputs promote Cd and Cu immobilization in co-contaminated soils remains unclear. We engineered MgH₂-biochar granules capable of sustained H₂ release for up to 448 h. The granules exhibited high adsorption capacities in aqueous Cd-Cu systems (Cu: 59.76 mg g⁻¹; Cd: 35.76 mg g⁻¹). In soil, MgH₂-biochar treatment was associated with enhanced microbial hydrogenase activity, reduced oxidative stress, and enrichment of functional taxa, together with significant reductions in available Cd (10.9-22.5%) and Cu (14.2-30.1%) (P < 0.05). Notably, Mg-associated alkalization elevated soil pH and contributed to physicochemical immobilization. Microbial community analyses further revealed H₂-associated shifts in community structure and significant associations between H₂ metabolism and metal resistance (Cd: P < 0.001; Cu: P < 0.03). Genome-resolved metagenomics identified 10 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) that co-harbour [NiFe]-hydrogenases (Groups 1 and 4) and Cd/Cu resistance genes (e.g., actS, czcA, and copC). Exploratory pathway modeling further indicated associations of Cd/Cu immobilization with H₂-associated microbial processes and Mg-associated physicochemical effects. This work provides integrated material, geochemical, and microbial evidence supporting an H₂-associated contribution to heavy-metal immobilization in soils.

title: Persistent Hypoperfusion on Post-Recanalization Digital Subtraction Angiography Perfusion Maps in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite high recanalization rates with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion stroke, a large proportion of patients remain disabled. This study aims to investigate the clinical impact of persistent hypoperfusion that was detected immediately after recanalization. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with large vessel occlusion with near-complete or complete recanalization, perfusion maps were generated from post-recanalization digital subtraction angiography. Focal hypoperfusion within the ischemic territory was detected and categorized as regional or cortical according to spatial distribution. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2). The associations of no-reflow and outcomes were examined by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: P P P P P P P Among 375 patients (median age 69 [interquartile range 57-77] years; 67.5% men), persistent hypoperfusion was detected in 29.6% of patients. Patients with hypoperfusion had higher baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (median 14 versus 12,=0.076) and more thrombectomy passes (=0.021). The presence of persistent hypoperfusion was strongly associated with reduced functional independence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.23, 95% CI 0.13-0.39,<0.001), higher rates of hemorrhagic transformation (aOR=1.88, 95% CI 1.14-3.11;=0.013) and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aOR=2.95, 95% CI 1.20-7.23;=0.018). Quantitative analysis revealed minimum regional cerebral blood flow as a key factor of functional outcome (aOR=1.67, 95% CI 1.07-2.60;=0.023). There is no significant agreement with 24-hour computed tomography perfusion-defined hypoperfusion (κ=0.106,=0.524). CONCLUSIONS: Persistent hypoperfusion could be detected immediately post-recanalization in one-third of successfully treated large vessel occlusion strokes. The adverse impact to functional outcome highlights its potential as an intraprocedural biomarker for future adjunctive therapies.

title: The role of excitotoxicity in post-cardiac arrest brain injury.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Post-cardiac arrest brain injury (PCABI) remains the leading cause of neurological disability and death following cardiac arrest. While considerable improvements have been made in achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) following cardiac arrest, effective neuroprotective therapies have lagged behind. This review examines the potential utility of targeting early glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity and explores why previous neuroprotective strategies have failed to improve clinical outcomes. RECENT FINDINGS: Preclinical models have recognized glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity as a key mechanism contributing to early ischemia-reperfusion injury following cardiac arrest. Early interruption of this excitotoxic cascade may preserve vulnerable neurons and mitigate downstream secondary brain injury. Emerging therapies targeting glutamate have demonstrated mixed but encouraging early clinical results. We propose that these therapies should be integrated into a broader multimodal neuroprotective strategy that adapts to the evolving pathophysiology of PCABI. SUMMARY: The failure of neuroprotective therapies after cardiac arrest may reflect delayed therapeutic delivery rather than the absence of viable biological targets. Future progress will require improved characterization of human cerebral ischemia, earlier implementation of neuroprotective interventions, and therapies that are tailored to the evolving biology of PCABI.

title: Advanced Imaging-Guided Intravenous Thrombolysis Beyond 4.5 Hours: A Single-Center Experience in Mexico.
abstract: Introduction Intravenous thrombolysis is the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke within the first 4.5 hours; however, many patients present with unknown symptom onset or delayed presentation. Advanced neuroimaging allows identification of salvageable brain tissue and extension of the therapeutic window up to nine hours, and recent evidence suggests that, in carefully selected patients, reperfusion may be beneficial up to 24 hours after stroke onset. Objective The objective of this study is to report the institutional experience with advanced imaging-guided intravenous thrombolysis in the extended therapeutic window, including its frequency of use and workflow times. Methods We conducted a retrospective, descriptive study including consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke who received intravenous thrombolysis between March 2022 and May 2025. Patients treated beyond 4.5 hours after symptom onset or with unknown onset time were identified and analyzed. Eligibility for thrombolysis was determined using computed tomography (CT) perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) mismatch criteria. Descriptive analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 27 (Released 2019; IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results Fourteen patients (17.7%) out of a total of 79 were identified. Female sex predominated (79%), with a mean age of 67 ± 17 years and a median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 9 points. The most frequently affected territory was the anterior circulation (79%), primarily the middle cerebral artery. Onset was unknown in 36% of cases. Median time from symptom onset was 327 minutes; door-to-imaging time was 30 minutes, and door-to-needle time was 74 minutes. No in-hospital mortality was recorded. Conclusions Advanced imaging-guided thrombolysis is feasible in tertiary care centers in Mexico, thereby expanding access to reperfusion therapy for patients with delayed presentation.

title: Periprocedural body temperature and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion in large vessel occlusion stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Functional recovery remains heterogeneous among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke, even after successful reperfusion. Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 219 patients with large-vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke (LVO-AIS) who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion, defined as a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score of 2b-3. Pre and post-EVT body temperatures were recorded. The primary outcome was favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2 at 90 days. Logistic regression analyses and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between body temperature and clinical outcomes. RESULTS: P P P P P P Among the 219 included patients, 104 (47.5%) achieved favorable functional outcome at 90 days. Pre-EVT temperature was not significantly associated with functional outcome. In unadjusted analysis, each 1 °C increase in post-EVT temperature was associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome (OR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.20-0.79;= 0.01) and higher odds of mortality (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.11-3.66;= 0.02). However, these associations were attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.19-1.15;= 0.10; adjusted OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.49-3.02;= 0.67). In exploratory subgroup analyses, a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and lower odds of favorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15 (adjusted OR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.08-0.98;= 0.047), although the interaction was not statistically significant (for interaction = 0.64). CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, body temperature was not independently associated with functional outcome in the overall cohort. Although a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and unfavorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15, the interaction was not significant. This finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation with pre-specified subgroup analyses.

Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain.

title: Optimal Catheter Size for Medium Vessel Occlusion in Aspiration Thrombectomy.
abstract: The efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion remains controversial, and optimal recanalization strategies are lacking. We investigated factors associated with successful recanalization using aspiration thrombectomy in patients with medium vessel occlusion. We conducted a retrospective study on patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent aspiration thrombectomy for M2 occlusion between July 2021 and November 2025. We examined the factors associated with successful recanalization by focusing on the ratio of the catheter outer diameter to the target vessel inner diameter (Catheter-to-vessel ratio). Overall, 64 patients were included. First-pass successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction ≥ 2c) was achieved in 24 patients. In patients with successful recanalization, the ratio of the catheter outer diameter to the target vessel inner diameter (Catheter-to-vessel ratio) was significantly higher than in those without successful recanalization (p = 0.029). In multivariate analysis, the Catheter-to-vessel ratio was independently associated with successful recanalization after adjustment for catheter position and thrombus size (odds ratio per 0.1 increase, 3.688; 95% confidence interval, 1.478-9.202; p = 0.0007). In the receiver operating characteristic analysis, the threshold for the Catheter-to-vessel ratio distinguishing successful recanalization was 0.70, with a sensitivity of 79% and a specificity of 63%.In aspiration thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion, a Catheter-to-vessel ratio ≥ 0.70 may be an exploratory indicator associated with first-pass successful reperfusion.
englishSummary: The efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion remains controversial, and optimal recanalization strategies are lacking. We investigated factors associated with successful recanalization using aspiration thrombectomy in patients with medium vessel occlusion. We conducted a retrospective study on patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent aspiration thrombectomy for M2 occlusion between July 2021 and November 2025.

title: Nanoparticles in the Diagnosis and Management of Stroke: A Review.
abstract: Stroke is the third leading cause of death and the fourth leading cause of disability-adjusted life years worldwide, yet disease-modifying treatment remains largely confined to reperfusion of large-vessel ischemic occlusion within a narrow window. No neuroprotective or hemostatic agent has entered routine practice. Engineered nanoparticles have been proposed to improve delivery across the blood-brain barrier, concentrate drug within the ischemic or perihematomal microenvironment, and add imaging or sensing functions. The resulting literature is large but fragmented across platforms, models, and outcome measures, so it is not evident which platforms carry the strongest evidence or which are closest to clinical evaluation. This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence on nanoparticle-based diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and monitoring in ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 2025 using predefined Boolean strings and assigned each included study an evidence tier to separate extrapolated and cross-field evidence from stroke-specific data. Comparative tables summarize nanoparticle type, payload, model, route, dose, treatment window, particle size and surface charge, principal outcomes, safety assessment, and translational readiness. Therapeutic evidence is almost entirely preclinical: Efficacy has been shown in young, male, comorbidity-free rodents treated within minutes of reperfusion and followed for 24 h to 28 days, with group sizes typically between three and 15, and few studies reporting any bleeding or coagulation endpoint. Diagnostic applications are closer to patients because iron-oxide nanoparticles have already been given to humans, although not for imaging. We identified seven registered clinical studies of nanoparticle-related interventions in stroke; one perfluorocarbon nanodroplet emulsion completed a randomized dose-escalation trial in acute ischemic stroke, the EU Clinical Trials Register returned none, and none exists in hemorrhagic stroke. Nanoparticle platforms, therefore, remain investigational, and progress will depend less on new chemistry than on comorbid and large-animal models, realistic treatment windows, systematic reporting of bleeding risk and of interference with follow-up imaging, and reproducible manufacturing.

title: Intracranial rescue stenting in the German stroke registry: a propensity score-matched multicenter study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intracranial stenting (ICS) is used as a rescue strategy in patients with failed reperfusion after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). However, real-world data on clinical outcomes and safety remain limited. METHODS: This retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment (GSR-ET) included patients with acute ischemic stroke due to middle cerebral artery (MCA) occlusion treated between June 2015 and December 2023. Patients undergoing ICS were compared with a 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort with failed reperfusion after EVT (final modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] score <2b) who received no further endovascular treatment. Functional, safety, and subgroup outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: Among the 14,714 eligible patients, ICS was performed in 352 (2.4%). After matching, 218 patients undergoing ICS were compared with 218 controls with failed reperfusion. ICS was associated with a shift toward better 90-day functional outcomes in unadjusted (cOR 0.52, 95% CI 0.37-0.73; p<0.01) and adjusted analyses (acOR 0.41, 95% CI 0.29-0.59; p<0.01). Malignant MCA infarction occurred less frequently in the ICS group (1% vs. 8%; p<0.01), as did 90-day mortality (26% vs. 37%; p=0.02). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage did not differ between groups (4% vs. 5%; p=0.63). CONCLUSIONS: Patients treated with ICS had a shift toward better functional outcomes and lower 90-day mortality than those with failed reperfusion who received no further endovascular treatment. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage did not differ between groups. These findings support further investigation of ICS after failed EVT, although randomized studies are needed to determine its efficacy and safety.

title: CYC1 silencing exacerbates hypoxia-induced neuronal death via mitochondrial apoptosis under hyperglycemia.
abstract: Cytochrome c1 (CYC1) is a subunit of mitochondrial complex III, which is known to play a key role in ischemic brain injury. However, the functional role of CYC1 in hyperglycemic cerebral ischemia/reperfusion remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the effect of CYC1 gene knockdown in an in vitro model mimicking hyperglycemic ischemia/reperfusion. HT22 cells with normal CYC1 expression (wild-type) and CYC1-knockdown cells were exposed to 4 h of hypoxia under high-glucose and acidic conditions, followed by reoxygenation. Assessments were conducted at 0, 6, and 12 h post-reoxygenation. Cell viability (CCK-8), cell injury (LDH release), ROS production (DHE probe), mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 probe), and apoptosis (TUNEL staining) were evaluated. CYC1 knockdown reduced cell viability, increased LDH release and ROS production, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and upregulated expression of Cyt c, cleaved caspase-3, and AIF, indicative of activation of the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. These results indicate that CYC1 deficiency exacerbates hippocampal neuronal injury under hypoxic, high-glucose, and acidic conditions mimicking diabetic cerebral ischemia.

title: Preprocedural CT Radiomic Features of the Basal Ganglia Are Associated with Post-Thrombectomy Hyperdense Transformation: A LASSO-Based Logistic Regression Analysis.
abstract: Purpose: Materials and Methods: Results: Conclusions: To investigate whether radiomic characteristics of visually unremarkable basal ganglia on preprocedural non-contrast computed tomography (CT) are associated with subsequent post-thrombectomy hyperdense transformation (HT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke.This retrospective single-center study included a derivation cohort of 84 patients with preserved Alberta Stroke Programme Early CT Scores (ASPECTS ≥ 8), no visually appreciable basal ganglia abnormality, anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion, and complete reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy between January 2022 and July 2023. An independent temporal validation cohort comprised 31 consecutive eligible patients treated between August and November 2023. The ipsilateral basal ganglia were manually segmented on preprocedural non-contrast CT, and radiomic features were extracted using LIFEx. Candidate features underwent interobserver reproducibility assessment and correlation filtering before least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation. The final model was applied without modification to the temporal validation cohort. Nested cross-validation and learning-curve analysis were additionally performed to assess model-development optimism and stability.The final model retained two texture features, Gray-Level Run Length Matrix Short Runs Emphasis and Gray-Level Size Zone Matrix Grey Level Variance. In the derivation cohort, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.760 (95% CI, 0.652-0.855), with 48.8% sensitivity, 95.3% specificity, and 72.6% accuracy. When applied without modification to the independent temporal validation cohort, the AUC was 0.677 (95% CI, 0.475-0.858), with 33.3% sensitivity, 93.8% specificity, and 64.5% accuracy. Nested cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.673 ± 0.037, with variability in feature selection across resampling iterations. Learning-curve analysis showed an early plateau, with little improvement in cross-validated discrimination as the training sample increased within the evaluated range.Radiomic analysis of visually unremarkable basal ganglia on preprocedural non-contrast CT identified an exploratory two-feature imaging signature associated with subsequent post-thrombectomy HT. The model retained modest discriminatory ability in temporal validation, although internal resampling demonstrated model-development optimism and limited feature-selection stability. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant further evaluation using larger datasets, alternative modeling approaches, and independent multicenter validation.

title: An intrascrotal bioadhesive nanoplatform for sustained hydrogen delivery ameliorates age-associated testicular dysfunction.
abstract: - Testicular aging is characterized by progressive spermatogenic decline. Accumulating oxidative injury and insufficient metabolic support from Sertoli cells may contribute to this process. Although molecular hydrogen has shown antioxidant potential, its therapeutic application in reproductive aging is limited by rapid dissipation after administration. To overcome this barrier, we developed the localized hydrogen-releasing system S-H/B. This platform integrates hydrogenated silicon nanosheets (S-H) with a bioadhesive polymer, aldehyde-functionalized polylactic acid-hyperbranched polyglycerol (PLA-HPG-al). The resulting formulation adhered to peritesticular tissue following intrascrotal injection, showed prolonged local retention, and enabled sustained hydrogen release under physiological conditions. This sustained local hydrogen delivery reduced age-associated testicular degeneration and promoted spermatogenesis in aged mice. Notably, single-cell RNA sequencing revealed enhanced HIF-1 signaling and glycolysis-related transcriptional programs in aged Sertoli cells following S-H/B treatment. Further mechanistic analyses indicated that S-H/B reduced ONOOlevels and limited PHD1-dependent HIF-1α hydroxylation, thereby slowing HIF-1α degradation and promoting its nuclear localization. Consistently, S-H/B increased glycolytic enzyme expression, glucose uptake, glycolytic flux, and lactate production in Sertoli cells, whereas HIF-1α inhibition attenuated these metabolic changes. The increased lactate production may have contributed to improved seminiferous epithelial function. Overall, this work presents a bioadhesive hydrogen delivery strategy for age-associated male reproductive dysfunction and suggests that metabolic remodeling in Sertoli cells may contribute to its beneficial effects.

title: The selective IGF-1 fusion protein scp776 targets apoptotic cells and promotes recovery of ischemia/reperfusion injured tissues: Engineering and preclinical validation.
abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS) continue to be substantial burdens on global health, despite recent advances in care. Current treatment strategies focus on blockage removal and establishment of reperfusion, but there are no approved treatments to protect cells from apoptosis resulting from hypoxia or reperfusion injury. Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is a pleiotropic modulator of mitogenic and anti-apoptotic pathways across multiple cell types. Administration of IGF-1 reduces cell death and promotes recovery following ischemic injury. However, the development of IGF-1 therapeutics for apoptotic injuries has been limited by its short half-life, extensive protein binding, and non-specificity. We aimed to develop a targeted IGF-1 therapeutic, capable of preferential accumulation in injured tissues with large populations of apoptotic cells. A fusion protein consisting of an IGF-1 signaling domain, an albumin backbone, and an Annexin-V targeting domain was optimized for binding to apoptotic cells through iterative protein engineering. In vivo targeting to injured tissue, and in vitro prevention of apoptosis in cardiomyocytes, neurons, and neuroglia was demonstrated for the lead molecule scp776. Single dose scp776 treatment reduced infarct sizes in rat and pig AMI models. In a cynomolgus monkey model of AIS, a 5-day regimen of scp776 reduced lesion volume and neurological deficits within the acute post-ischemic window (first 3 days) and significantly improved survival at two weeks. These results demonstrate the potential of this novel class of targeted growth factors in different tissue types and motivate the clinical assessment of scp776-mediated rescue from acute ischemic injury.

Current treatment strategies focus on blockage removal and establishment of reperfusion, but there are no approved treatments to protect cells from apoptosis resulting from hypoxia or reperfusion injury. Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is a pleiotropic modulator of mitogenic and anti-apoptotic pathways across multiple cell types.

title: Beyond Absolute Blood Pressure Targets During Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Narrative Review of Intraprocedural Hemodynamics.
abstract: Hemodynamic management is a central component of procedural care for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) during endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Current guideline recommendations predominantly provide absolute blood pressure (BP) targets for intraprocedural management. Studies have also examined relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, and blood pressure variability (BPV), providing additional measures of systemic hemodynamic exposure during EVT. However, definitions, baseline reference pressures, measurement intervals, and BPV metrics vary widely across studies, and associations with neurological outcomes are inconsistent. Importantly, these systemic BP parameters do not directly establish cerebral perfusion. This limitation supports investigating cerebral autoregulation as a complementary, patient-specific assessment. Evidence linking individualized autoregulatory limits to outcomes remains predominantly post-EVT, with very limited evidence during the pre-recanalization phase under anesthesia. This review examines intraprocedural BP during EVT under anesthesia beyond absolute pressure targets. It considers relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, pressure-time burden, BPV, and individualized autoregulatory limits in relation to cerebral perfusion. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed for studies evaluating hemodynamics during EVT under anesthesia, supplemented by screening of selected reference lists. Studies examining intraprocedural BP targets, relative changes, hypotension duration, pressure-time burden, and BPV in relation to neurological or imaging outcomes under anesthesia were prioritized, with emphasis on the pre-recanalization period. Post-EVT hemodynamic studies were not included in the primary synthesis, except where they informed the discussion of cerebral autoregulation and future research. Intraprocedural hemodynamic variables during EVT characterize different aspects of systemic arterial-pressure exposure that may be relevant to cerebral perfusion in the ischemic penumbra. Absolute pressure, relative change, magnitude and duration of hypotension, pressure-time burden, and BPV should be regarded as complementary rather than interchangeable measures. Differences in reference pressures, definitions, measurement intervals, exposure periods relative to recanalization, and anesthesia techniques limit comparisons and standardization across studies. Future prospective studies, particularly during general anesthesia (GA), should integrate clearly defined systemic BP metrics with dynamic cerebral autoregulation. This may help determine which parameters or combinations best reflect cerebral physiological vulnerability. Individualized autoregulation-guided BP targets remain investigational and require prospective validation before they can inform routine clinical hemodynamic management.

title: Gastrointestinal tract delivery of hydrogen by dynamic gas-releasing frameworks.
abstract: 2 2 2 2 Given the broad therapeutic benefits of molecular hydrogen, gastrointestinal delivery of this gasotransmitter is attractive for treating localized inflammatory diseases, yet conventional H-releasing formulations suffer from limited solubility and poor tunability. Here, we develop gas-releasing frameworks (GRFs) for effective Hdelivery to the gastrointestinal tract. GRFs provide 20,000-fold higher hydrogen storage than hydrogen-rich water (HRW), prevent burst leakage in acidic gastric fluid, and enable sustained, inflammation-targeted Hrelease in the intestine. After Hrelease, the dynamic framework sequesters toxic boron within a reconstituted Si-O-B architecture, promoting fecal rather than systemic boron accumulation and improving long-term biosafety. Consequently, GRFs outperform HRW in mitigating oxidative damage and inflammation in dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis, radiation-induced colitis, and high-fat diet-induced non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Collectively, these gas-releasing frameworks provide a feasible, safe, and translatable strategy for gastrointestinal delivery of therapeutic gases and treatment of inflammatory disorders.

title: Postischemic endothelial immune reprogramming in stroke.
abstract: Large-vessel recanalization is essential in acute ischemic stroke, but it does not guarantee microvascular reperfusion. Endothelial responses may contribute to persistent tissue hypoperfusion through leukocyte trafficking and immunothrombosis. Many of these responses may begin during ischemia and may continue or intensify when blood flow returns. We therefore use postischemic or ischemia/reperfusion-associated terminology unless experiments isolate the contribution of reperfusion. We propose that endothelial immune reprogramming requires a coordinated molecular program, localization to a defined vascular segment and time, and a corresponding change in immune-regulatory function. An isolated increase in an adhesion molecule or circulating biomarker indicates activation or injury but cannot identify such a state. Barrier/stress, adhesive/chemotactic, and prothrombotic responses overlap. Experimental studies implicate endothelial signaling, leukocyte arrest, and platelet interactions with neutrophil extracellular traps, but have not established a common sequence of endothelial states. Human evidence comes mainly from circulating biomarkers, thrombectomy thrombi, post-mortem tissue, and perfusion imaging. The available findings have yet to link a defined cerebral endothelial state to downstream perfusion and clinical outcome in the same patients. Prospective studies should combine serial vascular biomarkers, repeated perfusion imaging, and longitudinal follow-up, with endothelial-enriched molecular profiling when tissue is available. Therapeutic studies should test whether modifying a reversible endothelial program relieves no-reflow while preserving later immune resolution and vascular repair. These approaches remain investigational.

title: Intraoperative cangrelor during mechanical thrombectomy: is the systematic addition of aspirin needed?
abstract: OBJECTIVES: In the hyperacute setting of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for large-vessel-occlusion stroke, periprocedural platelet inhibition may be required in cases of refractory occlusions or underlying cervical or intracranial arterial disease at risk of reocclusion. Cangrelor is increasingly used in this context, although its use remains largely supported by observational evidence, and the impact of concomitant aspirin remains uncertain. This study investigated the safety and efficacy of the addition of intravenous aspirin to cangrelor during MT. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the Endovascular Treatment in Ischemic Stroke (ETIS) Registry across 34 French comprehensive stroke centres. All consecutive MT patients receiving intraoperative cangrelor between July 2018 and April 2025 were included, irrespective of the indication for intravenous antiplatelet therapy. The primary endpoint was 90-day favourable outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2 or equal to pre-stroke mRS). Secondary outcomes included excellent outcome, early neurological improvement, angiographic recanalisation, day-1 arterial patency and intracranial haemorrhage (ICH). Propensity-score overlap weighting was used to adjust for confounding. RESULTS: A total of 644 patients were analysed (cangrelor + aspirin combination: 226; cangrelor alone: 418). Favourable outcomes at 90 days were similar between groups (57.1% vs 58.8%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.93; 95% confidence interval, 0.67-1.30; P = 0.69), as were excellent outcomes and early neurological improvement. Rates of successful and complete reperfusion were similar across groups. No differences were observed for symptomatic ICH (6.2% vs 9.2%; aOR = 0.66), any ICH, intra- and extracranial arterial patency on day-1 imaging, or 90-day mortality (22.3% vs 23.9%; aOR = 0.91). CONCLUSIONS: No significant differences in clinical, angiographic or safety outcomes were observed between cangrelor monotherapy and cangrelor combined with intravenous aspirin during MT. These findings provide comparative evidence on two cangrelor-based strategies currently used in clinical practice, although they should not be interpreted as demonstrating equivalence or excluding a potential benefit of adjunctive aspirin. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the role of aspirin coadministration in this setting.

Cangrelor is increasingly used in this context, although its use remains largely supported by observational evidence, and the impact of concomitant aspirin remains uncertain. This study investigated the safety and efficacy of the addition of intravenous aspirin to cangrelor during MT.

title: Sonic Hedgehog Protects Against Ischemic Brain Injury Via Modulating DRP1-Dependent Microglial Pyroptosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microglial pyroptosis plays a critical role in the neuroinflammation following ischemic stroke. Although Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) signaling has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects in cerebral ischemia, whether SHH regulates microglial pyroptosis and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. METHODS: Serum samples from patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and healthy controls were analyzed using ELISA. Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) mice and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-treated BV2 microglia were established as in vivo and in vitro ischemic models, respectively. SHH and DRP1 expression were manipulated using adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated knockdown or siRNA transfection. Pyroptosis-related molecules were evaluated by qRT-PCR, western blotting, immunofluorescence staining, and scanning electron microscopy. Infarct volume and neurological function were assessed by TTC staining, modified neurological severity score (mNSS), and corner test. RESULTS: Serum SHH levels were significantly reduced in AIS patients and negatively correlated with circulating inflammatory cytokines. Separately, GEPIA2 analysis of human brain tissue datasets revealed that SHH expression was negatively correlated with the pyroptosis-related genes IL1B, GSDMD, and CASP1. Both in vivo and in vitro ischemic interventions markedly upregulated the expression of SHH, DRP1, and pyroptosis-associated proteins in microglia. SHH knockdown elevated DRP1 expression, aggravated microglial pyroptosis, enlarged cerebral infarct volume, and worsened neurological dysfunction. Rescue experiments confirmed that DRP1 knockdown effectively reversed the pro-pyroptotic and injury-aggravating effects of SHH inhibition in microglia after ischemic stroke. CONCLUSIONS: SHH protects against cerebral ischemic injury by suppressing DRP1-mediated microglial pyroptosis. The SHH-DRP1 signaling axis represents a previously unrecognized regulatory pathway involved in ischemic stroke and may serve as a potential therapeutic target for limiting neuroinflammation and improving neurological outcomes.

Although Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) signaling has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects in cerebral ischemia, whether SHH regulates microglial pyroptosis and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. METHODS: Serum samples from patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and healthy controls were analyzed using ELISA.

title: Albumin for patients with acute large vessel occlusive stroke undergoing endovascular therapy-2 (ARISE-2): protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy is the standard of care for eligible patients with acute ischemic stroke due to LVO. However, nearly half of patients remain functionally dependent even after successful reperfusion. Albumin is a biologically plausible adjunctive cerebroprotective therapy and has shown neuroprotective effects in preclinical studies, but the clinical benefit of albumin combined with EVT remains uncertain. STUDY DESIGN: Albumin for patients with acute large vessel occlusive stroke undergoing endovascular therapy-2 (ARISE-2) is an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter, randomised, open-label, controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment (PROBE design). Eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either EVT plus intravenous 25% albumin at 0.5 g/kg (maximum dose, 37.5 g) initiated within 60 min after randomisation and then repeated once daily on days 2-4, or EVT alone. The initial target sample size is 1192 participants (596 per group). A prespecified adaptive sample size re-estimation will be performed after approximately 50% of participants have completed the 90-day follow-up, allowing the total sample size to be increased, but not reduced, to a maximum of 1788 participants. This trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of albumin administered in combination with EVT in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by anterior circulation LVO. STUDY ENDPOINTS: The primary outcome is a favourable functional outcome at 90 days, defined as a mRS score of 0-2, or return to the premorbid mRS for participants with a prestroke mRS score of 3-4. SUMMARY: The ARISE-2 trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of moderate-dose albumin combined with EVT in participants with acute ischemic stroke caused by anterior circulation LVO. The trial will provide evidence on whether albumin can improve functional outcomes as an adjunctive cerebroprotective strategy in patients undergoing reperfusion therapy. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07263308.

title: Superbore Aspiration Catheters: An Innovation in Mechanical Thrombectomy.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has become the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke caused by large vessel occlusion. Aspiration thrombectomy has evolved substantially over the past decade; however, conventional large-bore aspiration catheters (inner diameter ≥0.068″) may be limited by incomplete clot ingestion, distal embolization, and dependence on adjunctive devices such as balloon guide catheters to achieve proximal flow arrest. Superbore aspiration catheters, typically defined by an inner diameter ≥0.080 inches, are the most recent technological advancement in aspiration thrombectomy. Superbore catheters have the ability to navigate to the M1 segment of the middle cerebral artery, facilitating local flow control, complete clot ingestion, and distal flow reversal during aspiration. Since 2020, several superbore systems have been developed, including Zoom 88 (Imperative Care), HiPoint 88 (Route 92 Medical), Millipede88 (Perfuze), SOFIA 88 (Terumo), Broadway 8 (Stryker Neurovascular), and Cereglide 92 (Johnson & Johnson MedTech). Early clinical studies suggest that superbore catheters may improve first-pass effect and final reperfusion rates compared with standard aspiration thrombectomy devices, while maintaining an acceptable safety profile. This review summarizes the design characteristics, clinical evidence, and procedural considerations associated with currently available superbore systems. Although preliminary data are promising, further randomized clinical trials are needed to determine the optimal role of superbore aspiration in large vessel occlusion treatment.

title: Exosomal let-7c-5p From AMI Patient Plasma Modulates Neuronal PANoptosis via ZBP1 In Vitro.
abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) significantly elevates the risk of ischemic stroke (IS), yet the molecular mechanisms linking cardiac and cerebral injury remain unclear. Emerging evidence highlights the role of circulating exosomes in mediating inter-organ communication via microRNAs (miRNAs). In this study, plasma exosomes from AMI patients were isolated at three time points (before, 2 hours after, and 24 hours after reperfusion therapy (RT)), and the exosomal let-7c-5p level was measured. The effects of plasma exosomes on neuronal SH-SY5Y cells under normoxic and oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) conditions were evaluated by assessing cell viability and the Z-DNA binding protein 1 (ZBP1)/PANoptosis pathway using CCK-8 assay and western blot analysis. let-7c-5p was overexpressed to clarify its role in the ZBP1/PANoptosis pathway. Exosomal let-7c-5p from AMI patients showed differences at three time points. Exosomes collected before reperfusion therapy induced the most PANoptosis under normal conditions, whereas those collected 2 hours post-reperfusion therapy had the greatest effect under OGD. These effects correlated with dynamic changes in exosomal let-7c-5p levels and the expression of ZBP1. Let-7c-5p overexpression reduced ZBP1 and PANoptotic markers, suggesting a neuroprotective role under ischemic stress. Our study suggested that the exosomal let-7c-5p/ZBP1/PANoptosis axis may contribute to AMI-related brain injury, offering potential therapeutic targets for intervention.

title: Mechanisms Underlying Region-Specific Vulnerability and Resistance to Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in the Central Nervous System.
abstract: Selective neuronal vulnerability is a hallmark of ischemic injury in the central nervous system (CNS), yet the mechanisms underlying regional differences in neuronal survival and degeneration remain incompletely understood. Cerebral ischemia from ischemic stroke or cardiac arrest triggers a complex cascade of metabolic failure, excitotoxic signaling, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammatory responses that collectively determine neuronal fate. Notably, neuronal degeneration follows highly specific anatomical patterns rather than uniformly throughout the CNS. Classical experimental studies have shown that hippocampal cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) pyramidal neurons undergo delayed neuronal death after transient global ischemia, whereas neighboring CA3 neurons remain relatively resistant. Similar heterogeneity is observed in other regions, including the olfactory bulb and spinal cord, where mitral cells and dorsal horn neurons exhibit relative resistance to ischemic injury. Accumulating evidence indicates that selective vulnerability arises from the interplay of multiple molecular and cellular mechanisms, including excitotoxic glutamatergic signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, neurovascular unit dysfunction, and neuroinflammatory responses. In addition, structural and circuit-level determinants such as hippocampal connectivity and regional neurovascular organization further influence neuronal susceptibility to ischemic stress. This review integrates evidence from experimental and clinical studies to examine the mechanisms underlying neuronal vulnerability and resistance across the CNS. Particular emphasis is placed on the interplay between neuronal metabolism, glial responses, and neurovascular regulation in shaping regional injury patterns. Understanding these mechanisms may provide important insights for the development of mechanism-based neuroprotective strategies targeting selectively vulnerable neuronal populations.

title: Five-Day Glycemic Patterns and 3-Month Functional Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Admission hyperglycemia is associated with poor outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, but whether post-EVT glycemic pattern determines functional outcome remains unknown. METHODS: A Retrospective Study for the Prediction of Clinical Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients with Thrombectomy study was a hybrid prospective-retrospective multicenter cohort study nested within the Rescue on Reperfusion Damage in Cerebral Infarction by Nelonemdaz trial (NCT05041010) across 24 tertiary stroke centers in South Korea. Patients with ≥80% measurements within 80-140 mg/dL and no value ≥200 mg/dL were classified as normoglycemic (Group 1); the remainder were classified by group-based trajectory modeling into persistently elevated (Group 2) and variable hyperglycemia (Group 3). The primary outcome was 3-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) distribution. RESULTS: Among 457 patients, 319 were included (mean age 73.6±12.2 years; 53.6% male): 97 (30.4%) in Group 1, 159 (49.8%) in Group 2, and 63 (19.7%) in Group 3. Groups 2 and 3 had more diabetes and higher hemoglobin A1c; stroke severity, Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Scores, and reperfusion status were comparable. Both hyperglycemic groups had lower odds of a favorable mRS shift than Group 1 (adjusted common odds ratio [OR] 0.35, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.20-0.61 and 0.49, 0.25-0.94). Functional independence (mRS 0-2) was achieved in 63.9% of Group 1 versus 36.5% and 38.1% in Groups 2 and 3 (adjusted OR 0.26, 95% CI 0.13-0.53 and 0.31, 0.13-0.73). No significant difference was observed between Groups 2 and 3. CONCLUSIONS: Five-day post-EVT hyperglycemic status was independently associated with worse 3-month functional outcomes beyond chronic glycemic burden, supporting re-evaluation of targeted glycemic interventions during this vulnerable window.

title: Sensory stimulation enhances TFRC-targeted apoferritin nanoparticle delivery of ginsenoside Rb1 to promote endothelial protection and stroke recovery.
abstract: Effective treatment of ischemic stroke requires improved perfusion and drug delivery to the ischemic penumbra. We investigated whether sensory stimulation could enhance cerebral blood flow and improve delivery of an apoferritin (Aft)-based ginsenoside Rb1 nanodelivery system (Aft@Rb1). Sensory stimulation increased blood flow in the barrel cortex after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R). By exploiting increased transferrin receptor 1 expression in cerebrovascular endothelial cells, Aft@Rb1 achieved targeted delivery to ischemic tissue. In mice with cerebral I/R, sensory stimulation combined with Aft@Rb1 increased local Rb1 accumulation, reduced blood-brain barrier disruption and infarct area, and improved neurological recovery. These findings indicate that sensory stimulation can enhance local perfusion and nanodrug delivery, providing a potential combined therapeutic strategy for ischemic brain injury.

title: NETs and the thrombo-immune microenvironment: immune heterogeneity in recanalization, reperfusion, hemorrhagic transformation, and antithrombotic strategies.
abstract: Reperfusion therapies have revolutionized the treatment of acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but target-artery recanalization, downstream angiographic reperfusion, microvascular tissue reperfusion, and functional recovery are distinct endpoints. Patients may have persistent occlusion or early reocclusion, incomplete modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) reperfusion, microvascular no-reflow despite high-grade mTICI/eTICI reperfusion, hemorrhagic transformation (HT), or poor 90-day functional outcome. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) form a mechanistic link between thrombus structure, innate immune activation, endothelial injury, and antithrombotic responses. NETs provide a DNA-histone scaffold that stabilizes fibrin-rich thrombi, recruits platelets and coagulation factors, and exposes the neurovascular unit to cytotoxic granular proteins. The biological characteristics of NETs nevertheless vary among patients. Differences in neutrophil priming, platelet activation, monocyte-endothelial signaling, thrombus composition, collateral status, concurrent inflammation, and reperfusion injury create distinct thrombo-immune microenvironments. This article reviews how NET-driven immunothrombosis affects arterial recanalization, angiographic and tissue reperfusion, HT, and emerging antithrombotic strategies. It also proposes an operational immune-phenotyping framework with candidate biomarkers, assay-dependent research thresholds, sampling time points, and trial-level decision rules.

title: Intravenous thrombolysis use before interhospital transfer for thrombectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: AIMS: Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) before interhospital transfer for endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in patients with large-vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke (LVO-AIS) remains controversial. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of pre-transfer IVT in LVO-AIS patients who presented to primary stroke centers (PSCs) and required transfer to comprehensive stroke centers (CSCs) for EVT. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to July 2, 2026. Studies comparing IVT versus no IVT prior to interhospital transfer for EVT in patients with LVO-AIS were included. Efficacy outcomes included the primary outcome of excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1 at 90 days), as well as secondary efficacy outcomes including good functional outcome (mRS 0-2 at 90 days), interhospital recanalization, and poor functional outcome (mRS 5-6). Safety outcomes included 90-day mortality, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), any intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), and parenchymal hematoma (PH). Pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models, and adjusted estimates were synthesized using the generic inverse variance method. RESULTS: Sixteen observational studies were included. Pre-transfer IVT was associated with significantly higher rates of excellent functional outcome (OR 1.72, 95% CI 1.47-2.01, p<0.00001), good functional outcome (OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.35-1.99, p<0.00001), and interhospital recanalization (OR 7.71, 95% CI 4.08-14.55, p<0.00001), as well as significantly lower risks of poor functional outcome (OR 0.65, 95% CI 0.54-0.79, p<0.0001) and 90-day mortality (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.59-0.81, p<0.00001). No significant differences were observed between groups in the risks of sICH (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.50-1.11, p=0.15), any ICH (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.76-1.09, p=0.31), or PH (OR 1.43, 95% CI 0.88-2.33, p=0.15). In the adjusted analyses, the associations remained significant for excellent functional outcome (aOR 1.47, 95% CI 1.19-1.81, p=0.0004), good functional outcome (aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.25-2.07, p=0.0002), interhospital recanalization (aOR 8.06, 95% CI 4.71-13.82, p<0.00001), and 90-day mortality (aOR 0.64, 95% CI 0.49-0.84, p=0.001). The magnitude and direction of associations were generally consistent with the unadjusted analyses. CONCLUSION: Among LVO-AIS patients requiring interhospital transfer from PSCs to CSCs for EVT, pre-transfer IVT was associated with improved functional outcomes and interhospital recanalization, without increasing hemorrhagic risk. These findings support pre-transfer IVT as an effective reperfusion strategy in resource‑limited settings where timely EVT is not immediately accessible.

title: Sex differences following cardiac arrest: a conceptual framework for mechanisms and translational targets.
abstract: Biological sex is increasingly recognized as a fundamental variable in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, yet its integration into our understanding of post-cardiac arrest brain injury (PCABI) pathophysiology remains limited. Although mortality following cardiac arrest remains universally high, males have a higher lifetime incidence while females experience disproportionately poor survival and neurological outcomes, particularly after menopause. Rather than a binary difference, evidence indicates three possible functionally distinct risk profiles: males with relatively stable neurological vulnerability across the lifespan, premenopausal females with apparent neuroprotection, and postmenopausal females at increased risk of neurological sequelae. Neurological injury is the primary determinant of survival and long-term function after cardiac arrest, yet mechanisms underlying sex differences in PCABI remain poorly defined. To address this, this review integrates clinical observations with experimental and translational evidence to develop a conceptual framework for hypothesis generation in sex-specific PCABI. We examine differences in arrest etiology, resuscitation, and post-resuscitation care, drawing on pathophysiological insights from myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke to contextualize PCABI-relevant pathways. Across the phases of ischemic depolarization, reperfusion repolarization, dysregulation, and recovery/repair, we synthesize biologically plausible mechanisms through which hormones, autonomic regulation, vascular reactivity, immune responses, and excitotoxic signaling may shape diverging patterns of injury and recovery. We identify key calls to action for research priorities and propose strategies to incorporate sex- and age-informed frameworks into PCABI research. Specifically, our calls to action will address the inclusion of sex and age-disaggregated analyses into research designs, develop generalizable and standardized assessments for hormonal status to assist with phenotyping and consider confounding by disparities in healthcare access or delivery between sexes. Treating sex as a primary biological variable, rather than a covariate or supplementary analysis, will be essential for advancing precision critical care and improving outcomes following cardiac arrest.

title: Outcomes Following First-Pass Direct Aspiration Versus Stent Retriever for Endovascular Thrombectomy in Primary Medium or Distal Vessel Occlusion: An Analysis of the SVIN Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy is increasingly performed for acute ischemic stroke due to medium vessel occlusion (MeVO); however, recent randomized trials-primarily using stent retriever (SR) techniques-have not demonstrated a clear benefit over medical management. This study aimed to compare the direct aspiration first-pass technique (ADAPT) and SR in MeVO using a multicenter endovascular thrombectomy consortium. METHODS: The Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology registry was queried for all primary MeVO cases treated with ADAPT or SR as the first-pass technique. MeVO was defined as an occlusion of A1, P1, M2, or beyond. Outcomes included time to recanalization, recanalization rates, first-pass effect (defined as Treatment in Cerebral Infarction-3 after first pass), intracranial hemorrhage, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, and clinical outcomes. RESULTS: P P P P P P A total of 1391 patients with MeVO were identified; 415 (29.8%) in the ADAPT group and 976 (70.2%) in the SR group. The most common location of occlusion was the middle cerebral artery-M2 (75.9%), followed by the middle cerebral artery-M3 (11.4%). The median age was 70, and 698 (50.4%) patients were men. Time from angio-suite arrival to expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) ≥2b (54 versus 60,=0.002), time from endovascular access to final recanalization (42 versus 52,<0.001), time from endovascular access to eTICI 2b (31 versus 39,<0.001), and eTICI 3 (26 versus 34,<0.001) were shorter for the ADAPT group. Conversely, the SR group had higher rates of eTICI ≥2b (91.6% versus 86.3%,=0.002) and first-pass effect (31.7% versus 23.4%,=0.002). Rates of good outcome, excellent outcome, intracranial hemorrhage, and sICH were not significantly different between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Although ADAPT yielded faster recanalization, SR achieved a higher first-pass effect and slightly higher recanalization rates. Intracranial hemorrhage, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, and clinical outcomes were comparable between groups. This study suggests that both techniques may offer distinct advantages. Prospective randomized controlled studies are warranted to further understand the safety and efficacy of ADAPT versus the SR technique in patients with MeVO.

title: Associated Factors of Hemorrhagic Transformation in Patients Undergoing Anterior Circulation Thrombectomy: Data from a Comprehensive Stroke Center in Vietnam.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a common complication after mechanical thrombectomy. This study aimed to determine the incidence of and factors associated with HT, evaluate factors associated with sICH, and assess prognostic factors associated with 90-day functional outcome after anterior-circulation thrombectomy.We retrospectively analyzed 244 consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent anterior circulation thrombectomy between June 2022 and May 2023. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment variables were compared according to HT, sICH, and 90-day functional outcome. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed.HT and sICH occurred in 38.5% and 10.0% of patients, respectively. Cardioembolic etiology was independently associated with HT (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.31-4.36) and sICH (aOR 2.79, 95% CI 1.12-6.93). Successful reperfusion (TICI 2b-3) was independently associated with HT (aOR 2.51, 95% CI 1.09-5.77). Among patients with HT, younger age (aOR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.95) and a lower 24-h National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score (aOR 0.62, 95% CI 0.43-0.88) were independently associated with good functional outcome at 90 days.Cardioembolic etiology and successful recanalization were independently associated with HT, whereas cardioembolic etiology was independently associated with sICH. Among patients with HT, younger age and a lower 24-h neurological deficit were prognostic markers of better functional outcomes.

title: Mechanisms and precision intervention strategies of time-dependent dynamic regulation of matrix metalloproteinase-mediated cerebrovascular barrier disruption and neurovascular unit remodeling in stroke.
abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of global mortality and long-term disability. Despite the clinical success of reperfusion therapies, their efficacy is hampered by narrow therapeutic windows and the risk of secondary brain injury. Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), a family of zinc-dependent endopeptidases, have emerged as pivotal biphasic regulators in the onset, progression, and resolution of ischemic stroke. This review synthesizes current evidence regarding the multifaceted roles of MMPs in stroke pathophysiology. Prior to ictus, MMPs increase vascular vulnerability by driving pathological remodeling in atherosclerosis and hypertension. During the acute phase, the rapid activation of MMP-2, -3, and - 9 degrades tight junction proteins (e.g., occludin, claudin-5, ZO-1) and extracellular matrix (ECM) components, precipitating blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, neuroinflammation, and hemorrhagic transformation. Conversely, during the subacute and recovery phases, MMP-2 and MMP-13 facilitate neurovascular unit (NVU) repair by promoting angiogenesis, synaptic plasticity, and ECM remodeling. Furthermore, we highlight the role of aberrant MMP signaling in mediating the brain-peripheral organ axis, which triggers sympathetic imbalance and systemic immune dysfunction. Despite promising preclinical results with small-molecule inhibitors and tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), clinical translation has been stifled by the nonspecific toxicity of broad-spectrum inhibitors and the inadvertent suppression of beneficial MMP functions during the repair phase. We conclude that the therapeutic paradigm must shift from broad-spectrum inhibition to precision regulation. Tailoring interventions to specific molecular subtypes, cell types, and temporal windows is essential. This review provides a theoretical framework for developing stage-specific MMP-targeted therapies to improve clinical outcomes in stroke patients.
